home_pitcher_note: Manager Manny Acta said Perez received the nod as the Opening Night starter because he has more experience than anyone in the starting rotation. The southpaw, who's entering his 10th Major League season, was 8-11 in 26 starts for the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson will be making his fifth Opening Day assignment and looking to continue his career-long dominance against the Nationals franchise.  In eight starts against the club dating back to Montreal, he's gone 5-1 with a 1.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: This home opener will mark the start of what Glavine hopes to be a good homecoming. The veteran southpaw, who notched his 300th career win last year, pitched in Atlanta from 1987-2002.
away_pitcher_note: Snell will be making his first career Opening Day start. Fresh off signing a multiyear deal that could potentially keep him in Pittsburgh for the next five years, he will look to repeat last year's success.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens earned a spot in the rotation with the poise and maturity he showed during Spring Training. Acquired from the Tigers in October, the 22-year-old right-hander has good control of his 93 mph fastball and has the ability to consistently throw a sharp slider for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: After leading the Pirates with 14 wins last season, Gorzelanny looks to begin just his second full season in Pittsburgh. The lefty pitched past the 200-inning mark last year and made a staff-high 32 starts. A year ago, Gorzelanny followed a shaky spring by jumping out to start the season 3-0 with a 2.05 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Hampton's first start since Aug. 19, 2005. The injury-plagued southpaw has missed the past two seasons while recovering from separate elbow surgeries.  Throughout Spring Training, he impressed with his patented sinker and a curveball that he hasn't shown since the early days of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Duke makes the start in place of Paul Maholm, who was scratched with a stiff back. In his only start against the Braves last year, Duke took the loss after allowing four earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. Overall, the Pittsburgh left-hander is 1-2 with a 3.43 ERA in his three career appearances against the Atlanta team. Duke has, however, been hit hard by Atlanta right-fielder Jeff Francoeur, who is 5-for-8 with three extra-base hits against the southpaw.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson surrendered two first-inning runs in Sunday's Opening Day start against the Nationals and then ended his outing by retiring 19 consecutive batters. He was 2-2 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts against the Mets last year.
away_pitcher_note: For much of last season, the Mets needed Maine to be their ace -- and he filled that role as best he could. This year, the Mets simply need him to be a rock -- and he's shown no reason why he can't fill that role even better.

home_pitcher_note: Smoltz will be making his season debut with a right shoulder that he says has proven to be healthy over the past week. The tightness he'd had between his neck and right shoulder wasn't present when he completed five innings in a Minor League game on Sunday. The veteran hurler's only Spring Training start against a big league team occurred on March 15 against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Santana was in control throughout his Mets debut against the Marlins on Monday. If not for a two-run home run by Josh Willingham, he would have escaped unscathed. As it was, he allowed three hits and two walks and struck out eight in seven innings. But the Marlins' batting order and that of the Braves bear little resemblance. He threw 100 pitched and fatigue didn't appear to be an issue.

home_pitcher_note: Cook, looking for secondary pitches to enhance his sinker, mixed his changeup with his new cut fastball in his first start, an 8-3 Rockies loss to the Cardinals. He gave up six runs on four hits in six innings. His seven groundball outs were not as many as a normal start for him, but he left the outing feeling comfortable with how he used his new pitches. He'll need to sharpen the execution.
away_pitcher_note: Glavine surrendered two runs  -- one earned -- in five innings of Monday's home opener against the Pirates.  The veteran southpaw was pushed back from Sunday, when he would have faced the Mets, who employed him the past five years. He was in line for a victory into the seventh inning on Monday and was hurt by two separate two-out errors.

home_pitcher_note: What Jimenez lacked in efficiency, he made up for in persistence in his opening start of the season, a 3-0 road loss to the Cardinals. Jimenez threw 100 pitches in five innings, giving up seven hits and five walks (one intentional), with a couple of wild pitches. But he held the Cards to three runs and struck out four. He struggled against the Braves in his only previous start against them, giving up six runs on six hits and five walks, but getting seven strikeouts, in 4 2/3 innings of a 6-4 loss at Turner Field last Aug. 4.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens enjoyed a successful Atlanta debut on Wednesday night, when he limited the Pirates to two earned runs in 5 1/3 innings and got the win. The 22-year-old right-hander, who was acquired from the Tigers in October, surrendered three hits and both of those runs in the sixth inning. This will be his first career appearance against the Rockies and at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: After not walking anyone in official Spring Training games and walking just one in a Minor League game while camp was in session, Redman put himself in trouble by walking two in the first inning of Friday afternoon's home opener against the Diamondbacks. Redman never established early that he could hit the strike zone with his sinker, and the Diamondbacks hit his elevated pitches. He gave up nine hits, including a home run, and three walks. On the positive side, he struck out four.
away_pitcher_note: James didn't experience any problems during Spring Training with his left shoulder, and now he'll be looking to enjoy a successful season debut. He will make his first start in place of Mike Hampton, who is back on the disabled list with a strained pectoral muscle. James has won 11 games during both of his first two big league seasons. Primarily a two-pitch pitcher who has been susceptible to surrendering home runs, he has been working on a slider.

home_pitcher_note: Left-hander Matt Chico lasted six innings and gave up four of the five runs. Bad mechanics had nothing to do with giving up the runs. He made a couple of mental mistakes, according to pitching coach Randy St. Claire. For whatever reason, Chico had problems with the bottom of the Cardinals' batting order. In the second inning, Adam Wainwright and Cesar Izturis, batting eighth and ninth, respectively, had RBI singles, while Yadier Molina, a career .248 hitter, drove in two runs with a single in the next inning. Chico didn't have any problems with meat of the order -- Brian Barton, Rick Ankiel, Albert Pujols, Troy Glaus and Ryan Ludwick -- went a combined 2-for-14. The rest of the order -- Molina, Adam Kennedy, Wainwright and Izturis -- went 5-for-10.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson was undefeated against the Nationals last year, going 4-0 with a 0.60 ERA over 30 innings. He faced them on Opening Night in D.C., allowing two runs on three hits over seven innings while striking out three, though he got no decision in a game the Braves ultimately lost. After surrendering two first-inning runs, he retired the final 19 Nationals he faced. He got a win against the Mets on Saturday, going six innings and allowing three runs while continuing to baffle hitters with his sinker.

home_pitcher_note: One thing can be said about Lannan: He finds a way to right the ship whenever he gets off to a slow start. Last Sunday afternoon was an example of how Lannan battled back. He walked Brian Barton to lead off the game and then gave up an RBI double to Rick Ankiel, but retired the next eight hitters he faced. After looking shaky again in the third -- getting two outs, then giving up a solo home run to Ankiel and walking the next two hitters -- Lannan righted himself again and went on to pitch 6 2/3 innings, while giving up only seven hits. He struck out four and walked three but took the loss in a 3-0 defeat.
away_pitcher_note: Smoltz looked both impressive while recording six strikeouts in five scoreless innings against the Mets on Sunday afternoon.  The 40-year-old hurler opted to cut his effort short after feeling some tightness in between his neck and right shoulder.  He experienced similar discomfort in late March, but isn't concerned about missing this next start. Along with a 96 mph fastball, he showed the Mets some curveballs and backdoor sliders.

home_pitcher_note: In a 10-7 loss to the Marlins last Monday, Redding thought some of the damage in the game could have been avoided if he was able to get Alfredo Amezaga out to end the third inning. With runners on second and third, two outs and the Nationals leading 3-2, Redding was supposed to pitch around Amezaga and get to pitcher Andrew Miller instead. But Amezaga drove a 2-2 pitch to right field, doubling in two runs. Miller reached on an infield single and scoring on Hanley Ramirez's three-run homer to make it a 7-3 game. Redding lasted four innings and gave up seven runs, only one earned because of two errors.
away_pitcher_note: Although he's allowed just one earned run in his first 11 1/3 innings this season, Glavine still has only two no-decision to show for his effort.  He surrendered just three singles in 6 1/3 scoreless innings at Coors Field on Monday night. The 42-year-old southpaw has shown his usual control and is still baffling hitters with his patented changeup.

home_pitcher_note: For a team that needs starters to go deep into games, Olsen is providing some necessary innings. In his last outing, the 24-year-old left-hander worked 7 2/3 innings, following up a six-inning no-decision while facing the Pirates. The 7 2/3 stint was his most since he lasted 7 1/3 innings against the Astros on Aug. 5, 2007. A year ago, Olsen was 0-2 (7.58) in four starts vs. Atlanta. For his career, he is 1-4 (8.54) in eight meetings with Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing four earned runs and nine hits in seven innings on Monday night at Coors Field, Jurrjens never lost his composure. After surrendering Matt Holliday's fifth-inning RBI single, he retired seven of the final eight batters he faced. The 22-year-old right-hander has displayed his usual control, recording eight strikeouts and issuing just one unintentional walk in his first 12 1/3 innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off an economical outing, Hendrickson cruised through seven innings at Washington, allowing one run on three hits. He struck out two, didn't walk a batter, but hit Nick Johnson with a pitch. Still, the left-hander exited after 80 pitches, and provided a much-needed quality start, which eased the stress on the bullpen. Hendrickson has thrown at least five innings in all three of his starts. Lifetime against Atlanta, he is 0-2 with a 4.15 ERA in two games.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson was simply dominant on Friday night while prolonging his career-long success against the Nationals franchise with eight scoreless innings. Now he gets to face a Marlins organization that has also seen him enjoy plenty of success. In the 10 starts he's made against them since the start of 2005, Hudson has surrendered just one earned runs seven times. The veteran right-hander has a 1.87 ERA in five career starts at Dolphin Stadium. The only time he surrendered more than one earned run there came on April 25 last year -- during a game he carried a shutout into the ninth inning.

home_pitcher_note: It was an up-and-down first start of the season for Nolasco, who gave up six runs (five earned) in five innings at Houston. The right-hander was making his first MLB start since May 17, 2007, and his five-inning stint was his most since that day. There were some encouraging signs for Nolasco, as he logged 82 pitches. But in the fifth inning, he gave up two homers. Before joining the rotation, Nolasco threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings out of the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: While Smoltz's right shoulder might provide discomfort all season, it hasn't proven to be a hindrance while he's allowed just one earned run and combined for 11 innings in his first two starts of the season. The 40-year-old hurler is 14 strikeouts shy of becoming the 16th pitcher in Major League history to reach the 3,000 mark. He is 2-1 with a 2.08 ERA in his past four starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Bennett learned late Thursday afternoon that he'll be pitching Friday's series opener, despite the fact that he made a 28-pitch relief appearance on Wednesday night. The right-hander proved successful as a starter late last year with Triple-A Richmond and had a successful four-inning emergency start in place of Mike Hampton on April 3. He issued four consecutive two-out walks in Sunday's loss to the Nationals and surrendered a decisive two-run homer in Wednesday's setback.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe was the beneficiary of the Dodgers' first bona fide batting explosion of the season, an 11-1 romp over the Padres on Saturday, in which he went eight innings, allowing four hits while striking out six and walking none. Besides inducing mostly groundouts following a semi-shaky, 20-pitch first inning, Lowe was near-perfect over the next seven. After Josh Bard touched him for a single in the second, he retired the next 15 batters, and 20 of the last 21 he faced. In his career, Lowe is 5-0 against the Pirates with a 3.03 ERA, including 1-0 and 4.70 in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Lefty Chuck James will make his second start of the season, replacing Tom Glavine, who was scratched Friday night due to a strained right hamstring. James has a career record of 22-15, but was hit hard (three innings, six earned runs, five hits) in his only start for Atlanta this season, April 9, in Colorado. James, who is 0-1 with a 1.69 ERA with Richmond, was 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in his one appearance against the Dodgers in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley's last outing, on Sunday, was cause for optimism, albeit coming on the losing end of Greg Maddux's 349th career victory, in which the Dodgers mustered all of five hits. In giving up one run over five innings that day, Billingsley struck out eight, walked two, and gave up a hit in each of the first four innings. Along the way, he lopped more than four runs off his ERA. The 23-year-old has no decisions against the Braves, having faced them once in 2007, when he went a combined 3 1/3 scoreless innings over two games.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens struggled with his control, throwing just 56 of his 101 pitches for strikes, against the Marlins on Tuesday night. But still, the 22-year-old right-hander allowed just two earned runs and four hits. Jurrjens has provided the Braves a chance to win each of his first three starts. His three walks on Tuesday matched the total he issued in his first two starts combined.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first at Dodger Stadium, right-hander Hiroki Kuroda continued his impressive introduction to the Major Leagues after and 11-year career in Japan. Through three games and 18 2/3 innings, Kuroda, 2-1, has a 2.89 ERA.  On Monday he gave up seven hits and three earned runs over six innings against the Pittsburgh Pirates.  Next up is an afternoon game against the Braves in Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson provided some concern Wednesday night when his fastball was clocked between 83-85 mph -- at least seven mph slower than normal. He allowed four earned runs in three innings and was removed with what the Braves hoped was just a dead arm.  In his two previous starts against the Nationals this year, Hudson has worked 15 innings and allowed just two earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Chico admitted that he didn't feel right once he stepped on the mound against the Mets. He was rushing to throw his pitches, and couldn't find a happy medium when he was on the mound. Not feeling right proved to be costly for Chico, as he gave up three home runs in a 5-2 loss. The Nationals were ahead, 1-0, when he gave up a solo home run to Ryan Church in the bottom of the first inning. The biggest blows came in the fifth inning. The Nationals had a 2-1 lead when Jose Reyes tied the score with a solo shot. Three batters later, Carlos Beltran hit Chico's first pitch -- a changeup -- for a three-run home run.

home_pitcher_note: Smoltz has won each of his three starts and allowed just one earned run in 16 innings, despite the fact that he's battled tightness between his neck and right shoulder. His 10-strikeout performance in five innings against the Marlins moved him within four of becoming the 16th Major League pitcher to record 3,000 career strikeouts. The 40-year-old veteran says his slider might be better than it's ever been.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan had the game of his life in his hometown on Thursday. A native of Long Beach, N.Y., Lannan pitched six innings and struck out a career-high 11 batters, while giving up a run on three hits against the Mets. It marked the seventh time in Nationals history that a pitcher had double-digit strikeouts in a game. Prior to the game, Lannan did not have a history of striking out a lot of batters. Lannan said he was able to fool hitters on Thursday because of a slider he developed during Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: The versatile, rubber-armed right-hander may have earned himself another round in the rotation with a strong effort in a surprise start Friday night against the Dodgers. Pitching for the fourth time in six days, Bennett didn't get a decision, but was superb, shutting out the Dodgers on two hits in a season-high 4 2/3 innings. He has struggled in three career appearances against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: What was shaping up as a disastrous last outing became a no-decision for Miller. The 22-year-old gave up three runs in the first inning against the Nationals. He labored, throwing 34 total pitches in the first, with 20 pitches out of the strike zone. By working five innings, he matched his season high. Yet, they remain tough innings as he works deep into counts. He exited with 90 pitches against the Nationals. Miller has had back-to-back five-inning games.

home_pitcher_note: James found success on Saturday in his second emergency start of the young season, throwing five solid innings while allowing only one run -- on an Andruw Jones homer -- and four hits. Although allowing the leadoff man to reach in four of the five innings, he frustrated Dodgers hitters, who were 0-for-4 with runners in scoring position. James hopes to frustrate the Marlins, against whom he is 3-1 lifetime, with a 1.19 ERA. Last year he was 2-0 with a 0.66 ERA (one earned run in 13 innings) against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: Throwing strikes typically isn't a concern with Badenhop. It happened to be a problem, however, in his last outing. The 25-year-old, making his second big league start, walked five while allowing three runs to the Nationals. Because he rolled up 80 pitches, he was out of the game after three innings. He wasn't involved in the decision. In his first start, on April 13 at Houston, he lasted five-plus innings in a loss. This will be his second road start and fourth appearance overall. He threw a scoreless inning of relief at Washington on April 9.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey had a shaky start in his last outing, giving up four runs and 10 hits over five innings against the Phillies on April 20 in a no-decision. Pelfrey has benefited from great run support in all three of his starts this season. The Mets produced eight runs in the Mets' 8-2 victory over Philadelphia on April 9 and six runs in a 6-0 win over Washington on April 15. He was down 4-0 against Philadelphia on Saturday, when the Mets responded with four runs in the sixth to get him off the hook with a no-decision. Pelfrey, however, did see his ERA balloon from 1.50 to 3.18.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has continued to impress with an aggressive approach that proves he's not afraid to pitch to contact.  But with a lively fastball and a good changeup on Sunday afternoon, he recorded a career-high eight strikeouts and limited the Dodgers to one run in seven innings.  While his stuff is good, the Braves have been most impressed with the 22-year-old pitcher's composure and knowledge about pitching.

home_pitcher_note: Maine was inefficient on Monday, allowing the Cubs only two runs in six innings but needing 109 pitches to do it. Those runs were enough to give Maine his second loss, despite the fact that he shaved a sizable chunk off of his ERA for the third consecutive game. In Maine's previous start against the Braves, eight hits led to four runs in four innings. Maine defeated the Braves once last year in three tries.
away_pitcher_note: Concerns about Hudson's health were silenced on Monday night, when his fastball returned to its normal velocity -- between 91-93 mph.  On Wednesday in Florida, he lasted just three innings and couldn't throw his fastball above 85 (mph). Now that he's seemingly overcome the effects of the flu he fought two weeks ago, the veteran right-hander will look to claim his second win against the Mets.  He gained his first win of the year on April 5, when he allowed three earned runs in six innings against them.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa held his own against a potent Cubs lineup on Tuesday, giving up three runs in five innings in an 8-1 loss at Wrigley Field. The Mets are happy with him in the rotation while Pedro Martinez rehabs his balky left hamstring, as Figueroa was something of a Spring Training revelation.
away_pitcher_note: John Smoltz became the 16th pitcher in Major League history to reach 3,000 strikeouts in his last start, a hard-luck loss to Washington on Tuesday. He has struck out 10 in back-to-back games for the first time since 1997. Smoltz, 40, has allowed just 15 hits and two runs in 23 innings, striking out 31 and walking six. His seven innings against Washington marked his longest outing of the season. He beat the Mets in his first start, allowing just two hits in five scoreless innings at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start on Wednesday, Redding ended up pitching five-plus innings, giving up three runs on four hits against the Mets. Redding had problems with the bottom of the order. In the top of the fifth inning, Redding walked both Brian Schneider and pitcher Johan Santana. Two batters later, the Mets had runners on second and third when Luis Castillo reached base on an infield single that allowed Schneider to score. Redding had a feeling that Wednesday would be a long night, because he didn't feel right during his warm ups. Nats manager Manny Acta said Redding had poor command of his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Glavine will be returning to the scene of where he suffered the injury that forced him to make his first career trip to the disabled list. The strained right hamstring that Glavine suffered before he'd registered an out against the Nationals on April 13 has healed and the 42-year-old southpaw is looking to resume the success he had during his first two starts of the season. During those outings, he worked 11 1/3 innings and allowed just one earned run.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hill pitched five innings while giving up six hits and three runs for the no-decision. He said the pain in his right forearm is almost gone and he's expected to make his next start against the Braves. Hill has an 0-2 record with a 4.91 ERA in two previous starts against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has continued to show maturity beyond his 22 years and proven that he has the stuff to be a successful Major League pitcher.  The young hurler was perfect in five of his six innings against the Mets on Friday and rebounded from four consecutive third-inning walks to retire each of the final 10 batters that he faced.  He has pitched into the sixth inning of each of his first five starts.

home_pitcher_note: While lasting just three innings for the second time in three starts on Saturday afternoon, Hudson provided more reason to wonder what has been wrong with him lately. But in between allowing four runs in both of those three-inning stints, he managed to limit the Nationals to one run in 6 2/3 innings. Thus the Braves don't believe he has any physical problems. Since struggling with his velocity during his April 16 start, he has been able to throw his fastball at normal speeds.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez will be going for his fifth consecutive victory, which would match the start by Bronson Arroyo in 2006. Volquez struck out a career-high 10 batters in beating the Giants in his last outing in which he also matched a personal best by going seven innings. His curveball, fastball and changeup all were working, and he has not allowed more than one earned run in any of his five starts this season. He also delivered a run-scoring groundout for his first career RBI in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes showed why the Braves believe he has such a bright future by limiting opponents to just one run in the first 21 innings he completed for Triple-A Richmond this year. He did allow two runs and four hits in just two innings against Durham on Tuesday night. This outing was likely abbreviated because the Braves are planning to put him into their rotation void on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Belisle hasn't been very good in his two starts since coming off of the disabled list. Despite giving up four earned runs and five hits over five innings on Saturday, he benefited from great run support in a 10-9 win over the Giants. Belisle will be pitching on six days of rest because of an off-day on Thursday, which would have been his normal day to start.

home_pitcher_note: Glavine has allowed two earned runs or less in each of his four starts and still is in search of his first win of the season. The only start he's exited without being in line for the victory came on April 13, when he suffered a right hamstring strain that prompted his first career trip to the disabled list. The only runs he surrendered in six innings against the Nationals on Tuesday came courtesy of back-to-back, third-inning homers.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo notched his first victory in six starts and made his first quality outing in the Reds' 4-3 win over the Cardinals on Monday. He credited better zip on his fastball for helping him get through game. The extra strength, he claims, came from starting a new workout program in a swimming pool.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has worked into the sixth inning of each of his six starts and proven that he certainly belongs at the Major League level. The 22-year-old right-hander from Curacao has allowed just four hits in his past 13 innings.  The four walks he's issued during this stretch came in succession during a wacky third inning at Shea Stadium on April 26. He limited the Nationals to one run in seven innings on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Young turned in his second consecutive impressive outing in his last start against the Phillies, where he allowed a two-run home run to Chase Utley in the first inning but little else. Manager Bud Black was impressed with Young's improved velocity, a function of his arm continuing to build strength through pitching. Young had six strikeouts and three walks in the game and benefited from three double plays turned behind him as he lowered his ERA to 3.63.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson has had both great success and grand struggles this season. After lasting just three innings in two of his three previous starts, the right-hander went out Friday night and tossed a three-hit shutout against the Reds. He credited his changeup, which he hadn't previously thrown successfully since his days with the A's. The pitch allows him to keep hitters off his two-seam, sinking fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf pitched well in facing his former Phillies teammates for the first time on Thursday, allowing two runs on six hits in six innings with nine strikeouts. It's already the second time this season the left-hander has struck out nine hitters in a game. Wolf didn't make mistakes against his former teammates, though he wished he could have had the RBI double he allowed to Pat Burrell back in the third inning, a hit that tied the score. But Wolf mixed his pitches well to a powerful lineup and kept the ball in the ballpark.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old lefty earned a second start after a superb 2008 debut last Saturday against Cincinnati. Filling in for injured John Smoltz, Reyes showed why the Braves believe he has such a bright future, limiting the Reds to one run on four hits in 5 1/3 innings. Reyes, who was 2-2 with a 6.22 ERA with Atlanta in 2007, threw 20 scoreless innings to start the season for Triple-A Richmond this year before losing his last start for the R-Braves (two runs on four hits in two innings). He will look to exact a little revenge on the Padres, who roughed him up in his Major League debut (five runs on five hits, including two homers, in three innings), last July 7 at PETCO Park.
away_pitcher_note: Ledezma moves into the starting rotation, though it may be for only one game, as the Padres purchased the contract of veteran left-hander Shawn Estes on Thursday. Ledezma has pitched well out of the bullpen, posting a 1.96 ERA in long relief. The Padres worked extensively with him in Spring Training on his mechanics and it appears to be paying off. Ledezma makes his first start of the season against his former team, the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Allowing four runs in six innings, Snell said he never felt like he had command of the ball. While the Pirates always count on him to deliver a solid outing, he shied away from the "ace" label, saying that his other teammates were also putting up good numbers this year. Manager John Russell wants to see Snell develop more control on his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty is still looking for his first win of the season. A victim of run support in three of his four starts (the other he was injured and left in the first inning), Glavine was spotted seven runs his last time out, Sunday against Cincinnati, but lasted only 4 2/3 innings, allowing a season-high six runs (his ERA went from 2.63 to 4.50) and an uncharacteristic five walks (also a season-high). Glavine is 22-12 career against the Bucs, with a 3.12 ERA. He got no decision in Atlanta's 2008 home opener on March 31, despite allowing only one earned run and seven hits in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: After doing some throwing on the side on Monday and Tuesday, Gorzelanny is still expected to be ready to make the start on Saturday. The left-hander had his last start skipped after being bothered by tightness in his lower back. Assuming everything goes fine during his mid-week bullpen session, however, the minor tightness that remains shouldn't keep Gorzelanny out any longer. Not only does Gorzelanny have to contend with a sore back, but he also has command issues that need to be addressed. He has averaged fewer than five innings per start in his six starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: James is expected to be called up from Triple-A Richmond to make his fourth start of the season. Since he struggled in his April 9 season debut, the 26-year-old left-hander has impressed. In three appearances for Richmond, he has posted a 1.59 ERA. In addition, he beat the Dodgers on April 19 and the Marlins on April 24. He has been attempting to regain strength in his shoulder that bothered him last year.

home_pitcher_note: Duke will take the mound after making back-to-back quality starts that appear to have the left-hander on some sort of early-season roll. He has now finished at least seven innings in half of his starts this season, and his sinker has been consistently down in the zone again, something that wasn't so much the case a year ago. Duke will get his second chance of the season against Atlanta on Sunday. He pitched 5 2/3 innings against the Braves in his first start of the season and allowed two earned runs on 10 hits.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing one run and seven hits in six innings against the Padres on Tuesday, Jurrjens arguably had his least impressive outing in three weeks. In his four previous outings, he had limited opponents to a .124 batting average. The 22-year-old right-hander has been one of the game's top rookies. But now that there are more enhanced scouting reports of him, he'll have to show his ability to make quick adjustments.

home_pitcher_note: Van Benschoten will be making his first career start against the Braves. Van Benschoten hasn't pitched in any capacity since May 3. He was 0-7 last season for the Pirates in nine starts with a 10.15 ERA. This season, he is 0-1 and has allowed two runs in 3 2/3 innings pitching out of the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since throwing a three-hit shutout against the Reds, Hudson went seven strong innings, allowing two runs on six hits in the Braves' 5-2 win over the Padres on Wednesday. Hudson was charged with a run in the first inning after his pickoff move to third base was ruled a balk. He was nearly ejected from the game for arguing, but settled down and kept the Braves in a close ballgame. Hudson has allowed just three runs on nine hits in his last 16 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander's ERA has slowly declined over his last three starts. While he's allowed 25 hits in 19 innings against the Braves, he's limited the damage to three earned runs each time. He's tossed 11 innings spanning two starts, and posted a 4.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes left Thursday's game against the Padres in the third inning after a blister developed on the index finger of his pitching hand. After the game he said he doesn't expect to miss his next scheduled start, his third of the season. Reyes allowed one earned run on five hits in 2 2/3 innings against the Padres. Against the Reds on April 30, Reyes pitched 5 1/3 strong innings, allowing one run on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is stymied by what has been a frustrating return to the starting rotation. He had his worst outing on Thursday, allowing six earned runs on nine hits and three walks in five innings to Arizona. Catcher Chris Coste hopes Myers doesn't try to change to much, since he thought Myers' stuff was plenty good enough. Myers has thrown more innings against the Braves than any other opponent, posting a 4-6 record and a 4.16 ERA in 24 appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Glavine has allowed three earned runs or fewer in each of the four starts that he's lasted at least five innings. Still, for the first time in his career, the 42-year-old southpaw is still winless six starts into a season. He kept the Pirates scoreless before surrendering a seventh-inning, two-run, two-out single in Friday's no-decision. He was 2-0 with a 2.14 ERA in five starts against the Phillies last year.

home_pitcher_note: Despite good overall numbers, Hamels has been in a downward trend since posting an 0.82 ERA in his first three starts. In his next five outings, he went 2-2 with a 4.98 ERA, uncharacteristic results from the team's best pitcher. In those outings, he's allowed fewer than four runs once, though he still logs innings. His six career starts against Atlanta has produced a 3-2 record and a 4.42 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: James pitched six innings in his last start, Saturday against the Pirates, allowing five runs on five hits, striking out seven while walking four. It was James' fourth start with the Braves. He also has made three appearances (two starts) with Triple-A Richmond. James left two pitches over the middle of the plate in Saturday's game and it cost him. Pirates left fielder Jason Bay hammered a two-run home run to right-center field in the fourth inning, and catcher Ronny Paulino hit a two-run double that gave the Pirates a 5-2 lead in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: The Braves have decided to bring Jurrjens back on short rest for the first time in his career. The 22-year-old rookie right-hander threw 69 pitches while allowing three runs in five innings against the Pirates on Monday afternoon. The only damage he incurred came courtesy of a fifth-inning, two-out, three-run double. He had won each of his previous three decisions and pitched into the sixth inning in each of his previous seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland had another solid start in Saturday's loss to the Rangers, allowing three earned runs in six innings. Eveland has pitched into the sixth inning in seven of his eight starts. He gave up a two-run home run to Milton Bradley on Saturday, but that matched his home runs allowed for the season. Eveland has allowed just two home runs in 47 2/3 innings this season, and seven homers in 111 2/3 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson had arguably his best outing of the season Monday, scattering two hits over seven innings to get the win against the Pirates, which snapped the Braves' seven-game road losing streak. Hudson didn't allow a run for the second time in three starts; he pitched a three-hit shutout on May 2 against the Reds. He has allowed just two extra-base hits in the past 23 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Harden struggled in his first start since April 2, allowing five runs in 3 2/3 innings in the A's 12-6 victory over the Rangers. Harden, who had been on the disabled list with a strained right shoulder, was held to a 90-pitch count. He struggled with his control, allowing four walks and hitting a batter. Three of those runners scored. Harden's main goal is staying off the DL. His recent trip there was his sixth in the last four seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes believed he made the finest start of his young career on Tuesday night, when he allowed 11 hits and five earned runs in 6 2/3 innings against the Phillies. He wasn't alone in his assessment as Braves manager Bobby Cox and Chipper Jones indicated they'd never seen him any better. Their praise was result of the fact that he didn't issue a walk and threw first-pitch strikes to 27 of the 32 batters that he faced. Control has been the one issue that has troubled him early in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Indians in Cleveland his last time out, Duchscherer gave up a run on a two-out single in the first inning, but he retired the next 13 batters he faced on the way to 6 2/3 innings of four-hit work with two walks (one intentional) and six strikeouts while throwing a season-high 108 pitches. He took the loss, though, because the A's were blanked by Paul Byrd over 7 1/3 innings. Duchscherer, who spent two weeks on the disabled list with biceps tendinitis after leaving his first start of the season after five innings, has allowed a total of six earned runs in five starts since being activated. Both of Duchscherer's career outings against Atlanta have come in relief; he's pitched three innings, allowing three earned runs on five hits, including two homers.

home_pitcher_note: Glavine will be making his first start against the Mets since signing a one-year, $8 million deal with the Braves in November. Glavine recorded his first win of the season Wednesday against the Phillies, allowing four runs on four hits in 5 2/3 innings that gave the Braves a rare road win. It was his first win since September 8, 2007 and his first win in a Braves uniform since Sept. 19, 2002. He has pitched well this season, allowing two runs or less in five of his seven starts. The 304-game winner spent 16 seasons with the Braves before pitching the last five with the Mets, when he compiled a record of 61-56 with a 3.98 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maine won his fourth straight start, throwing 109 pitches in six innings against the Nationals Tuesday. One of the two runs charged to him was unearned. He surrendered a home Zimmerman, the fourth he has allowed what now is 48 innings. Maine allowed one other hit, hit one batter and walked one. He struck out five.He has allowed no more than two runs in seven straight starts, the longest streak of that nature by a Mets starter since Masato Yoshii had eight such starts at the end of his 1999 season.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo will make his second Major League start during the second game of Tuesday's doubleheader against the Mets. Campillo hasn't made a start since 2005 when he was with the Mariners. In that start, he lasted just one inning before taking himself out of the game with a right elbow injury. Turns out that injury would require Tommy John elbow ligament transplant surgery three weeks later. Campillo has allowed three earned runs in 21 1/3 innings of relief this season. He has been used primarily as a long relief specialist, as he has pitched two or more innings in seven of his 13 appearances this season.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas allowed two runs over 6 1/3 innings of his Mets debut, leaving a tie game but taking the loss when Aaron Heilman allowed his inherited run to score. He struck out six Nationals and walked four. Vargas, whom the Mets signed to a Minor League contract last month, faced the Braves only in a relief capacity last year, when he was a member of the Brewers. He allowed four runs over 1 2/3 innings in that outing, though he holds a 4-1 record and 3.94 career ERA at Turner Field

home_pitcher_note: Pitching on short rest for the first time in his young career, Jair Jurrjens allowed two runs -- none earned -- on eight hits in a 3-2 win on Friday over the A's. In five innings, the 22-year-old surrendered three walks and struck out three, but had no-decision. The A's eight hits were the most allowed by Jurrjens since his April 8 start against the Rockies (nine hits). Still, Jurrjens has not given up more than four runs in any of his nine outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey pitched six innings of no-hit ball against the Nationals last week, eventually allowing three hits -- and one run -- but nothing else. That was enough for him to take the loss, as his own offense could muster anything off of Jason Bergmann. Since discarding his mouthpiece and deciding to throw fewer sinkers, Pelfrey has been brilliant, losing twice but making noticeable strides in his game. He'll look to continue that trend against the Braves, a team that tagged him for five runs in 5 1/3 innings in April.

home_pitcher_note: After looking spectacular in three straight starts, Tim Hudson uncharacteristically struggled with his control on Saturday against the A's. The Braves ace gave up season highs in runs (five), home runs (two) and walks (five) in five innings. Entering Saturday's start, Hudson ranked third in the National League with fewest walks per nine innings (1.6). Hudson didn't pitch into the sixth inning for just the third time in 10 starts this season. He allowed two homers Saturday, which doubled his previous season total. The loss to the A's also snapped a personal three-game win streak.
away_pitcher_note: The home runs that have vexed Santana throughout his Mets career were again present Sunday against the Yankees, when he allowed three of them but managed to win anyway. Pitching into the eighth inning, Santana allowed four runs in all, giving up seven hits, walking two and striking out five. Following the game, he ranked fourth in the Majors with 11 home runs allowed, but also sixth in the National League with five wins. Santana lost to the Braves in his first outing against them this season, despite giving up only one run in seven innings at Turner Field.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes has been bothered by a blister on the index finger of his pitching hand. The pain intensified after the first inning Sunday, but Reyes still pitched five strong innings, allowing two runs on eight hits to pick up his second win of the season against the A's. Reyes left with two runners in scoring position and no out in the sixth, but the bullpen scattered four hits over the next four innings to preserve the win. Reyes has walked a combined two batters in his last two starts, an encouraging sign for the 23-year-old who has been erratic in the past.
away_pitcher_note: The club has not announced officially who will start this game, but signs point to Davis. The left-hander has been on the disabled list since he started April 8 against the Dodgers. Two days later, he underwent surgery to remove a cancerous thyroid. Davis has made two rehab starts for Triple-A Tucson. The last one was on Sunday, when he allowed two runs over five innings and threw 92 pitches, 54 for strikes. This spot in the rotation had been filled by rookie Max Scherzer, who has been impressive in his four games (three starts).

home_pitcher_note: Campillo baffled the Mets on Tuesday in his first start since August 2005. Campillo allowed three hits and no runs in six innings, and he didn't allow a baserunner to reach second base. It was Campillo's first Major League win and it may have cemented a permanent spot in the starting rotation. Campillo has not issued a walk in his last four outings and in 10 of his 14 appearances this season.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson has won his last three starts to give him 288 for his career. His last outing was last Sunday afternoon against the Tigers at Chase Field. The lefty tossed seven shutout innings, the longest he pitched in any of his seven starts this year. In the start prior to that, he wasn't particularly sharp as he allowed four runs over five innings to the Rockies at Chase Field. He also hit a ball off the wall in the second, but stumbled over first base and had to hold with a single.

home_pitcher_note: Glavine shook off a first-inning home run and retired 17 in a row at one point to pick up his second victory of the season Tuesday against the Mets. Glavine lasted six innings before taking himself out of the game because of slight pain in his right knee. It was the first time the pain had bothered him during a game. He allowed one run on three hits, striking out four and walking one. Glavine has pitched five or more innings in six of his eight starts this season. Luis Castillo's home run in the first was the fifth allowed by Glavine this season.
away_pitcher_note: Owings deserved a better fate in his last start, against the Marlins in Florida. The right-hander scattered seven hits and allowed three runs over seven innings in a 3-2 loss. One of the RBI hits was just out of the reach of a leaping Mark Reynolds at third and the other landed just fair down the right-field line. Owings struck out a career-best 10 in the game. In a start in Atlanta last year, Owings not only got the win, but also went 4-for-5 with a double, two homers and six RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: Jair Jurrjens improved to 5-3 this season after holding the Mets to just five hits in a career-high seven innings on Wednesday. The 22-year-old allowed one earned run and has not allowed more than three earned in a start since April 8. He hasn't allowed more than four runs in any of 10 starts this season. Jurrjens' 2.64 ERA is the lowest among Braves' starters. He'll have a tough task Monday in the Diamondbacks' Brandon Webb, who lost his first game of the season on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Webb's winning streak came to an end on Wednesday night at Dolphin Stadium as he fell, 3-1, to the Marlins. Webb was trying to become just the third pitcher since World War I to win his first 10 starts of the year. Andy Hawkins won his first 10 starts in 1985, and Eddie Cicotte won his first 12 in 1919. Dating back to last July, Webb is 19-3 with one no-decision in 23 starts.

home_pitcher_note: It has been a one step forward, two steps back kind of season for Bush, who tied for the team lead with 12 wins in each of the last two seasons but has already been demoted to the Minors once this year. He took another step back on Thursday in Pittsburgh, allowing only a cheap infield single through three scoreless innings and then six earned runs and two home runs over the next two frames. Four of the runs scored with two outs, continuing a trend, and manager Ned Yost did not exactly give Bush a ringing endorsement after the game when asked if he would consider further changes to the starting rotation. Bush allowed one run in seven innings against the Braves last season in his only career start against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson bested Johan Santana in a much-anticipated duel on Thursday, allowing two runs in eight innings in the Braves' 4-2 win over the Mets. Hudson gave up seven hits, including two home runs. He shook off the back-to-back homers and struck out four. Hudson didn't allow a baserunner to reach third over the next six innings of work. He threw 100 pitches, none more important than his last, when he induced an inning-ending double play to end the Mets' threat in the eighth.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan was in complete control for the majority of his outing against the Nationals, but a defensive error triggered a four-run inning that didn't count against his ERA, but tagged him with the loss. Manager Ned Yost was effusive in his praise, calling the 89-pitch outing one of Suppan's best this season. The righty will try to build on that momentum against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: The Braves are high on Reyes and understand that his battle to find consistent control will play a big role in their bid to win a division title. The 23-year-old southpaw regressed on Friday night, when he struggled to control his fastball and was facing a five-run deficit before recording his third out of the evening. If he finds his control, the Braves believe he has the stuff to be a future front-line starter.

home_pitcher_note: McClung turned in a terrific performance in his first Major League start in two years. He used first-pitch strikes to keep his pitch count low. Despite throwing just 68 pitches, he made it through five innings and picked up the win. McClung is a viable candidate for the fifth spot in the Brewers rotation, and his start against the Braves will be closely analyzed with that in mind.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo left after the fourth inning of Saturday's start against the D-backs, but the 29-year-old reliever-turned-starter said he expects to make his next start Thursday against the Brewers. As a starter, Campillo has not allowed an earned run. In 10 innings, he has given up just six hits. Campillo has three blisters on his index and middle fingers, and said it hurts when he grips the seams.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez pitched 1 2/3 innings in relief in a marathon game against the Padres on Sunday, giving up three runs -- all unearned -- on one hit with a walk and two strikeouts to improve his Major League-best ERA to 1.31. In his last start, Volquez pitched six innings and gave up one run on two hits with a career-high 12 strikeouts in no decision against the Padres on Friday. He also threw just 92 pitches -- the second-fewest he's thrown this season, and had nine strikeouts through four innings. He's allowed more than one earned run just once in his 10 starts and averages 7.4 strikeouts per game. Volquez's first loss of the season came against the Braves on May 2, when he gave up two runs  on four hits in a 5-3 defeat.
away_pitcher_note: Glavine issued a season-high six walks in his last start Sunday against the D-backs. He also surrendered a first-inning homer for the second straight game. Glavine tied a season high with six earned runs, four of which came on an Eric Byrnes grand slam with two outs in the fifth. Glavine was coming off arguably his best start of the season, when he gave up one run on three hits Tuesday against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Fogg was named the starter for Saturday after former starter Matt Belisle was optioned to Triple-A Louisiville on Friday. Fogg started the season as the No. 5 starter, but was sent to the bullpen after a lackluster performance in his first three starts. He went 1-2 with a 13.09 ERA in a combined 11 innings of work in those starts, the last of which came April 16 in a loss to the Cubs in which he gave up nine runs in seven innings with two walks and three strikeouts. He pitched 2 2/3 innings in relief against the Braves on May 4, giving up five runs on six hits with two walks and three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens didn't get out of the fifth inning Monday for the first time in 11 starts this season. He allowed eight hits and three runs and was pulled with two outs in the fifth and his pitch count rising. The 22-year-old also developed two blisters on the inside of his right thumb, which was covered with a bandage after the game. Jurrjens has thrown 66 innings this season, second only to Tim Hudson, and Braves manager Bobby Cox stressed after Monday's game that they need to start taking better care of their young right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto struggled with his location and reached his highest pitch count of the season in his last start on Tuesday against the Pirates. He threw 119 pitches, despite working just five innings. The 22-year-old right-hander gave up three runs -- two of them earned -- on nine hits with three walks and four strikeouts. The three walks tied his season high, which he has set twice. The 119 pitches marked just the third time this season his pitch count reached triple digits. Cueto has never faced the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson allowed a season-high 11 hits in a no-decision Tuesday against the Brewers. Hudson gave up two runs and struck out six. He pitched eight innings for the second straight start. In the eighth inning, Hudson got hit in the right foot by a grounder up the middle by J.J Hardy, but stayed in the game and got the final out of the inning. He didn't factor in the decision for the second time this season, the first since March 30 against the Nationals, when he pitched seven innings and allowed two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Jo-Jo Reyes pitched the best game of his young career on Wednesday against the Brewers. The 23-year-old left-hander struck out nine and allowed two hits in seven innings, but was dealt the loss. Reyes walked J.J. Hardy on four straight pitches to start the eighth inning, and when reliever Blaine Boyer allowed a two-out RBI triple to Richie Weeks two batters later, Reyes' stellar outing was erased. Reyes had been bothered by a blister on the index finger on his left hand, but it was healed by Wednesday's start.
away_pitcher_note: Reduced velocity continues to make Olsen have to struggle to log innings. In his last outing, a five-inning affair at Shea Stadium against the Mets, the left-hander gutted out five innings, giving up four runs on six hits. He was not involved in the decision. He struck out three, and allowed two home runs -- both on 85 mph fastballs. He's now given up four home runs in his last two starts, which total 8 1/3 innings. Olsen has not thrown more than six innings in his last four starts, or since he went 8 2/3 innings on May 6 in a win over the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo has allowed just one earned run and nine hits in the 15 innings that he’s totaled since becoming a starter on May 20.  The 29-year-old right-hander has shown precise control and the ability to succeed without overpowering stuff.  The fifth-inning homer he surrendered on Thursday was the first run he allowed in a span of 20 1/3 innings.  Campillo has battled a blister on his right middle finger that has caused him to exit the game early in both of his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: A couple of off-days meant the team could tinker with its rotation. Each time, Badenhop was the starter pushed back. As things shook out, the right-hander ended up going 11 days between appearances. When he threw 1 1/3 innings of relief on Friday at Philadelphia, it was his first appearance since a May 18 start, where he tossed three innings in a loss to the Royals. The first batter Badenhop faced was Ryan Howard, who homered. He then retired the next four he faced. This will be his eighth MLB start, and 10th appearance. On April 24, the 25-year-old gave up six runs in five innings in a loss to Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing a season-high six walks and tying a season high with six earned runs in his last start, Tom Glavine gave up two runs and five hits in six innings Friday against the Reds, but earned a no-decision. He struck out five and walked two, and the only runs he gave up came in a two-run sixth inning. Glavine has been inconsistent this season. In one start, he will look out of sorts and miss with his location on the corners. In another start, he has pinpoint precision and gives up nothing more than harmless singles.
away_pitcher_note: His last start was a forgetful one. Hendrickson allowed a career-high 10 runs (all earned), which matched a Marlins franchise record now reached four times. The Phillies jumped on the 6-foot-9 lefty, slapping out seven hits and two homers. He had won two straight decisions and seven of eight decisions before his season-short 3 2/3-inning outing. On April 16, Hendrickson beat the Braves, giving up three runs (two earned) in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens struggled with his control posted his shortest outing of the season when he lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Reds on Saturday. He gave up six runs on nine hits with a season-high six walks and two strikeouts in receiving a no decision. He developed a blister on his throwing hand in his previous start against the Diamondbacks on May 26. Jurrjens also became the 383rd different pitcher to give up a home run to Ken Griffey Jr. when he gave up Griffey's 599th in the first inning. He gave up another to Brandon Phillips in the next at-bat, marking the first time in his career that he's given up back-to-back home runs. Jurrjens lost his only start against the Marlins this season on April 15. He gave up two runs on four hits with three walks and five strikeouts in an 8-5 loss.
away_pitcher_note: At a time the Marlins needed a quality start, the right-hander delivered. Nolasco stepped up in a big in his last start, tossing 6 2/3 solid innings in a win at Philadelphia. The victory snapped a three-game losing streak, and quieted a red-hot Philadelphia offense. Nolasco yielded two runs on four hits, and he struck out five. The right-hander has now won four straight decisions since his last defeat on May 3 to the Padres. On April 17, Nolasco faced the Braves in Florida. He came out on the losing end of a 8-0 shutout. In 4 2/3 innings, he yielded six runs.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson left during the seventh inning of Sunday's game with a strained left hamstring, and was reevaluated by Braves doctors on Monday in Atlanta. Before exiting, Hudson allowed four runs -- three earned -- on seven hits and struck out three in six innings. Hudson allowed a home run in the second and third inning, the third time in four starts he has given up two homers in a game. Hudson walked three on Sunday, and it was only the third time this season that he has issued three or more walks in a game.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer earned his team-leading sixth win on June 1 against the Marlins. Moyer allowed two early home runs to Florida's Mike Jacobs, falling behind by four runs. But the veteran lefty battled back, lasting seven innings, striking out three and walking none to earn the win with a little help from his offense. The Phillies' offense has been particularly helpful to Moyer lately. In his last six starts, Moyer has received an average of about 10 runs of support.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes has pitched effectively in five of his seven starts this season and proven that he's at least improved the control issues that plagued him last year. Still, after he allowed three earned runs and issuing just one walk in six innings on Monday against the Marlins, manager Bobby Cox said the 23-year-old southpaw needs to reduce the number of pitches he leaves in the middle of the plate. When Reyes faced the Phillies on May 13 in Philadelphia, he allowed five earned runs and 11 hits in 6 2/3 innings. But he didn't issue a walk and threw first-pitch strikes to 27 of 32 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick lasted 5 1/3 innings in his last start, June 2 against the Reds. The right-hander held Cincinnati scoreless through the first three innings before running into trouble with home runs to Jay Bruce and Edwin Encarnacion. Kendrick has started three games against the Braves in his career and is 2-0 with a 4.24 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo gave up two home runs to Dan Uggla in his start Tuesday against the Marlins. In his 16 previous appearances this season, Campillo had allowed just one homer. He also didn't pitch into the fifth inning for the second time in his past three starts. Braves manager Bobby Cox pulled Campillo after he reached the 80-pitch mark, hoping that Campillo will be able to throw about 100 pitches against the Phillies. The four earned runs Tuesday were three more than he had allowed in 15 previous innings as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Eaton lasted 6 1/3 innings Tuesday against Cincinnati, giving up one run and three hits while striking out five and walking none. It was Eaton's third quality start in a row, his best stretch since his first three starts of 2008. Eaton did not face the Braves when they visited Citizens Bank Park in May, but he has eight lifetime starts against them. Eaton is 3-3 against Atlanta with a 6.14 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly was Houdini-like in his last start, escaping jams in the sixth and seventh innings against the Padres. But he couldn't get out of trouble in the eighth, and took the loss in a 2-1 decision. The lefty struck out eight, and gave up two runs on seven hits and two walks over 7 1/3 innings. It was a quality start and gave the Cubs bullpen a breather. Lilly felt his curve needed to be sharper, and that he made some mistakes. He didn't make many and seems back on track.
away_pitcher_note: Another of Tom Glavine's solid outings was spoiled Wednesday in a late-inning meltdown. Glavine pitched five innings and allowed two runs on six hits while striking out five against the Marlins. He received a no-decision after Manny Acosta blew the save in the ninth. Glavine has now struck out five in each of his past two starts. The 42-year-old left-hander is 2-2 with a 4.47 ERA this season, and has allowed two runs or less in eight of his 11 starts. Glavine is returning to Wrigley Field for the first time since he won his 300th game on Aug. 5, 2007, as a member of the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster will be happy to be back at Wrigley Field. The right-hander is 7-0 at home but has yet to win on the road. In his last start, in Los Angeles, Dempster did not get a decision, giving up three runs on five hits over 5 1/3 innings. He was cruising along until the fifth, and in the sixth, he fell behind three hitters quickly and was pulled. Dempster said he was angry at himself for not being able to go deeper into the game.
away_pitcher_note: Bennett will start after scheduled starter Jair Jurrjens sprained his right ankle leaving Wrigley Field on Tuesday night. Bennett is 0-1 with a 3.07 ERA in three spot starts this season for the Braves, who lost Tuesday's series opener, 10-5. His most recent start was an April 23 loss to the Marlins, when he allowed three runs on five hits in six innings. Bennett, who turned 28 on Tuesday, has made 27 appearances out of the bullpen this season. He has not pitched since Saturday, when he allowed two runs on two hits in one inning against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs tweaked the rotation to keep Zambrano on five days rest, and moved him up. But hide the Gatorade coolers. Zambrano lost the game and his temper in his last start against the Dodgers. He had a 3-2 lead going into the seventh, and the Dodgers scored on a throwing error, a RBI single by Russell Martin and a three-run homer by Matt Kemp. Then he kicked and tossed the coolers in the visitor's dugout. For the game, Zambrano gave up seven runs on 13 hits over 6 2/3 innings, striking out six. Manager Lou Piniella says he doesn't mind the emotion, as long as nobody gets hurt. Zambrano could've blamed his teammates, but blamed himself.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson saw his eighth win of the season vanish because of a ninth-inning error in the Braves' 4-3 loss on Friday night to the Phillies. Hudson pitched 7 2/3 strong innings, allowing one run on five hits, and was in line for the victory until an error with two outs in the ninth. Hudson walked four (one shy of his season high) and struck out three. On a hot and humid night, Hudson said he nearly ran out of gas and decided it would be best if he was taken out with two outs in the eighth and a lefty at the plate. The only run he gave up Friday came on an RBI groundout. He has pitched at least six innings in each of his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Back on his game pounding the strike zone, Garland was working on a shutout entering the eighth inning in Oakland before yielding a two-run homer to Travis Buck and departing with a season-high eight strikeouts against one walk. He'd allowed only two hits going into the eighth, winning his third straight decision. He hasn't lost since April 28. Garland is facing the Braves for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes has pitched effectively in each of his past three starts and still has gone 0-2 during that stretch.  The four earned runs he surrendered in 7 1/3 innings on Saturday night against the Phillies weren't indicative of the way he pitched. Before allowing a pair of eighth-inning runs at the end of a career-high 109-pitch effort, he'd surrendered just two solo homers. The 23-year-old southpaw's teammates say they can sense his enhanced confidence.

home_pitcher_note: Santana left with a lead after another solid effort in Oakland on Sunday, but lost his shot at the win when the A's rallied to tie the game against the bullpen. Throwing consistently in the 95-97 mph range with a nasty slider and changeup, Santana struck out nine in 6 1/3 innings, leaving four runners in scoring position while allowing two earned runs on seven hits and three walks. Santana is having an All-Star caliber season, and he'll try to improve his stock against the Braves, a team he's never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Morton will make his Major League debut on Saturday against the Angels. The 24-year-old right-hander has been impressive in Triple-A Richmond, going 5-2 with a 2.05 ERA in 12 starts. He did not give up a homer in 79 innings, and he struck out 72 while walking 27. Opponents batted .181 against him. Morton allowed a season-high four runs and four hits in five innings on Sunday. The Braves would have preferred to let Morton mature in the Minor Leagues, but weren't afforded that luxury with a rash of injuries to their starting rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders had easily his worst start of the season Monday against the Rays. He allowed eight earned runs in just 4 2/3 innings and gave up three consecutive home runs to Evan Longoria, Willy Aybar and Dioner Navarro to begin the second inning. The eight earned runs he allowed tied a career worst. Saunders has never pitched against the Braves, but is 1-0 with a 4.05 ERA in two career Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo allowed three runs and seven hits in 5 1/3 innings on Sunday against the Phillies. Campillo threw a career-high 105 pitches, but didn't factor in the decision. Sunday was the first time he pitched into the sixth inning since his first start, on May 20 against the Mets, when he pitched six strong innings. Campillo has faced the Angels once in his career, Sept. 20, 2007. He gave up four hits and four runs in 2 2/3 innings last season as a reliever.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez is coming off one of his best outings of the season. He tossed seven shutout innings, struck out three and gave up just four hits in a no-decision against San Francisco on Wednesday. The right-hander showed supreme control against the Giants, effectively mixing his fastball, curveball and changeup to fool San Francisco's hitters. Jimenez has just one win this season, and it came against the Braves on April 8, when he allowed three runs on six hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens is expected to start the Braves' makeup game against the Rockies. The game was originally scheduled for April 10 but was postponed because of snow. Jurrjens was scratched from his start on Wednesday against the Cubs after twisting his right ankle while walking down the stairs the night before. The 22-year-old right-hander allowed a season-high 11 hits in his last start, June 5 against the Marlins, but he got the win, his sixth of the season. He has given up four homers in his past three starts, after surrendering just one in his first 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla avoided a loss and got a no-decision in his last outing, when the Rangers scored 10 runs in the final three innings against the Royals. He went six innings and gave up five runs (four earned). Padilla has already surpassed his win total (six) of last year. In his his last three starts, Padilla is 2-1 but has given up 12 runs in 18 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson allowed one run on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings on Thursday against the Cubs, but the Braves' bullpen surrendered a ninth-inning homer to negate Hudson's strong effort. Hudson did exactly what an ace was supposed to do to halt a dismal road losing streak, but he received no help. The Braves went 0-for-9 with runners in scoring position to provide very little run support (two runs) for Hudson. He has pitched into at least the seventh inning in each of his past five starts, and he has not allowed more than three earned runs during that span. Hudson is 6-5 with a 4.01 ERA in 16 career starts against the Rangers. His last start against the Rangers came on July 13, 2005, when he gave up five runs on five hits in 2 2/3 innings and took the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Hurley made his Major League debut on Thursday against the Royals and allowed four runs in six innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out three in the Rangers' 6-5 loss. A first-round Draft pick from 2004, Hurley was 2-5 with a 5.30 ERA in 13 starts at Triple-A Oklahoma, including 1-2 with a 2.57 ERA in his last four starts before being called up.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes recorded his first win since May 18 after scattering five hits and two runs in eight innings on Friday against the Angels, snapping the Braves' five-game losing streak. He gave up a solo homer in the second inning but recovered and picked up his third win of the season. He hasn't pitched badly in his past three starts, he just hasn't been rewarded with a victory. He has allowed no more than four earned runs in each of those three starts, and has struck out at least five in three of his past four starts. Reyes has shown remarkable improvement from the beginning of the season, when he was erratic with his location and couldn't pitch deep in the games. The 23-year-old left-hander has since become a dependable mid-rotation starter.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 0-2 with a 5.35 ERA in his last six starts. The Rangers are 1-8 on the season in his nine starts, even though six of them have been classified as "quality." He is 1-0 with a 3.32 ERA in seven games, including five starts, at home, as opposed to 0-3 with a 7.33 ERA on the road. Opponents are hitting .302 off him with runners in scoring position and .206 off him through his first 60 pitches and .319 off him after that.
away_pitcher_note: Morton impressed during his Major League debut on Saturday, limiting the Angels to three earned runs over six innings. He was perfect in four of his innings and allowed each of the three runs with two outs. The lanky 24-year-old right-hander, who was a third-round selection in the 2002 First-Year Player Draft, has a live fastball and the ability to buckle hitters with a sharp curveball. He was 4-2 with a 2.05 ERA in 13 appearances (12 starts) for Triple-A Richmond.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo lost his first start of the season Sunday against the Angels, despite allowing two runs on seven hits in a career-high eight innings. The Angels' two runs off Campillo came on a good pitch -- a changeup down in the zone that Casey Kotchman looped down the right-field line and into the second row. Campillo struck out seven, but lost for the first time in 28 career appearances. He has not given up more than four runs in any of his six starts this season. Campillo made eight appearances with the Mariners from 2005-2007, and will be facing them for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander gave the Mariners a quality start against the Nationals, but they didn't get him his fifth win. He settled for a no-decision in a game he surrendered two earned runs over six innings, striking out eight. 63 of his 100 pitches were strikes and, for the fourth consecutive start, did not allow a home run. Bedard has never faced the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: After missing a start when he rolled his ankle on the Wrigley Field dugout steps, Jurrjens rebounded in commanding fashion Monday, shutting down the Rockies for 7 2/3 innings, the longest start of his career. He pounded the inside of the strike zone and went to a rejuvenated and devastating changeup for big outs, repeatedly stranding runs in scoring positions. Jurrjens was efficient with his pitches, taking advantage of an overly aggressive Rockies lineup that swung at a lot of first pitches, and pitching to contact, allowing eight hits and two walks while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn put together his fourth consecutive solid outing with an impressive performance during his last start against the Nationals, holding the NL East team to one run over six innings, nearly a carbon copy of his previous outing against the Blue Jays. Washburn settled for another no-decision and remained stuck on two wins this season. The Braves are one of three MLB teams Washburn never has faced.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson gave up a season-high six runs in a loss Tuesday to the Rangers, his first start since he was treated for dehydration following a game against the Cubs. Hudson allowed six hits and walked two. He struck out three of the first six batters he faced, but struggled through 4 1/3 innings. It was the first time Hudson had allowed six runs since he gave up that many in a July 5, 2007, loss to the Dodgers, a span of 30 starts. Entering his start Sunday against the Mariners, Hudson is 0-10 with a 7.82 ERA in Interleague Play with the Braves. He is 12-6 with a 3.32 ERA in 23 career starts against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander's last start ended prematurely, not because of his pitching but his deportment. He said something he shouldn't have to first-base umpire Bill Welke and was ejected from his start against the Marlins two outs into the fifth inning. Silva has gone more than two months since his last win, which came on April 17 against the Athletics. He was 3-0 at the time, but has lost eight straight since. The veteran has a 2-0 record and a 2.12 ERA in his career against the Braves, tossing a shutout against the National League East team last season.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes allowed two runs -- one earned -- on five hits for the second straight start, but when he left after the seventh inning, the Braves still hadn't broken out of a 2-2 tie. The 23-year-old left-hander, who has made significant strides since the first month of the season, struck out three and walked four, one of which led to his only earned run of the night. Reyes lost against the Brewers earlier this season, on May 28, despite allowing just one run on two hits in seven innings. He also struck out a career-high nine in that game.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets didn't have his best stuff last time out, but still was able to claim a victory as his teammates provided enough run support to give the Brewers a 5-4 win. Sheets (8-1) walked four batters for the first time in nine starts, but won his fourth straight decision by limiting the Blue Jays to two runs over six innings of work. Closer Salomon Torres came in to work out of a jam and record the last five outs for the save, giving Sheets his team-high eighth win.

home_pitcher_note: Morton allowed three runs Thursday against the Rangers, but his five-plus innings of work were spoiled when reliever Jeff Ridgway gave up a three-run homer to the first batter he faced. Two of the runs were charged to Morton. The lanky 24-year-old right-hander scattered five hits before departing with no outs in the sixth after allowing two baserunners. He threw 91 pitches, striking out three and walking four. He didn't possess the same pinpoint control that he had in his big-league debut on Saturday. In that start, he impressed with a mid-90s fastball and a sharp sinker.
away_pitcher_note: Bush carried a no-hitter into the eighth inning in his last start, lasting until Lyle Overbay lifted a 1-0 pitch into left field to break up the no-hit bid. Bush (3-7) went on to allow a run in the inning, but this outing was by far his best of the season. The veteran right-hander carried a perfect game into the fifth inning, setting down the first 15 batters he faced; carried a no-hitter through seven, walking just one; and ended up with eight innings of two-hit baseball to his credit.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo was hit hard by the Mariners on Friday night, allowing four runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings. He took the loss, his second of the season. Campillo exited in the seventh after allowing the go-ahead run to score and two baserunners to reach base. The 29-year-old right-hander allowed four doubles, and five others reached the warning track. Campillo hasn't won since May 29, which coincidentally came against the Brewers. In that start, he allowed one run on four hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan had his shortest start in 10 years, as he didn't make it out of the second inning against the Orioles on Friday. The first three batters of the game singled, eight Orioles came to the plate and four runs scored in the inning. Suppan notched two outs in the top of the second inning, but was knocked out of the game when two more runs scored and he walked the bases loaded. The right-hander ended up with a final line of six runs on seven hits, with two walks and one strikeout in 1 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, McGowan picked up a win despite a rocky performance. In five innings, the righty allowed four runs (three earned) on nine hits with two strikeouts and one walk against the Pirates. Walks have played a key role in McGowan's 4-1 record over his past six outings. In those starts, McGowan has 32 strikeouts, compared to just six walks. In his previous three starts, McGowan had 10 walks against eight strikeouts, and he went 0-2 with a 7.80 ERA over that span. McGowan is 4-1 with a 1.73 ERA at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens had another strong outing on Saturday night, but he wasn't rewarded with a win. The 22-year-old right-hander allowed three runs -- none earned -- in six innings, striking out four and walking two. The Mariners scored three runs on two errors in the first inning off Jurrjens. Despite the long first inning, he responded well and struck out the side in the second. Jurrjens will be facing Toronto for the first time. He is 2-3 with a 3.98 ERA in seven road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: With Shaun Marcum (right elbow) on the disabled list and likely out until after the All-Star break, the Jays need a fifth starter for Saturday and again on July 13.
