Parrish gets the call after going 10-1 with a 2.74 ERA in 15 games, including 11 starts, at Triple-A Syracuse. Over those outings, the 30-year-old lefty struck out 92 and walked 35 across 82 innings. Parrish is 12-12 with a 4.63 ERA in 161 big league games between stints with the Orioles and Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson finally got over his Interleague woes on Sunday, pitching seven shutout innings against the Mariners to improve his record to 1-10 in 13 Interleague starts in a Braves uniform. He walked four and struck out two, and didn't allow a baserunner to reach third base. He improved to 116-5 in games in which he has received four or more runs of support while he is still in the game. His eight wins are the most on the Braves' staff. Hudson has pitched extremely well against Toronto in the past, going 10-2 with a 2.61 ERA in 14 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Facing the Reds in his last start, Burnett dominated the Cincinnati hitters for most of his eight innings. The hard-throwing right-hander allowed just one run on four hits, while walking three and striking out seven. Burnett needed 111 pitches to complete the outing. The Toronto starter has now allowed two earned runs or less in six starts this season. In his career against the Braves, Burnett is 4-9 with a 4.03 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes pitched the shortest outing of his career (2 1/3 innings) in a loss to the Brewers on Monday. He gave up a two-run homer and two run-scoring doubles before exiting with one out and the bases loaded in the third. Reyes had trouble locating his fastball, which led to six hits and two walks. Reyes was 1-2 with a 2.80 ERA in five straight starts leading up to Monday's. He recorded just one strikeout on Monday; he had 29 in his past five starts. The 23-year-old left-hander has never faced Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has given the Braves three solid outings to start his Major League career, yet the 24-year-old right-hander now has two losses. He was dealt another tough-luck loss on Tuesday night, when he allowed four runs -- two earned -- on six hits in six innings against the Brewers. He has two quality starts in three outings, but the Braves haven't been able to manufacture runs until he is out of the ballgame. While Morton has been in the game, the Braves have scored just two runs in his past two starts, a span of 12 innings. Morton will get a taste of a division rivalry when he faces the Phillies for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old turned in the longest and best start of his career against Oakland on June 25, throwing eight shutout innings, walking one and striking out four. The win moved Kendrick into a three-way tie with Jamie Moyer and Cole Hamels for the team lead. He's started twice against the Braves in 2008, and pitched well in both outings, allowing a combined five earned runs over 11 1/3 innings. This year, the Phillies are 12-4 in Kendrick's starts -- the best record among Phillies starters.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo has become more than just a pleasant surprise for the Braves -- he's a bona fide starter with an entire arsenal of pitches. The 29-year-old right-hander tossed seven strong innings Wednesday against the Brewers, allowing two runs on four hits and picking up his first home win of the season. After allowing two run-scoring doubles, Campillo retired the next 12 batters he faced. He said his start June 15 against the Angels was better -- two runs in a complete-game effort -- but he was equally dominant against the Brewers. Campillo got a no-decision against the Phillies on June 8, when he allowed three runs on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings. He also allowed six hits in two relief appearances against the Phillies, which totaled 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has given up three or fewer runs in 12 of his 16 outings this season, and the Phillies are 7-9 overall when he starts. His June 26 performance was another example of this trend. Unfortunately, two of the three runs he allowed came in the first inning, and Oakland starter Rich Harden sailed from there. Eaton has made one other start against the Braves this season, and gave up three runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens limited the Blue Jays to three hits in eight strong innings, and has not allowed an earned run in his last 23 2/3 innings. The three hits off Jurrjens on Friday were singles. The 22-year-old right-hander has not lost since May 12, and he has lowered his ERA to 2.94. He has pitched at least six innings in each of his past four starts. Jurrjens will be making his first career start against the Phillies. He is 5-0 with a 2.49 ERA in eight home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels is coming off an outing in which he allowed four runs in seven innings to the Rangers, a considerable accomplishment against the highest scoring team in the American League. He pitched a four-hit shutout against the Braves on May 15 in Philadelphia, walking two and striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson was in the midst of a good season until Interleague Play, during which he went 1-3 with a 7.17 ERA.  In three career starts against the Astros, he’s compiled 24 innings and allowed just three earned runs. In his past two starts against them, he's totaled 17 innings and allowed just seven hits. The veteran right-hander is 6-1 with a 2.24 ERA in eight home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler has been impressive since joining the rotation, and in his last two starts -- 6 1/3 innings, one run allowed against Texas and 5 2/3 innings, one run allowed against Boston -- he was particularly impressive. The 36-year-old right-hander is 1-4 with a 5.12 ERA in 12 career appearances (five starts) against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes allowed one run on six hits in seven strong innings on Sunday against the Blue Jays, but he was saddled with the loss when the Braves dropped another one-run road game, this time 1-0. Reyes stranded a runner on third base in four innings. The 23-year-old left-hander was much more effective with his fastball than he was in his previous start, when he pitched 2 1/3 innings and gave up four runs. He is 1-0 with a 5.59 ERA in two career starts against the Astros, both of which came last season.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson gets the start in place of Roy Oswalt, who is healing from a hip abductor strain. Sampson opened the season in the rotation but moved to the bullpen after going 3-3 with a 6.04 ERA in 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton experienced the first rocky start of his young career on Tuesday, when he allowed the Phillies five earned runs and eight hits, including two homers in two innings. The 24-year-old right-hander hadn't allowed a home run in any of his previous 15 starts -- including 12 for Triple-A Richmond -- this year. Used primarily as a reliever last year, he has already thrown 18 1/3 innings this year, more than he did last year and within two innings of his 2006 total.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had a rare poor home start his last time out, allowing five earned runs over five innings, walking four and striking out five. Rodriguez has had more good outings than bad this year, and the club is confident he can be a force in the rotation now and in the future. Rodriguez has faced the Braves three times in his career, twice as a starter. The lefty is 1-1 with a 10.13 ERA vs. Atlanta, allowing 12 earned runs over 10 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Three weeks on the disabled list did the trick for Hiroki Kuroda, who returned with seven scoreless innings against the Astros and showed no signs of the right shoulder tendinitis that sidelined him. He scattered five hits, walked only one and threw an efficient 83 pitches, with his fastball clocked around 94 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo uncharacteristically struggled with his control on Wednesday night and paid the price against a talented Phillies lineup. Whenever he falls behind, the right-hander's varied repertoire of pitches becomes limited.  This was the second time the Phillies had seen him as a starter and his fourth appearance against them. The Dodgers haven't seen the 29-year-old rookie hurler this season. But there might be some reason to wonder if the National League will have better success against him when they get their second looks later this year.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley has a four-game win streak, although his most recent victory in Houston wasn't nearly as bizarre as the previous one, in which the Dodgers scored the game's only run without a hit. Nonetheless, Billingsley has emerged as the most consistent starter on the club, with three quality starts in his last four outings after losing his first four decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Before allowing four runs to the Phillies on Thursday night, Jurrjens had gone three consecutive starts  (21 2/3 innings) without allowing an earned run.   The three homers  --  all solo shots --  he surrendered were two less than he'd allowed in his first 16 starts of the season.  This was the first loss in nine starts for the 22-year-old right-hander, who limited the Dodgers to one earned run in seven innings on April 20.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe has been the victim of stingy run support by his teammates this year, but they got him off the hook and turned a loss into a win by erasing a three-run deficit in a 10-7 win over the Giants. Lowe has pitched much better than that game and suffered defeats this year, so there was some justice in picking up a win despite allowing eight hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson scattered four hits over seven strong innings and picked up his ninth win of the season Friday against the Astros. Hudson struck out six for the first time since May 27, a span of six starts. The only run charged to Hudson came after Kelly Johnson bobbled a potential inning-ending, double-play grounder one batter earlier. Hudson is 5-1 with a 4.07 ERA in nine career starts against the Dodgers. He last faced them on July 5, 2007, when he allowed six runs on 10 hits in three innings and didn't factor in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy is coming off one of his best starts of the season, having allowed just three hits in seven shutout innings in the Padres' 3-0 victory at Arizona on July 5. Peavy, making his fifth start since missing a month after he strained his right below, retired 14 consecutive hitters at one point, showing a live fastball that touched 96 mph and a the same kind of devastating slider that helped him run away with the National League Cy Young Award honors in 2007. He allowed a double to Chad Tracy in the seventh inning but struck out Stephen Drew and Chris Young before getting Miguel Montero on a pop-up to end the inning.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes lost his third straight start Saturday against the Astros after allowing four runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings. He was coming off arguably his most impressive outing of the season, when he gave up one run on six hits in seven strong innings against the Blue Jays but lost, 1-0. Although the 23-year-old left-hander hasn't allowed more than four earned runs in any of his past eight starts, he is occasionally struggling with his command, which can get him into trouble, especially early in games. Reyes allowed two runs (one earned) on five hits against the Padres on May 8, before leaving with two out in the third with a recurring blister on his index finger.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux was his usual self in getting multiple ground-ball outs in his last outing against the Florida Marlins on July 7, but he still came away with the loss. Maddux has been a victim of either no-decisions or decisions where he hasn't gotten enough run support all season. Against the Marlins, Maddux went a solid six innings giving up two runs (one earned) on four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Charlie Morton gave up six runs on eight hits Sunday against the Astros, but his start was inconsequential after the Braves needed 17 innings to pick up the win. Morton hung a two-out breaking ball to Ty Wigginton, who hit a third-inning grand slam and put Morton and the Braves in an early hole. Morton responded well, though, retiring the next nine batters he faced before giving up another run in the sixth inning. Morton is now 0-2 with an 8.36 ERA in three starts at Turner Field. He is 1-0 with a 4.91 ERA (6 ER in 11 IP) in two road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf is coming off his best start in recent memory, when he allowed one run in seven innings with one strikeout in the Padres' 10-1 victory over the Marlins on Tuesday. Wolf had lost his previous four starts, but after allowing seven runs in three innings against Colorado on July 2, he and pitching coach Darren Balsley looked at video of his starts earlier this season and spotted a mechanical flaw that wasn't allowing him to get as much extension with his left arm. The change worked well and Wolf not only had good command but good stuff against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo pitched seven strong innings Monday against the Dodgers, but he hung two breaking balls and it cost him three runs -- and a win. He allowed five hits, walked three and struck out two. Some in the Braves' organization have referred to Campillo as the Mexican Greg Maddux, and he will get the chance to face the former Braves hurler on Sunday. Campillo allowed one run on two hits in 1 1/3 innings of relief on May 8 against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson held the Dodgers without a hit for four innings on July 9 but was saddled with a loss, his seventh of the season, when the Braves could produce just one run off Derek Lowe. Hudson scattered four hits and two runs over seven strong innings and trimmed his ERA to 3.16. In 11 career starts against the Nationals, Hudson is 7-1 with a 1.13 ERA. He is 1-0 against them this season, allowing three runs on 13 hits in 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Redding picked up his first win in 10 starts on July 11 against Houston, snapping a streak of nine straight no-decisions. He pitched six innings, allowing no runs and striking out six. The seasoned right-hander said after the game that he felt comfortable with his fastball, which helped him get ahead of hitters routinely in the Nationals 10-0 win over Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens capped off the first half of his rookie season with a resounding victory, pitching six innings and striking out six in a 9-3 Braves win over the Dodgers on July 8. It was Jurrjens' ninth win of the season, as the 22-year-old entered the All-Star break with loads of confidence. Jurrjens will be returning from the All-Star break to face the Nationals, against whom he has had success this season. He gave up just two hits and one run in seven innings on April 30 but did not factor in the decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan threw his 13th quality start July 9 in a 5-0 victory against Arizona, his first win since May 18. Long suffering from poor run support, Lannan got more than enough against the D-backs, as Jesus Flores' three-run homer packed away the game in the sixth. Though he admitted he didn't have his "best" stuff, Lannan still threw six shutout innings, inducing three double plays in the process.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes' final start before the All-Star break lasted only four innings, as he gave up two runs on five hits, including two triples, in a losing effort. Reyes struggled with his command and was taken out after throwing just 64 pitches. The 23-year-old left-hander has not reached the sixth inning in three of his past four starts. Reyes hasn't won since June 13, a span of five starts. He has never faced the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Perez got himself into trouble more than once against Houston in his last start before the break, allowing nine hits over six innings. However, thanks to six strikeouts and some cluth pitching, the left-hander allowed just three runs to cross the plate. It would not be enough, however, as the Nationals fell to Houston, 5-0, at home.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a storybook beginning to Volstad's big league career. Promoted from Double-A Carolina on July 6, he collected a win that day, tossing two innings of scoreless relief. Then on July 11, in his first big league start, the 21-year-old was on the verge of a complete game, but on his 100th pitch, he allowed a two-out RBI single to Russell Martin. Volstad ended up beating the Dodgers at Dodger Stadium, giving up one run in 8 2/3 innings. So he's allowed just one run in 10 2/3 innings to start off his MLB career. He struck out six in L.A. and walked just one.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo allowed two runs on five hits in six strong innings Sunday against the Padres, and he finally received some run support in picking up just his second win since May 29. He struck out four and walked two. Campillo would have pitched at least seven innings, but he fouled a ball off his left ankle during his at-bat in the seventh. The 29-year-old right-hander has made three appearances against the Marlins this season, including one start. That start came on June 3, when he gave up four runs on six hits -- including two homers -- in four innings. He did not factor in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins are expected to make it official after Monday's game, but unofficially, VandenHurk appears the choice to take the mound in the second of three with the Braves. The right-hander opened the season as Florida's No. 2 starter, but he was 0-1 and threw 5 1/3 innings this season before being optioned to Double-A Carolina. With the Mudcats, the right-hander was 3-3 with a 4.32 ERA. He had been on the Minor League DL for a while with an ulnar nerve issue.
away_pitcher_note: Morton allowed one run on four hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Padres on July 12, earning his first win since his Major League debut on June 14. Since that win against the Angels, Morton was 0-2 with a 7.58 ERA in four starts. Against the Padres, he struck out four and walked three. Prior to that start, he had allowed at least five runs in each of his past two starts. The 24-year-old right-hander has never faced the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco hasn't been very accustomed to losing recently, but that's exactly what happened in his last start Friday against the Phillies. The 25-year-old gave up four runs on seven hits in seven innings and took his first loss since June 5 -- a span of eight starts. That June 5 loss to the Braves was also the last time he allowed more than three runs in an outing. Going into the All-Star break, Nolasco sported a five-game winning streak and had allowed just six runs in his previous 29 innings. He exited Friday's game after striking out five, walking one and throwing 100 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson battled some post-All-Star-break rust while allowing the Nationals five earned runs in 6 2/3 innings on Friday night, unable to notch his 16th quality start of the season. Hudson faced the Marlins on April 16, when he lacked velocity and allowed six earned runs in a season-short three innings. He is 4-1 with a 2.95 ERA in seven career starts at Dolphin Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick set career highs for earned runs allowed and home runs surrendered in his loss to the Marlins Saturday. Florida tagged him for seven earned runs, including three homers, in 4 1/3 innings. Still, Kendrick remains one of Philly's most reliable starters. Philadelphia has recorded a 14-6 record in his outings, the best mark among the team's starters. In five career starts against the Braves, Kendrick is 3-0 with a 4.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: A lengthy layoff during the All-Star break seemed to affect Jurrjens' control on Saturday, when he allowed the Nationals five earned runs in 6 1/3 innings. The 22-year-old rookie right-hander has lost two of his past three starts, including his July 3 outing against the Phillies. The three homers he surrendered that evening matched the total he’d allowed in his previous five starts combined. He has been inconsistent since not allowing an earned run in his final three June starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels had only two blemishes in his last start, against the Marlins on Sunday. But those two mistakes, solo home runs to Cody Ross and Jeremy Hermida, were enough to hand the lefty a no-decision. Other than that, the 24-year-old was in fine form, giving up four hits while striking out seven through eight innings before leaving with 96 pitches under his belt. Hamels had a no-hitter through three innings and retired nine straight batters at one point. His velocity, however, was down a few mph after the long layoff with the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton will make his first Major League start in 35 months Saturday when he pitches the second game of a critical three-game set against the Phillies. The 35-year-old left-hander has strained his left pectoral muscle twice this season and had his recent rehab assignment derailed by a strained left groin. But after tossing an incident-free bullpen session on Tuesday, manager Bobby Cox said Hampton would get the start Saturday in place of young lefty Jo-Jo Reyes, who has lost five consecutive starts. Hampton is 32-20 in three injury-shortened seasons with the Braves. He hasn't pitched in a Major League game since Aug. 19, 2005. He missed the entire 2006 and 2007 seasons after having separate surgeries on his left elbow.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton did not get a decision in his Phillies debut against the Mets on Tuesday at Shea Stadium, surrendering five runs in six innings. He gave up a few untimely walks and left two breaking balls up that resulted in home runs. Still, the Phillies will continue to look to the right-hander to be an innings-eater and take the place of the struggling Adam Eaton in the Phils' rotation. Blanton, having just moved to the National League from Oakland, has never faced the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: With the Braves in dire need of a win, Campillo pitched his finest outing since he became a starter in mid May. He scattered two hits -- both singles -- over seven shutout innings on Monday, needing just 91 pitches. Campillo's array of offspeed pitches fanned six Marlins, which matched his total over his past three starts. The two hits allowed were the fewest since May 24, when he pitched four innings against the D-backs before leaving with a blister. In his last start against the Phillies, on July 2, Campillo allowed five runs on eight hits in five innings and took the loss. Campillo is 0-1 with a 5.27 ERA in four games (two starts) against the Phillies this season, surrendering eight runs in 13 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morton was recalled from Triple-A Richmond to start Monday's series opener against the Cardinals after lefty Jo-Jo Reyes, Monday's projected starter, was needed during Sunday's game. Morton was optioned to Richmond on Saturday to make room on the active roster for Mike Hampton. Since impressing while making his first three career Major League starts in June, Morton has battled rookie inconsistency. He is 1-2 with a 7.58 ERA in his past four starts. While facing the Marlins last week, a pair of walks hurt him when Mike Jacobs followed with a homer. The lanky 24-year-old right-hander has had trouble showing consistent command with his live fastball. This will be his first career appearance against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Though his line against the Brewers in his last start was very good -- five innings pitched, seven hits, one earned run -- Looper had to exit early because of a high pitch count. He also picked up the loss because the Brewers' CC Sabathia shut out the Cardinals. However, Looper rebounded from a poor start on July 18 and pitched a solid game against one of the better lineups in the Majors. Looper is winless since June 24 -- a statistic he would love to change against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Tim Hudson has been placed on the disabled list, so the ongoing Atlanta shuffling means that Campillo will start. The right-hander started on Sunday, but he pitched only 1 2/3 innings before a lengthy rain delay in Philadelphia forced him out of the game.
away_pitcher_note: For a while on Thursday, it appeared Wellemeyer was going to win his second straight decision for the first time since June 5. After the Cardinals bullpen lost their 23rd game of the year, though, Wellemeyer received another no-decision. For four innings, Wellemeyer had excellent stuff but succumbed to two long innings that drove up his pitch count. It was a better showing from May's Pitcher of the Month, though, and Wellemeyer another solid start would seem to say he has regained his consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Jair Jurrjens tossed eight shutout innings and allowed just three hits Friday against the Phillies, helping the Braves claim a crucial series-opening win over their division rival. Jurrjens made a spectacular defensive play to end the eighth inning, knocking down a comebacker and making a strong throw to first to get the out. Jurrjens also didn't allow a runner to reach third base. The 22-year-old right-hander walked one and struck out six while becoming the second Braves pitcher to reach 10 wins this season; Tim Hudson has 11. Jurrjens trimmed his ERA to 3.02.
away_pitcher_note: This is the moment the Redbirds have awaited for more than a season and a half, the return of their ace to the mound after a lengthy battle with elbow troubles that culminated in Tommy John surgery last July. Carpenter probably won't go much past 90 pitches, and his usually exceptional command may still be less than perfect. But he's the man for the Redbirds, and his return is a very, very big deal.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton, making his first start since Aug. 19, 2005, allowed six runs on eight hits in four-plus innings Saturday against the Phillies, but did not factor in the decision. Staked to a 9-3 lead, Hampton exited with the bases loaded and no out in the fifth. All three baserunners scored in what became a demoralizing 10-9 loss. The oft-injured left-hander tossed 91 pitches -- 55 for strikes -- and threw first-pitch strikes to 12 of the 22 batters he faced. Hampton, who missed the first four months of the season with a strained left pectoral muscle, is 10-8 with a 3.59 ERA in 26 games (21 starts) against St. Louis. He hasn't faced the Cardinals since May 12, 2004, when he allowed four runs on eight hits in six innings and lost.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro has been getting leads, but not holding them. And that's a problem. He's been ahead at some point in 15 of his starts, and yet he has only picked up three wins. He can be excellent, but he can also be frustrating. With Adam Wainwright's return coming fairly soon, Pineiro is one of three conceivable candidates to be bumped from the rotation, so he needs to show something in his next couple of starts.

home_pitcher_note: James, who was scratched Wednesday at Triple-A Richmond so he could make this start, has not pitched for the Braves since May 15, when he allowed five runs on six hits and walked five in four innings. After that start, he was optioned to Richmond, where he was 4-5 with a 2.48 ERA in 14 games (13 starts). The 26-year-old has not pitched for the R-Braves since last Friday, when he allowed six hits and one run in six strong innings. Control was the primary reason the Braves optioned James; he walked 16 batters in 23 innings, a span of five starts. James has issued four walks in his past 17 innings for Richmond.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan was fine for four innings Sunday, but things turned abruptly in the fifth when he was lit up by Houston for seven runs, including three on the second homer of the game from Geoff Blum. In his second start since returning from a brief stint on the disabled list, the right-hander finished with eight runs on 11 hits allowed in six innings. He has yet to recapture the form that made him an integral contributor in May and June, allowing 22 runs in 21 July innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morton allowed a career-high eight runs on seven hits and issued four walks against the Cardinals on Monday in yet another disheartening Braves loss. Morton struggled mightily with his command, leaving too many fastballs and sliders up in the zone. The 24-year-old was briefly demoted to Triple-A Richmond last Saturday, but was needed two days later to fill an open roster spot. Morton is now 1-3 with a 9.53 ERA in his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia didn't have his best stuff last time out, against the Cubs, and didn't get a decision as a defensive error by the Brewers allowed Chicago to tie the game. The Cubs would later break the tie and beat Milwaukee closer Salomon Torres. Sabathia missed his shot first shot at reaching 5-0 since his trade to the Brewers.  His final line was four runs -- three earned -- on nine hits over 6 2/3 innings of work.  He threw 129 pitches as the Cubs hitters made him work. After the game, Sabathia said, "I really didn't have my out pitch, my cutter. I was leaving that up and away and they were just looking for that. I tried to do the best I could."

home_pitcher_note: Campillo scattered two runs and seven hits over seven strong innings Tuesday against the Cardinals, but did not factor into the decision after the Braves' bullpen allowed six runs in the eighth and ninth innings. Campillo was staked to a 2-1 lead in the sixth before allowing a solo homer to Albert Pujols, who took advantage of a hanging breaking ball over the inside half of the plate. Campillo's schedule was a little off for this start after having his previous outing, on Sunday against the Phillies, stopped after 1 2/3 innings and a near two-hour rain delay.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets and the Brewers were stunned by the Cubs in his last outing. Sheets started back-to-back with CC Sabathia in a 1-2 punch that Milwaukee hoped would knock Chicago out of their four-game series, but instead the Brewers aces dropped two straight and dug a hole for the club. Sheets started out strong, allowing just one run in the first five innings, but gave up seven straight hits to lead off the sixth on his way to a game-changing, five-run inning. He only notched one out in the inning before being pulled and ended up taking the loss as the Cubs' Carlos Zambrano was brilliant, shutting out the Brewers for eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cain pitched superbly in July, recording a 2.09 ERA in six outings. All but one was a quality start and he pitched shutout ball in three of them, including a complete-game effort July 24 against Washington. In Cain's last start, he surrendered two runs in seven innings in a 2-0 loss at Los Angeles. Cain threw 89 strikes among a season-high 118 pitches in that one and walked none for the second start in a row, the first time in his career that he has managed this feat.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens continued his impressive rookie season while allowing three earned runs and seven hits in seven innings against the Cardinals on Wednesday. But the 22-year-old right-hander lost for the second time in the three starts he's made since the All-Star break. He has pitched at least seven innings in five of his last seven starts. This will be his first career appearance against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez just finished a month he'd like to forget. After sailing in June (5-1, 3.10 ERA), he struggled in July (0-3, 8.57 ERA). He failed to last more than 5 1/3 innings in any of his five starts during the month and battled control problems, walking 16 in 21 innings. The Braves treated Sanchez rudely in his two relief appearances against them last year, as he absorbed a defeat and recorded a 10.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton still hasn't regained the form he had before his injury woes began in 2005.  But while making his first two starts since then,  he has at least proven durable and capable of being successful in the Majors.   While allowing the Cardinals four earned runs in five innings on Thursday, he showed inconsistent control with his sinker.  Still, he thought his command was better than it had been five days earlier in Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum recorded his fifth double-digit strikeout total and second in a row in his last start, collecting 11 at San Diego Friday. He received his second consecutive no-decision despite leaving with a 2-1 lead after seven innings. It marked the sixth time the bullpen has blown a lead it inherited from Lincecum, who's 3-2 with a 3.55 ERA in 10 starts at AT&T Park. Lincecum started twice against Atlanta last year and won both, although his ERA against the Braves was 4.09.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing the Brewers six earned runs in just 2 2/3 innings during his return from the Minors on Friday, James didn't provided much reason for optimism.  He surrendered a pair of homers and issued four walks. In his past 15 Major League starts, he has  gone 5-6 with a 7.29 ERA, issued 29 walks and  allowed 24 homers.  Plagued by inconsistent control and the inability to develop a third pitch, he's far from being the same pitcher who won 11 games both of the past two seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Petit didn't have his best outing against the Dodgers in Los Angeles. The right-hander allowed three runs on five hits over five innings. His big mistake was a fastball that he left too far out over the plate that Manny Ramirez clubbed for a homer. Petit took the place of Micah Owings in the rotation after Owings was sent to Triple-A Tucson. Petit lacks overpowering stuff but has a good feel for pitching and excellent control.
away_pitcher_note: Morton regained some confidence while allowing the Brewers two runs over seven innings on Saturday. The 24-year-old right-hander, who had been 1-3 with a 9.53 ERA in his previous five starts, allowed just one hit during the first six innings and showed more consistency with his control. He has allowed at least one homer in five of his last six starts. This will be his first career appearance against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis went from high to low in a hurry in his last start, as the Dodgers roughed him up for five runs in just 1 2/3 innings. It was quite a contrast from the start before, when he carried a no-hitter into the seventh against the Padres. This time around, Davis lacked command and when he fell behind hitters, he had to come over the plate with his stuff and they made him pay. He is better off when he can work the corners.
away_pitcher_note: Jorge Campillo scattered six hits and struck out six in seven shutout innings against the Brewers on Sunday. The 29-year-old right-hander's only trouble came in the seventh, but he struck out the final two batters to end the inning and the threat. He is 3-0 with a 1.26 ERA in his past five starts. Campillo started against the D-backs earlier this season, on May 24, but had to leave after the fourth inning when a blister formed on his right index finger. In that start, he had allowed two hits and struck out three in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Haren struggled with command his last time out against the Pirates, but thanks to 13 runs of support, the All-Star right-hander picked up his fifth consecutive win. He struggled early on, allowing three first-inning runs, but the D-backs roughed up the Pittsburgh pitching staff for their biggest offensive explosion of the season. Haren has given up seven runs in just 11 2/3 innings, but still is 2-0 in his career against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens was victimized by multiple miscues and some inconsistent control while allowing the Giants four runs in six innings on Monday. The 22-year-old rookie had allowed just one earned run in his four previous road starts combined.  His only previous appearance against the D-backs came on May 26, when allowed eight hits in 4 2/3 innings. His struggles that day could have been blamed on a blister that affected him for three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Webb was true to his form in his last outing, giving up only one fly-ball out in his complete-game victory over the Pirates. He cruised through the first eight innings, not allowing a single runner past first base until the ninth inning. Webb made quick work of the Bucs, too, as the time of the game didn't even eclipse two hours. Against the Braves, Webb is 2-2 with a 1.90 ERA and two shutouts in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton regained the grip on his sinker and used it to produce 13 groundouts while earning his first Major League win since Aug. 14, 2005, on Tuesday night.  While tossing seven solid innings against the Giants, he showed the tenacity that had been lacking in his previous two starts this season. The veteran southpaw, who missed the past two seasons while recovering from separate elbow surgeries, says he's felt more confident after each of his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has seemingly turned the corner while allowing runs in just one of his past 14 innings. The best outing of his young career arguably came on Thursday, when he allowed five singles in seven scoreless innings against the Diamondbacks. Just five days earlier, he'd blanked the Brewers for six innings before allowing a pair of seventh-inning runs. Confidence has always been an issue with this right-hander, who has been hurt by an inability to consistently keep his pitches down in the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis picked up his first win since June 21 in his last start, but he wishes he could have pitched better. The right-hander gave up four runs (three courtesy of a Carlos Lee homer) in 6 1/3 innings against the Astros and was backed by 11 Cubs runs. This will be his first start versus the club that drafted him since June 9, 2007. Marquis hopes for better results than that last outing in Atlanta when he was tagged for six runs in 1 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo won a fourth straight decision despite not having his best stuff against the Diamondbacks on Friday night. The 29-year-old rookie hurler's pinpoint location and ability to change speeds has made it difficult for opponents to plan any sort of attack against him. This will essentially be the first time the Cubs have seen him. He threw one pitch in a relief appearance at Wrigley Field on June 12.
away_pitcher_note: Harden did not get a decision in his last outing Tuesday against Houston. He gave up five runs on eight hits over 5 2/3 innings and admitted to being tired in the sixth. He'll be pitching against the Braves on eight days' rest. One aspect of National League play that he has to get used to is baserunning. In the second, Harden beat out a bunt single, and that may have resulted in the weary legs.

home_pitcher_note: Glavine has overcome the elbow problems that have sidelined him since he was forced to make an early exit from his June 10 start against the Cubs. Mechanically he's felt sound in two Minor League rehab appearances and the elbow discomfort that plagued him in May hasn't been present. The 42-year-old left-hander wants to impress in the season's final two months to at least give himself a chance to pitch again next year.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start against the Cardinals, but he pitched well. The lefty gave up two runs on seven hits and two walks over 7 1/3 innings, and was economical with his pitches, throwing 83. He was pulled in the eighth with a runner on and Albert Pujols coming up. It made sense. This was Lilly's fifth straight quality start, and he's 2-0 in that stretch with a 2.76 ERA. However, he does lead the NL in home runs allowed, and served up No. 26 to Joe Mather.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has struggled with control and his changeup during his past two outings. Entering the season, he'd never thrown more than 140 innings in a single campaign in his professional career and has already completed 144 1/3 innings this year. The Braves will need to show caution with their 22-year-old right-hander, who leads all Major League rookies with 11 wins. Shoddy defense and inconsistent location plagued him on Aug. 4, when he allowed the Giants three earned runs and nine hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Through 6 2/3 innings of his last start, Cain was in control. But one bad throw to Manny Ramirez ruined his afternoon. Pitching with a one-run advantage in the seventh, Cain tossed Ramirez a waist-high fastball with men on the corners, and Ramirez crushed it for a two-run double. The hit ended Cain's streak of three consecutive solid outings, while extending Cain's woeful mark against the rival Dodgers -- he's 0-6 against them in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton is still fighting some of the rust that he developed during his injury-induced three-year absence from the Majors. The 35-year-old southpaw's inconsistencies were apparent in his past two starts. After providing seven strong innings against the Giants on Aug. 5, he struggled with his location and sinker in Sunday's loss to the Diamondbacks. During his outing against the Giants, he allowed two runs and produced 13 groundouts.
away_pitcher_note: Palmer gets the spot start for the Giants after Jonathon Sanchez was scratched due to a left shoulder strain. Palmer is making his Major League debut.

home_pitcher_note: After impressing in his previous two outings, Morton took a step backward while issuing four walks in just 2 1/3 innings against the Cubs on Wednesday. The 24-year-old rookie right-hander has had occasional trouble locating his fastball and doesn't possess the secondary pitches to compensate for this. The Braves are hoping he gives them the confidence that he can fill one of the final rotation spots next year.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum's status for this game was in doubt after he sustained a bruised right knee in his previous outing at Houston. Brad Ausmus led off the fifth inning by smashing a 3-1 pitch off the outside of Lincecum's knee, knocking the 24-year-old All-Star out of the game. To that point, Lincecum had struck out seven batters, displaying his typically electric stuff. He even struck out the side in the fourth inning after scoring from first base on Randy Winn's two-out double in the top of the inning.

home_pitcher_note: Many have wondered when Campillo's bubble might burst, and while allowing a total of nine earned runs in his past two starts, he's provided some indication that time might have arrived. But while allowing the Cubs five runs on Wednesday, the 29-year-old rookie surrendered just five singles and limited them to one run after the first inning.  During his previous six starts, he had gone 4-0 with a 2.31 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Zito sailed through his last start, blanking Houston for five innings on two hits. "He was locked in," manager Bruce Bochy said. Then came the sixth, when an infield hit and a bloop hit helped Houston load the bases. Before Zito left, he walked three batters, hit one and yielded two sacrifice flies. That led to a six-run inning, which precipitated Zito's Major League-leading 15th loss. Zito did not face the Braves last year and is 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA against them in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perez continued to impress with his last outing, a three-run, eight strikeout affair. The left-hander tossed 6 2/3 innings of scoreless baseball before tiring and allowing three Nationals to score, cuing his exit from the game. The New York bullpen held up, though, and Perez got more than enough run support in a 9-3 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes has proven he can be effective at the Triple-A level, having gone 1-1 with a 2.31 ERA in eight starts for Richmond this year. But when the 23-year-old southpaw is brought back up to make this start, he'll have to show the consistent control that he lacked in 15 starts for the Braves earlier this year. In his past six big league appearances (five starts), he went 0-5 with an 8.74 ERA.  Opponents produced a .451 on-base percentage during that span.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets have won 11 of Pelfrey's past 13 starts, and he's won nine of them. Now, he faces the team that beat him twice in his first eight starts. His ERA in 9 1/3 innings against the Braves this season is 10.61. Pelfrey has a 6-5 record at Shea Stadium that belies his 2.81 ERA there. He has allowed three home runs in 83 1/3 innings at home, one by Kelly Johnson. Chipper Jones hit one against him in Atlanta. Brian McCann has a .545 batting average, a .615 on-base percentage and a .909 slugging percentage in 13 career plate appearances against Pelfrey.
away_pitcher_note: Despite losing four of his first six starts since the All-Star break, Jurrjens has produced a 3.57 ERA. He recorded a career-high nine strikeouts and received just one of support in Friday's loss to the Giants. The rookie right-hander says he's not fatigued, despite the fact that he's surpassed his previous career-high innings total. Some of his recent struggles have been the result of an inconsistent changeup. He is 2-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two starts against the Mets this year.

home_pitcher_note: His record over .500 and his ERA lower than 5.00 for the first time this season, Martinez has a chance to accomplish something that has been beyond him since his first two starts last season -- win successive starts. He completed seven innings against the offensively challenged Pirates on Saturday night; that was a 2008 first for him. And he has allowed merely four earned runs in his past three starts (19 1/3 innings). He hasn't faced the Braves since Sept. 27, 2006, when he tore his right rotator cuff while striking out Scott Thorman.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton will be attempting to win consecutive starts for the first time in more than three years. Since ending a three-year injury-induced absence from the mound, the 35-year-old southpaw has progressively gained confidence in his health and pitches. He had his sinker working on Saturday, when he induced 10 ground-ball outs in six innings against the Giants. Hampton is motivated by the fact that he must prove himself before his contract expires at the end of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright will be making his 14th start and first since June 7. He has been on the DL with a right middle finger sprain since June 8. Wainwright has pronounced himself fully ready to face Major League hitters and claims he is snapping off his curveball harder than he was prior to the injury. The jury is still out on whether Wainwright will remain in the starting rotation or go to closer when Chris Carpenter returns. For now, Wainwright is just happy to be on the mound again in any capacity.
away_pitcher_note: In his next start, Morton will be looking to avenge the worst start of his young career. In 3 2/3 innings against the Cardinals on July 28, he allowed eight earned runs and issued four walks. During the four starts that have followed, the 24-year-old rookie right-hander has gone 1-3 with 3.63 ERA. He showed better control while allowing three earned run and issuing two walks in a losing effort against the Giants on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse will be making this start while appealing a five-game suspension handed down by Major League Baseball for throwing a pitch near the head of Cincinnati's Edinson Volquez last Sunday. Offering consistency in a year of pitching turbulence on the Cardinals' injury-riddled staff, Lohse has proven to be an astute free agent pickup. He has delivered a staff-high 162 innings and his 13 wins leave him tied for fifth place in the National League in that category.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo has struggled in the first inning of his last two starts, giving up four runs to the Cubs and three to the Giants. He needed 37 pitches to get out of the first against San Francisco before settling down and pitching well. Campillo retired 14 straight batters until Aaron Rowand hit his 12th home run leading off the sixth inning. Campillo has surrendered 15 earned runs in his past 18 innings. Prior to that, he had allowed no more than three runs in six consecutive starts.

home_pitcher_note: Looper pitched three-hit ball over seven innings in his last start and allowed just one run. But he emerged as a tough-luck loser against Pittsburgh, continuing a recent pattern. Looper has allowed just nine earned runs in his last six starts for a 2.03 ERA. But his record is only 2-3 over that span. The Cardinals have scored only a combined four runs in those three losses.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes worked on the rhythm of his delivery while with Triple-A Richmond earlier this month, and he showed improvement while limiting the Mets to two earned runs in six innings on Tuesday. The 23-year-old southpaw has battled control issues all season, and his three walks against the Mets proved he still has some room for improvement. Before Tuesday, he had gone 0-5 with an 8.74 ERA in his previous six big league appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens couldn't bounce back from first-inning struggles against the Mets on Wednesday. He was tagged for five runs (three earned), and his pitch count inflated to 44 through the opening inning. Jurrjens is 1-4 with a 4.35 ERA in his last five starts, and Wednesday night marked the first time he has not thrown at least six innings since May 31. He have up six hits through five innings, recording three walks and no strikeouts. Jurrjens is 1-1 with a 5.25 ERA in two games against Florida this season.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen's record is a bit deceiving, because he's pitched better than his string of dropping four consecutive decisions. In his last outing, a no-decision at San Francisco, the 24-year-old lefty carried a one-run lead into the sixth inning. But he was tagged for four hits in that inning, and surrendered three runs. Olsen exited after six innings, having allowed four runs on nine hits. The lefty has faced the Braves twice this season. He won on April 15, but wasn't involved in the decision on June 2.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton gave his team a chance to win Thursday night, holding the Mets to three runs in his sixth start of the season. After injuries kept him off the mound for three years, he has grown more comfortable with each start of 2008. Hampton said the velocity on his fastball is returning, and it hit 90 mph several times Thursday. He scattered eight hits, striking out two with one walk to come away with the no-decision. Physically, Hampton said he felt good on the mound, and he is making progress with consistent quality pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson has worked at least six innings in five consecutive starts. But in his last outing, the right-hander was not involved in the decision. Still, he was effective at San Francisco, posting a quality start. Johnson gave up three runs on nine hits with four strikeouts at AT&T Park. Johnson has made eight strong starts since coming off the disabled list and seeing his first action on July 10. He has not yielded more than four runs, and in seven of his starts he didn't give up more than three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Based simply on his stuff, the Braves still have plenty of faith in Morton. But while issuing a career-high five walks and retiring just 10 of the 14 batters he faced against the Cardinals on Friday, the 24-year-old right-hander once again showed his youth. Control has been a constant issue for Morton, who hasn't completed three innings in two of his previous three starts. He started this month by allowing just two earned runs in his first 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez was pretty solid in his last outing, even though he didn't factor into the decision or record a quality start. The 24-year-old yielded four runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings. He added seven strikeouts while walking one in a no-decision at Arizona. What stood out is how Sanchez handled himself and battled head-to-head against Randy Johnson. This will be Sanchez's sixth start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander ended up having one of his worst outings, as the Nationals were defeated by the Cubs, 9-2, at Wrigley Field. Perez lasted 4 1/3 innings and gave up five runs (four earned) on 10 hits. It didn't help that Perez was suffering from a stomach virus before the game. He believes chicken noodle soup did him in.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo seemed to right himself while delivering five solid innings and getting a no-decision against the Cardinals on Saturday.  The 29-year-old rookie, who had allowed five earned runs in each of his previous three starts, allowed three earned runs against the Cardinals and each of those came courtesy of extra-base hits by Albert Pujols. Campillo's collection of offspeed pitches proved baffling to the aggressive Marlins, who saw him allow two hits in seven scoreless innings against them on July 21.

home_pitcher_note: On Sunday, Bergmann had one bad inning and it proved to be costly, as the Nationals lost to the Cubs, 6-1, at Wrigley Field. Early on, it looked like Bergmann would be in for a rough afternoon, as the Cubs scored three runs in the top of the second inning. Bergmann would settle down after that, allowing one run in the next 4 1/3 innings. Bergmann believes he had too much confidence in his fastball. After giving up the three runs, he relied heavily on his breaking stuff.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes has had plenty of bad outings this season, but none may have been worse than the one he produced against the Nationals on July 20. The 23-year-old southpaw allowed six earned runs and seven hits while issuing four walks in just 2 1/3 innings that afternoon. Patience has started to run thin as Reyes has gone 0-6 with a 7.60 ERA in his past eight Major League outings. During this span, he has worked 34 1/3 innings, allowed 47 hits and issued 23 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Balester won his third game of the season last Tuesday, giving up a run in five-plus innings against the Dodgers. He started to lose it, however, in the fifth and sixth innings, hitting batters and surrendering hits. But Marco Estrada bailed out Balester in the sixth and held the Dodgers to just one run. During August, Balester is 2-3 with a 4.28 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has thrown 16 more innings than he had during any of his previous professional seasons, and the fatigue is starting to show. The 22-year-old rookie, who is 1-4 with a 4.84 ERA in his eight starts since the All-Star break, lasted a season-short three innings while allowing a season-high six earned runs against the Marlins on Tuesday. He previous season high was five earned runs, which he surrendered against the Nationals on July 19. His only previous outing at Nationals Park came on April 30, when he allowed one earned run and two hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson continued his dominant comeback from Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery by tossing his first career complete game in a win against the Braves on Wednesday. The 24-year-old gave up just one run on four hits while walking three and striking out eight. In his last two innings, Johnson got into a couple of jams with runners in scoring position and less than two outs, but he was able to get away unscathed. The Marlins are now 7-2 when Johnson toes the rubber.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing three earned runs or less and completing at least six innings in his past three starts, Hampton is starting to quiet many of his doubters. The 35-year-old southpaw completed eight innings and allowed three runs in Wednesday's loss to the Marlins. He has steadily regained confidence and shown durability since returning to the mound on July 26, after spending more than three years battling multiple injuries.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez didn't have his best stuff in a loss to the Braves on Thursday. And it was evident from the get-go. Although he didn't give up a run in the first, the 24-year-old was tossed 29 pitches that inning, which led to a rather short outing. Sanchez pitched just five innings, yielding four runs on five hits while striking out two and walking a season-high five. In his last two starts, the Venezuela native has given up eight runs in 11 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morton provided the finest start of his young career on Thursday, when he limited the Marlins to one baserunner in the first five innings and two runs over six innings.  After allowing 10 of the 14 batters he faced to reach safely on Aug. 22, the 24-year-old rookie right-hander worked on his alignment and proved much more aggressive in the strike zone.  The Braves have raved about his stuff over the past year and as he continues to make mental and mechanical adjustments, he's providing indication that his future is bright.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough first inning that saw him give up the game's first run, Volstad was masterful against the Mets in a no-decision on Friday -- which saw the Marlins lose after a two-out, ninth-inning grand slam by Carlos Beltran. Volstad pitched 6 1/3 innings, giving up just the one run on five hits and three walks before exiting with a 2-1 lead in hand in the seventh inning. After the first inning, Volstad gave up just three hits and threw 78 pitches through 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Since becoming one of the most pleasant surprises the Braves have seen this year, Campillo has struggled. The 29-year-old right-hander has gone 1-3 with a 7.86 ERA in his past five starts. In the six starts that preceded this skid, he was 3-1 with a 1.77 ERA. One of his finest starts of the year came at Dolphin Stadium on July 21, when he limited the Marlins to two hits over seven scoreless innings. His offspeed repertoire could prove maddening to Florida's aggressive lineup.

home_pitcher_note: Parr, 22, will be making his Major League debut in place of Jo-Jo Reyes, who was scratched three hours before game time. Parr spent five seasons in the Minors. He reached Double-A last season, and this year went 8-4 with a 3.69 ERA for Double-A Mississippi before being promoted to Triple-A Richmond, with which he went 5-3 with a 3.23 ERA in 10 games (nine starts).
away_pitcher_note: Martis will make his Major League debut against the Braves. He is a keeper for Washington. So much so that Martis played for the World Team in the XM All-Star Futures Game at Yankee Stadium last July. Martis, 21, entered the contest in the ninth inning, picking up a save as the World Team blanked the U.S. Team, 3-0. Martis got off to a slow start by giving up a ground-rule double, but he retired three of the next four hitters to close out the game.

home_pitcher_note: Although he doesn't claim that he's tired, Jurrjens has been bothered by the inconsistent control that he's experienced since the All-Star break. The 22-year-old rookie was in line to beat the Nationals on Sunday before his bullpen imploded in the eighth inning. But he took some of the blame because it took him 109 pitches to complete six innings. Jurrjens is 1-4 with a 5.36 ERA in his past eight home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Last Saturday against the Braves, it looked like the Nationals were going to have a long night. Bergmann lasted 4 1/3 innings and gave up six runs on eight hits. His worst inning came in the third, when eight batters came to the plate and Atlanta scored four runs. However, the Nationals ended up winning the game, 9-8, in 10 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton reached another milestone, in what has already been a comeback year, during a no-decision against the Marlins on Monday. Five days after going a season-high eight innings, Hampton reached his highest pitch count since April 22, 2005, when he threw 106 pitches. The 35-year-old lefty gave up three runs on six hits in six innings while walking three and striking out two.
away_pitcher_note: Last Monday against the Phillies, Redding had a no-hitter after five innings. But one had a feeling Redding wouldn't last much longer in the game, for he had a high pitch count, walked two batters and hit two others. Redding acknowledged that he didn't have his best stuff. Manager Manny Acta noticed that Redding didn't have good command of his fastball, which is why his pitch count (106) was so high. Redding ended up pitching 5 2/3 innings and gave up three runs on two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes has shown little improvement as this season has progressed and his manager, Bobby Cox, showed little patience when he removed him from a game on Aug. 30 with runners at first and second and owning a four-run, fifth-inning lead against the Nationals. But at the same time, it took the 23-year-old southpaw 94 pitches to complete four innings. In two starts against the Nationals this year, he has totaled 6 1/3 innings and allowed 10 earned runs on 15 hits.
away_pitcher_note: Balester said recently that he wanted to go deep into the games. He did just that on Aug. 31 against the Braves, but he was credited with a no-decision. It was as if Balester pitched two games on Sunday. In the first four innings, Balester had a tough time with his location and he paid for it by giving up four runs. In fact, the biggest hit for the Braves came in the fourth. After Martin Prado walked and Omar Infante singled, Yunel Escobar hit a 1-0 pitch for a three-run homer over the left-field wall to give Atlanta a 4-2 lead. But Balester settled down after that, retiring eight consecutive batters and pitching a total of seven innings. It was first time Balester was able to pitch that many innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: While going 1-3 with a 7.39 ERA in his past six starts, Campillo has shown signs that he's tiring. The 29-year-old rookie right-hander had gone 3-1 with a 1.77 ERA in his last six starts. Knowing that he isn't a power pitcher, opponents have shown greater patience against Campillo's offspeed repertoire. This will be his first start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Cook had one of his worst outings of the season in his last start against the Giants. The right-hander gave up six runs on 10 hits in just three innings. It was the shortest outing of the season for Cook, who had trouble keeping his sinker down in the strike zone. Cook had been battling fatigue and lower back stiffness in recent weeks, but he said he felt fine and that the poor start was due to bad execution.

home_pitcher_note: Parr enjoyed a successful Major League debut while tossing six scoreless innings against the Nationals on Thursday night. The 22-year-old right-hander, who doesn't possess overpowering stuff, was labeled as being "sneaky quick" by Braves manager Bobby Cox. Primarily a fastball pitcher, he has the ability to keep his pitches out of harm's way. While combining for 13 wins in the Minors this season, he surrendered just 13 homers.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez is 1-3 with a 10.13 ERA since joining the Rockies, but positives have arisen from his last two starts -- a loss and a no-decision against the Giants. He pitched into the seventh inning in the loss and the sixth inning in the other game, won by the Rockies. Hernandez was able to change speeds effectively and stay out of the middle of the plate in both games. The only problem is when he loses his effectiveness -- it goes quickly and manager Clint Hurdle has to be alert and have relief help ready.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has exceeded his innings total from any previous professional season by more than 30 frames, and he's starting to show some fatigue as he nears the end of his rookie season. Despite enduring early control problems on Friday against the Nationals, the right-hander allowed one run in five innings and won for the first time in five starts. An extra day of rest may prove beneficial as Jurrjens attempts to claim his second win of the season against the Rockies. He scattered eight hits in 7 2/3 scoreless innings at Coors Field on June 16.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Jimenez rebounded nicely against the Astros after giving up six runs to the Padres. Against Houston, the right-hander relied less on his breaking pitches and focused exclusively on pounding the strike zone with his fastball. The results were encouraging: He surrendered just three runs on five hits in six innings, and the Rockies won. Jimenez is 1-1 with a 4.09 ERA in two starts against the Braves this season.

home_pitcher_note: Santana stopped the bleeding for the Mets Sunday, holding the Phillies to two runs in 7 1/3 innings following his club's two straight losses to its division rival. He allowed five hits -- one a home run -- striking out six and walking three. Most importantly, the 29-year-old once again extended his arm past 100 pitches, a workload he has surpassed in nine out of his last 10 starts, throwing 71 of his 116 pitches for strikes. While Santana has fared well against the Braves in most statistical categories, holding this National League East opponent to four earned runs in 14 innings, both starts have resulted in tough-luck losses and only four Braves have been struck out by Santana in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton surrendered a career-high four homers while getting a no-decision with a seven-inning effort against the Nationals on Saturday. The sinkerball specialist has been frustrated by the number of pitches he's been leaving up in the zone recently. While he's still showing some rust, the lefty has also steadily proven that he can still be effective at the Major League level. With injury questions still looming, Hampton needs to pitch well over the final weeks to increase the interest he'll gain on the free-agent market this winter.

home_pitcher_note: Niese got knocked around by the Brewers in his Major League debut on Sept. 3, allowing seven hits, four walks and five runs over three-plus innings. Niese said anxiety undermined him in the first inning. He surrendered a home run to Rickie Weeks on his second big league pitch and walked the next two batters. Nine of his first 13 pitches were balls.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday afternoon, Reyes was in line to earn his first win since June 13 before his bullpen imploded. Still, while limiting the Nationals to one run in six innings, the 23-year-old southpaw provided some reason for optimism. Reyes, who is 0-6 with a 6.90 ERA over his past 10 appearances (nine starts), limited the Mets to two earned runs and four hits in six innings while getting a no-decision at Shea Stadium on Aug. 19.

home_pitcher_note: Perez was roughed up early Tuesday night, giving up seven runs on eight hits in only 3 1/3 innings against the Nationals. It marked his shortest outing since June 2 and just the second time in his last 15 starts that he has not pitched at least six full innings. He struck out three, recording two walks. Until Tuesday, Perez had been consistent for the Mets lately, and he has not recorded a loss since Aug. 3. While his arm strength was there Tuesday, his command and location were not. In his only start against Atlanta this season, Perez held the Braves to three runs on seven hits through 6 1/3 innings to come away with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo was denied the opportunity to win for the first time in five starts on Tuesday, when the bullpen couldn't hold a ninth-inning lead. Still even while surrendering a pair of homers to the Rockies, the 29-year-old rookie right-hander looked better than he had since his last win on Aug. 8. Because he was facing a new opponent, he was able to utilize his offspeed repertoire effectively. Campillo's first start of the season came on May 20, when he limited the Mets to three hits over six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Other than the fact that his bullpen denied him a second win on Wednesday, Parr's career has started as impressively as he could have ever wished. The 22-year-old right-hander has tossed six scoreless innings during each  of his first two Major League starts. Without an overpowering fastball, Parr has found early success with his slider and changeup. Dating back to his final three starts with Triple-A Richmond this year, he's allowed one earned run in his past 29 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on three days' rest, the rock-steady Moyer struck out five and walked one in beating the Brewers on Thursday. Moyer has been the Phils' most consistent starting pitcher this season, holding opponents to three runs or fewer in 17 out of his past 18 starts. His 14 wins lead the team. He earned a no-decision in his only start this season against the Braves, holding Atlanta to two runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens showed some of his top velocity while recording a career-high 10 strikeouts and winning his second straight start on Thursday against the Rockies.  Per John Smoltz's advice, the 22-year-old right-hander has limited his running exercises between starts and consequently he says he's regained some of the leg strength he lacked while winning just one of his previous seven starts entering this month.  One of his finest starts of the season came against the Phillies on July 25, when he allowed three hits over eight scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: With Kyle Kendrick struggling mightily the past few weeks, there was an opening for Happ in the Phillies' rotation. Happ was chosen because of the Braves' unfamiliarity with him, and also because of the presence of several prominent left-handed hitters in their lineup. Happ has not started a game for the Phillies since July 9, but has performed well in that role. He has a 5.71 ERA overall, but has compiled a 3.27 mark in two starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton allowed two runs over six innings Saturday, but against Johan Santana, that effort was not enough to earn the 36-year-old a decision. The Braves would wait to claim victory after Hampton exited with 90 pitches (47 strikes). A lack of consistent location --  totaling five walks and six hits allowed -- put Hampton into a couple of bases-loaded jams, but he recovered for the most part, inducing double play groundouts in both situations.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels beat the Brewers Saturday, holding Milwaukee to two runs in 6 1/3 innings, striking out four and walking three. The 24-year-old, now in his third Major League season, is setting a career high in innings pitched with each successive start. Right now he's at 214 1/3. But the left-hander has been steady, recording a 4-1 record with a 2.21 ERA in his last six starts. In three starts this year against the Braves, Hamels is 2-0 with a 2.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes was yanked quickly in Saturday's outing against the Mets, surrendering four earned runs on two home runs in just two innings. The 23-year-old was pinch-hit for in his first chance for an at-bat, making his 37-pitch workload (23 strikes) light yet dubious. He had only one strikeout to offset a two-run home run in the first inning and a solo shot in the second frame. Reyes has lost seven straight decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Partly because it stood in such contrast to his previous start, Perez's outing on Sunday against the Braves proved to be rather encouraging. Perez lasted seven innings, allowing four hits and two runs. He struck out eight batters and walked three. And he did it with the Mets needing a win to maintain an increasing pace in the National League East. Perez's next start will also come against the Braves, whom he has now beaten five times in seven starts over the past two seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo was roughed up early in his fourth consecutive losing decision, allowing four runs -- three earned -- in 3 2/3 innings to the Mets on Sunday. All three earned runs were scored via home runs, the first a solo shot by David Wright in the first inning and the second a two-run homer by Wright in the third. Despite the short outing, Campillo still threw 87 pitches. He'll get another shot at the Mets, who have bested him two out of three times this season.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez has lost three of his last five decisions, and the Mets have lost six of his nine most recent starts. He allowed four runs in six innings against the Nationals on Monday. Armed once again with his cutter -- he hadn't thrown it in his preceding five starts because of a blister on the middle finger of his right hand -- Martinez wasn't sharp. He had gone seven days without pitching, his 18th start pushed back two days because of the rainout Friday. The location of his pitchers was imprecise, especially early. Martinez has faced the Braves once this season. He pitched seven innings in what became a 5-4 Mets victory at Shea Stadium Aug. 21. He allowed four runs in the non-decision, one on a leadoff home run by Yunel Escobar.

home_pitcher_note: Despite allowing four earned runs and 10 hits in 4 1/3 innings against the Phillies on Tuesday, James Parr still drew some postgame praise from manager Bobby Cox, who has been impressed by the rookie hurler's makeup and ability to mix his pitches. The 22-year-old right-hander had tossed six scoreless innings in both of his two previous career starts this month. While enjoying a successful August with Triple-A Richmond and finding some early success at the Major League level, Parr has at least made himself a candidate for Atlanta's 2009 starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: A double that might have been caught and a four-pitch walk that followed an extended interruption in play were Pelfrey's undoing Tuesday night against the Nationals. Cristian Guzman followed the walk with a booming double to drive in the run in a 1-0 loss. Pelfrey wasn't sharp -- seven hits and four walks in seven innings, but aside from Guzman's hit, he limited the damage. Now he faces the team that has knocked him around a few times this season. He has a 1-2 record and 6.87 ERA in three starts against the Braves. But the losses occurred in April, and he pitched a three-hitter, the first complete game of his career, against them Aug. 20 at Shea Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Happ will make his second start against Atlanta in five days. The rookie lefty dazzled them with six shutout innings on Wednesday, allowing just three hits, and has a 2.12 ERA in his three starts this season. Manager Charlie Manuel would love an encore.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens surrendered four runs during a 43-pitch first-inning against the Phillies on Wednesday and then held them scoreless while needing just 57 pitches to complete his final four innings. The early damage prevented the 22-year-old rookie from winning his third straight start and equal the success he had at Citizens Bank Park on July 25, when allowed three hits in eight scoreless innings against the Phillies. Facing the same lineup for the second time in five days, Jurrjens will look to be more aggressive in the strike zone and fight the temptation of showing too much respect to specific hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has been the team's most consistant pitcher and has posted a 2.73 ERA in his previous 10 starts. Already into uncharted territory as far as innings, Hamels isn't going to stop now until he gets the Phillies into the postseason. This could be his final start of the regular season, unless the Phillies don't have a spot clinched by Sept. 28.
away_pitcher_note: Two unearned runs and Pat Burrell's sixth-inning two-run homer prevented Hampton from beating the Phillies on Thursday night in Atlanta. This will be Hampton's third start of the season against the Phillies and likely his final opportunity to audition for a contract next season. While pitching into the seventh inning in each of his past seven starts, the injury-prone 35-year-old lefty has at least erased some of the durability issues that have surrounded him.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is coming off the worst start of his career, an outing in which he allowed 10 earned runs in four-plus innings. He had posted an 1.80 ERA in 11 starts prior to that, indicating that the poor start was a bump in the road, and not a severe regression to his first half, when he posted a 5.84 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Reyes' final opportunity to make the positive impression that he's been unable to provide while going 0-7 with a 7.79 ERA in his past 12 appearances. The 23-year-old hurler agitated Braves manager Bobby Cox while allowing the Mets five earned runs in just 3 1/3 innings on Friday. It marked the seventh time in 11 starts that he didn't complete at least five innings.  He is 0-2 with a 7.56 ERA in three appearances (two starts) against the Phillies this year.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler lasted only one inning in his last start against the Pirates, allowing five runs before being lifted in the second inning for a pinch-hitter. Moehler made one start against the Braves in Atlanta earlier this year, allowing five runs over six innings in a losing effort.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo will be making the final start of what has been a memorable rookie season. The 29-year-old right-hander, who didn't join the Braves' rotation until May 20, will be displaying his offspeed repertoire against the Astros for the first time this season. Campillo limited the Mets to two runs in six innings on Saturday to win for the first time in eight starts. He was 0-3 with a 6.88 ERA in his previous seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros haven't announced their starter for this one, but Backe is a likely candidate considering he hasn't pitched since giving up five runs in 1 2/3 innings at Florida on Sept. 17. Over his last two starts, both on the road, Backe has allowed eight earned runs in six innings. But the right-hander has always pitched better at home than on the road, and in his last start at Minute Maid Park he held the Reds to two earned runs in 6 2/3 innings back on Aug. 28. Backe is 2-1 with a 5.59 ERA in five career appearances vs. Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Parr is coming off the worst start of his young career, having lasted just 1 2/3 innings against the Mets on Sunday. The 22-year-old right-hander began his Major League career by tossing six scoreless innings in consecutive starts earlier this month. But in his past two outings, he has totaled six innings, allowed 14 hits and been charged with eight earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is the projected starter here, though the club hasn't officially made a decision. Rodriguez, in his first start since leaving his Sept. 7 start at Colorado due to a strained oblique muscle, allowed just two unearned runs in five innings against Cincinnati on Tuesday. He's faced Atlanta once this season, a no-decision (5 1/3 innings, 3 ER) back on July 6.
away_pitcher_note: Instead of pushing rookie right-hander Jair Jurrjens any further, the Braves have decided to start Mike Hampton in their season finale. Hampton, who has gone 2-2 with a 3.63 ERA in his past eight starts, looks forward to the opportunity to make another good impression before heading into free agency. The 36-year-old southpaw relocated his cutter on Tuesday night, while limiting the Phillies to two run in six innings of a victorious effort.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is starting Opening Night because left-hander Cole Hamels missed some time last month because of inflammation in his left elbow. But Myers has been here before. He has been the Phillies' Opening Day starter each of the previous two seasons. He seems determined to make this a good one. He showed up to Spring Training 25 pounds lighter than he finished last season. He wants to make up for his first-half struggles last season, when the Phillies optioned him to the Minor Leagues.
away_pitcher_note:
Lowe will look to prolong his success at Citizens Bank Park and end the struggles he's experienced during previous Opening Day starts. In the three season openers that he started for the Dodgers, the veteran sinkerballer went 0-3 with an 8.44 ERA.
