His finest Opening Day outing came in 2005, when he allowed two runs in seven innings against the Giants. While starting the next two openers against the Braves and Brewers, he totaled nine innings, surrendered 17 hits and allowed 13 earned runs.

Looking to halt his Opening Day misfortunes, the 36-year-old hurler said it will be important for him to reign his emotions while pitching on a night when Phillies fans will be getting their first look at their team as defending World Series champions.

This will be Lowe's third consecutive start against the Phillies. He went 0-1 with a 3.48 ERA in two starts against them during last year's National League Championship Series. The loss came in Game 1, when he kept the eventual world champions scoreless through five innings and then surrendered sixth-inning homers to Chase Utley and Ryan Howard.

Lowe, who signed a four-year, $60 million contract in January, went 6-1 with a 1.27 ERA in his final 10 starts last year. During this span, which began with an Aug. 11 win in Philadelphia, he limited opponents to a .195 batting average. Lowe has gone 4-0 with a 2.58 ERA during his past six regular season starts against the Phillies. He is 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in three career starts at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer turned 46 in November, but he keeps on going. He threw 196 1/3 innings last season, which he capped by picking up the win when the Phillies clinched their second consecutive National League East championship. He became the fourth pitcher in the modern era to win 10 games in a season he started as a 45-year-old. The others were Phil Niekro (1984-86), Satchel Paige (1952) and Jack Quinn (1929).
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a strong rookie season, Jurrjens will attempt to prove that his advanced cerebral approach to pitching will help him make the adjustments that will help him avoid a sophomore slump. The 22-year-old right-hander ranked fourth in the National League with .53 homers allowed per nine innings. This provides better reason to understand why he allowed just two earned runs in 15 2/3 innings he pitched at Citzens Bank Park. While not enjoying equal success during matchups at Turner Field, he went 1-2 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies picked up Blanton before the July 31 non-waiver Trade Deadline after they couldn't land left-hander CC Sabathia. But it worked out very well for the Phillies. They were 9-4 in his starts, and he won two games in the postseason: Game 4 against the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Division Series and Game 4 of the World Series, when he memorably hit a home run. Blanton is more comfortable in his new environment, and the Phillies are expecting big things from him this season.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez won't be starting his Braves career in an optimal environment. The flyball pitcher, who has surrendered at least 25 homers each of the past seven seasons, has gone 0-2 with a 9.90 ERA in his two career starts at Citizens Bank Park. Most of the damage incurred at CBP came when he allowed eight earned runs during a 2005 start. During a 2007 start there, three of the four hits he surrendered in six innings were solo homers. This will be his 24th career start against the Phillies but just the third since the end of the 2003 season.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his Opening Day start in Philadelphia, Lowe will have the honor to also start the home opener against the Nationals. He is 5-1 with a 2.41 ERA in six career starts against the Nationals and he went 1-1 with a 1.12 ERA in two starts against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: Martis beat out right-hander Jordan Zimmermann for the fourth spot in the rotation. Martis said he probably would have been in the Minor Leagues had he decided to play in the World Baseball Classic. Before he arrived in camp, Martis chose not to play for The Netherlands, because he felt he had a 50-50 chance to be the Nationals' fifth starter.

home_pitcher_note: Kawamaki spent the past 13 seasons as one of the top pitchers in Japan's Central League.  The 33-year-old right-hander captured the Sawamura Award  --  equivalent to the Cy Young Award --- and was named the Central League's MVP in 2004, when he went 17-7 with a 3.32 ERA. Over the past five seasons, he went  66-35 with a 3.12 ERA.  Known for his consistent control, he possesses an average fastball that is complimented by a slow curve that proved effective during the exhibition season.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan will face the Braves for the fourth time in his career. He is 2-1 with a 3.71 ERA against them. His best start against Atlanta occurred on April 22, 2008. Braves right-hander John Smoltz became the 16th pitcher to reach career strikeout No. 3,000, but the Nationals ended up winning the game, 6-0, thanks to a superb performance by Lannan. He pitched seven innings and gave up five hits. It was hard to figure out who was the veteran and who was the rookie on the mound. The only time the Braves had runners in scoring position against Lannan was in the second and fourth innings, but they all came with two outs.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens battled some early control problems and pitched around multiple jams while beginning his season with 5 2/3 scoreless innings against the Phillies on Tuesday night.   The 23-year-old right-hander once again showed his advanced maturity while making some necessary adjustments after totaling 46 pitches through the first two innings. He was 1-1 with a 3.70 ERA in four starts against the Nationals last year. His most recent start against them was on Sept. 5, when he allowed one run and six hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Olsen lasted only three innings and gave up all eight runs against the Marlins. In the first inning, Jorge Cantu gave Florida the lead with a two-run home run. An inning later, Emilio Bonifacio singled to left to drive in Ronny Paulino. In the third inning, the Marlins batted around and scored five runs. Dan Uggla highlighted the scoring with a two-run homer. More alarming was that Olsen had problems getting Marlins pitcher Josh Johnson out at the plate. Johnson went 1-for-1 with an RBI and a walk. Olsen also had troubles with Johnson on March 19 at Space Coast Stadium, where Johnson went 1-for-1 with two runs scored. Olsen is facing the Braves for the 12th time in his career. He is 2-4 with a 6.71 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Javier Vazquez limited the Phillies to three runs in six innings during a successful season debut that was ruined when his bullpen squandered a seven-run, seventh-inning lead on Wednesday.  The veteran right-hander enjoyed a stellar March that was highlighted on March 14, when he limited Team USA to one run in five innings of a World Baseball Classic game. Vazquez, who was obtained in a December trade with the White Sox, has gone 5-4 with a 3.45 ERA in 11 starts at Turner Field.  He hasn't faced the Marlins since 2005.
away_pitcher_note: During the series finale against the Nationals on Wednesday, Volstad's only troubles came in the first inning. That's when the 22-year-old right-hander gave up two runs -- one earned -- while throwing 27 pitches and getting behind five of the seven batters he faced. The rest of the way, however, Volstad looked as dominant as he did in the second half of last season. The Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., native went on to throw four no-hit frames thereafter while striking out seven batters -- a career-high -- and throwing 65 pitches. Volstad grew up a big Braves fan, and last season he went 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe opened the season by limiting the Phillies to two baserunners in eight innings. While not as dominant, he still proved to be impressive when he recorded six strikeouts and allowed the Nationals just one run in a three-inning effort that was halted because of a lengthy rain delay on Friday. He is 4-3 with a 4.59 ERA in eight career starts against the Marlins.  During his only outing against them last year, he allowed six runs -- three earned -- and eight hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming into his fourth season in the Major Leagues, Miller, the Marlins' No. 5 starter, will be making his first start of the year against the Braves. Last season, the 6-foot-7 23-year-old went 6-10 with a 5.87 ERA in 29 games -- 20 starts. Miller started the season in Florida's rotation, going 5-9 with a 5.63 ERA before landing on the 15-day disabled list with patella tendinitis in his right knee on July 18. After posting a 2.33 ERA in six rehab games, he was reinstated from his DL stint in September and finished off the season in the bullpen, giving up seven runs in 6 2/3 innings. The Gainesville, Fla., native is 2-0 with a miniscule 0.69 ERA in four career games against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami pitched around some early jitters and won his first Major League start while recording eight strikeouts and limiting the Nationals to three runs in six innings on Saturday night. Armed with an average fastball, the 33-year-old right-hander relies heavily on a slow curveball that proved to be effective during his successful 13-year career in Japan's Central League.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first start of the season, Sanchez was solid against the Mets on Friday, pitching five scoreless innings against a team he hadn't faced since 2007. The 25-year-old, who gave up four hits and three walks while striking out five, pitched out of trouble in his last two innings of work. In the fourth, he started with runners on first and second but got three straight outs. Then, in the fifth, Sanchez struck out Carlos Delgado with two men on base to end the inning and preserve a two-run lead. In his previous three years in the big leagues, Sanchez is 1-2 with a 5.09 ERA in four starts against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm delivered his second consecutive strong outing on Saturday afternoon, limiting the Reds to just one run on three hits in seven innings. He walked two and struck out three in a 101-pitch effort. Maholm retired the first 11 batters he faced and did not allow a hit until Brandon Phillips' single with two outs in the fourth. The Pirates left-hander was coming off his solid outing on Opening Day when he allowed just one earned run, one intentional walk and seven hits in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While winning his first two starts, Jurrjens has successfully utilized a bend-but-don't-break approach. Despite issuing eight walks and allowing opponents to compile a .347 on-base percentage in his first 11 innings, the 23-year-old right-hander has allowed just three earned runs. During his five-walk outing against the Nationals on Sunday, he said his control problems were a result of attempting to be too fine with his pitches. He was 1-1 with a 4.35 ERA in two starts against the Pirates last year.

home_pitcher_note: Finally at full strength, Snell allowed just two runs on five hits in six innings in a 2-0 loss at Cincinnati on Sunday. However, he was outdueled by the Reds' Aaron Harang who fired a complete-game, three-hit shutout. Snell's four-inning outing against the Cardinals the previous Tuesday was not the way he had planned to start the season, by any means. That start came after Snell missed his final Spring Training tuneup while dealing with a stomach flu, though he insisted that the lengthy layoff was not a contributing factor to the struggles.
away_pitcher_note: With Tom Glavine's shoulder ailing, Jo-Jo Reyes will be promoted from Triple-A Gwinnett to make his season debut. After going 0-7 with a 7.81 ERA in his final 13 appearances (12 starts) for Atlanta last year, Reyes refined his mechanics during the offseason and proved to be more aggressive in the strike zone during Spring Training.  The 24-year-old southpaw allowed five runs -- four earned -- and seven hits in six innings against Charlotte on April 10.

home_pitcher_note: Duke has been stellar in his two starts this season, the latter of which was a complete-game shutout. In 15 1/3 total innings, he's allowed just one earned run. He's throwing to both sides of the plate with ease and using his sinker and two-seam fastball especially efficiently. There is also a confidence seen in the left-hander as he continues to be able to throw the ball where he wants to, when he wants to. Duke is 2-2 with a 2.76 ERA in five previous starts against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez has encountered his share of early-season misfortune. The Braves squandered a seven-run, seventh-inning lead in his first start and produced just one run while he notched 12 strikeouts during Tuesday night's loss to the Marlins. The 33-year-old right-hander enjoyed a strong March that included an impressive showing for Puerto Rico in the World Baseball Classic. He has allowed 10 earned runs and totaled 12 innings in his past two starts against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann will be called up from Triple-A Syracuse to make his Major League debut. Selected by the Nationals out of the University of Wisconsin - Stevens Point in the second round of the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, Zimmerman went 10-3 in the Minors last year with a 2.89 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe struggled with his control while throwing 106 pitches and matching a career-high five walks in a five-inning effort against the Marlins on Tuesday night. His April 10 start against the Nationals was limited to three innings because of a lengthy rain delay. In his two starts against the Nationals last year, he worked 16 innings, surrendered seven hits and allowed just two earned runs. The 36-year-old sinkerballer began this season by allowing two hits in eight scoreless innings against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Martis pitched 6 1/3 innings and allowed two runs on five hits against the Phillies on Thursday. Of the 26 batters he faced, Martis threw 19 first-pitch strikes. Even more impressive, Martis held Jimmy Rollins, Chase Utley and Ryan Howard to a combined 1-for-6. Martis is a guy who is often overshadowed. It was believed that right-hander Jordan Zimmermann would be the fourth starter in the rotation, and Martis would start the season as the fifth starter and pitch in the Minor Leagues because of the off-days on April 9 and 14. But Martis outpitched Zimmermann in Spring Training, and now has helped the Nationals get the first victory of the season.
away_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see what kind of adjustments the Nationals make while getting their second look at Kawakami.  While winning his Major League debut against the Nationals on April 10, the 33-year-old Japanese right-hander allowed three earned runs and four hits in six innings. With an average fastball that occasionally sits up in the zone, he has already surrendered a pair of three-run homers in his young big league career. But with an effective slow curveball, he has also notched 15 strikeouts in 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan had his best outing of the young season last Friday. In his previous two outings, Lannan had allowed 10 runs in nine innings. He wasn't aggressive and was often behind in the count, but this time, Lannan lasted 6 1/3 innings and gave up just one run on three hits against the Marlins. The southpaw trusted his fastball, and he was able to get it on the inside part of the plate a lot more often. Lannan cruised through the first three innings, but he had problems in the fourth inning after allowing a solo homer to Marlins catcher John Baker. He loaded the bags following Baker's blast, but he got out of the jam without allowing another run.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling with his control while winning his first two starts of the season, Jurrjens produced one of the strongest starts of his young career and suffered his first loss on Friday night at PNC Park. The 23-year-old right-hander limited the Pirates to one run and four hits in 6 2/3 innings. The two walks he issued were drawn by the final two batters he faced at the end of his career-high 120-pitch effort. Jurrjens allowed three earned runs while issuing five walks in an April 12 start against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez was better than in his first two outings on Sunday vs. the Astros when he pitched six innings and gave up one run, three hits and five walks with seven strikeouts. He threw 104 pitches and still has some work to do at economizing his pitches. However, the right-hander had better command of his fastball, which reached 97-98 mph. His changeup was also very effective. In two previous starts vs. the Braves, Volquez is 0-1 with a 2.25 ERA. Over 12 innings, he walked five and struck out 16.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez notched his first win of the season while notching eight strikeouts in six scoreless innings against the Pirates on Sunday. He has proven effective with six strong innings during each of his first three starts, but he wants to prove more efficient to cut down on his early pitch count. As a flyball pitcher, he's seemingly prone to encounter problems at Cincinnati's Great American Ball Park. But in his only start there on Aug. 20, 2005, he allowed just one run in eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: With a 4-3 victory on Monday at Houston, Arroyo became the first Reds starter to get off to a 3-0 start since Mike Remlinger in 1997. Arroyo worked seven innings and allowed three earned runs on nine hits, walking none and striking out six. With his sinker working well, the right-hander induced 10 ground-ball outs and two double plays. Using only 81 pitches, Arroyo indicated to manager Dusty Baker that he was spent.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing three earned runs and seven hits in six innings against the Nationals on Monday, Lowe suffered his first loss in nine starts. The 36-year-old right-hander is 7-2 with a 1.78 ERA in his past 14 starts, dating back to Aug. 11. He is 3-1 with a 2.86 ERA in four career starts against the Reds. In his lone start at Great American Ball Park last year, he tossed 5 1/3 innings, allowing one run and three hits.

home_pitcher_note: During a 7-2 loss to the Cubs on Tuesday, Owings worked 4 2/3 innings, with two of his five runs earned on five hits. He walked four and struck out three. After a slow start, he started cruising through the third and fourth innings but hit a wall in the fifth. Back-to-back one-out walks were followed by an error and led to three runs that chased him from the mound. In two career starts vs. Atlanta, Owings is 2-0 with a 3.46 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Since winning his Major League debut on April 11, Kawakami has gone winless in the two starts that have followed. The 33-year-old right-hander has been able to keep opponents off balance with a a slow curve that has helped him notch 17 strikeouts in 17 innings.  He has surrendered one homer during each of his first three starts, and his 10 walks further indicate he isn't showing the same kind of control that was present during his days in Japan.

home_pitcher_note: Since issuing five walks during his April 12 start, Jurrjens has been a man on a mission.  Some of his teammates said the finest start of his career occurred on April 17, when he limited the Pirates to one run in 6 2/3 innings and suffered his only loss of the season.  But the 23-year-old right-hander fared even better on Wednesday, when he tossed  7 2/3 scoreless innings against the Nationals and got a no-decision. While he won his first two starts, he has proven much more efficient during his past two outings.
away_pitcher_note: A couple of patterns don't seem to favor Pineiro, but don't write him off. In the early going, he's alternated quality, with an excellent start followed by an iffy one followed by an excellent one. Moreover, he's been much better at home than on the road since he became a Cardinal. Still, he looks like something of a different pitcher this year, pitching aggressively with a two-seam fastball. He'll be looking to make it four wins in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: While enduring a four-run sixth inning on April 18 in Pittsburgh, Reyes ruined what was an otherwise impressive season debut. His season debut for Triple-A Gwinnett was also soured by a three-run sixth inning.  The 23-year-old southpaw is 0-8 with a 7.82 ERA during his past 14  big league appearances (13 starts).  This year he has committed himself to pitching to contact and avoiding the temptation to overpower opponents with his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse's last two starts haven't been as good as his first two, and it's fair to whether he's showing any ill effects from working hard in his first two games. The bigger question, though, is his right knee, which he turned in his last inning on Thursday. The Cardinals will watch him closely and make sure he's able to go before they send him to the mound on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Since encountering bad luck during his first two starts, Vazquez has won his past two outings and kept himself among the Major League strikeout leaders.  The 32-year-old right-hander has allowed just one earned run over his past 12 innings. Since issuing an uncharacteristically high four walks during his season debut, he's gone 18 innings during which he's recorded 29 strikeouts and issued just three walks. Vazquez hasn't faced the Cardinals since 2006.
away_pitcher_note: It took four starts, but Wainwright really looked like himself in his last outing. He located his pitches, got ahead in counts, got swings and misses, and made it through the seventh inning. It's exactly the sort of thing one expects to see from right-hander, and there's no reason to think he won't be able to offer more of the same on Wednesday. Pitching against the Braves, the team that drafted him, has tended to bring out the best in Wainwright. He has a 1.12 ERA in 24 Major League innings against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe limited the Reds to two runs over seven innings on Saturday to notch his first win in a span of four starts.  The 36-year-old sinkerballer was pleased with the fact that he showed better efficiency than he had in his previous two outings, during which he threw more than 100 pitches and didn't pitch more than six innings. He is 2-3 with a 3.15 ERA in seven career starts against the Astros.  In his lone start against them last year, he allowed six earned runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton yielded four runs over six innings in his last start versus the Brewers, taking a no-decision for the second game in a row. Hampton, a former Brave, will face his old team for the 21st time in his career. He's 4-9 versus Atlanta, with a 4.22 ERA. He's 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA over two starts on the road this year, having allowed three runs over 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has gone 0-2 while posting a 1.32 ERA in his past three starts. The Braves have scored a total of three runs during those starts and just one of those came while he was still the pitcher of record. The 23-year-old right-hander has been much more efficient than he was while winning his first two starts of the year with a 3:8 strikeout-to-walk ratio. The only two walks he issued during Monday night's loss to the Cardinals came during the second inning, setting the stage for him to allow a costly two-out single to Rick Ankiel. In his past 20 1/3 innings, Jurrjens has allowed three earned runs and issued six walks.
away_pitcher_note: After a less-than-stellar start to the season, Oswalt has begun to settle down. On April 17, he pitched six shutout innings and had no decision against the Reds, and last Monday, facing Cincinnati again, he threw seven innings and allowed six hits and one run. It's unfortunate for him he can't face the Reds every game. Although he's 0-2 through his first five starts this year, one shouldn't forget that he began last season 0-3 with a 9.00 ERA. He finished the year 17-10 with a 3.54 ERA. It looks like Oswalt is starting to get back into that groove.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes has gone 14 consecutive starts without a win.  But while limiting the Cardinals to one run in seven innings on Tuesday, the 23-year-old southpaw gave reason to believe that he has started to understand what it will take to be successful at the Major League level.  Braves manager Bobby Cox said Reyes' latest outing was the finest of his young career and further proof that the young hurler has ended his days of attempting to be a flamethrower.   In 12 2/3 innings this year, he has registered just two unintentional walks and recorded 22 ground-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: Wandy Rodriguez continues to show why his early-season success is no fluke. Against the Reds in his last start, Rodriguez was dominant, allowing five hits and a run while striking out five in seven innings. He's among the league leaders in ERA, and in his past three starts, he's held opponents to a .176 batting average while recording a 0.90 ERA. He's registered quality starts in all five of his outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez impressed through most of his season-high, eight-inning outing against the Cardinals on Wednesday. But a four-run fifth inning, during which he surrendered six singles, was enough to hand him his first loss in three starts. While notching eight strikeouts, he proved to be much more efficient than he'd been in his previous four starts, during which he needed at least 98 pitches to complete six innings. This will be his first start against the Mets since 2005. In his previous three outings against them, he's 1-1 with a 2.37 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maine did his best work since last season in his most recent start, last Monday against the Marlins. He completed the sixth inning for the first time in eight starts, dating to last season, and allowed one hit and an unearned run. The rainout Sunday in Philadelphia changed his next assignment from a team that hasn't beaten him in nine starts to the Braves, against whom he has forged a 2-3 record and 5.17 ERA in four career starts. His three starts at Turner Field have produced a 1-2 record and a 5.40 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami has had trouble consistently keeping his pitches down in the zone and has surrendered at least one homer during each of his first four career starts. The 33-year-old right-hander endured his worst start on Sunday, when he allowed eight runs and eight hits, including two homers, in just 4 2/3 innings. Known for his control during his playing days in Japan, he has issued 11 walks and surrendered 24 hits in 21 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez's four starts have produced -- in order -- a victory, a no-decision, a loss and a no-decision, just about what would be expected in total from a No. 5 starter for a sub. 500 team. He pitched into the sixth inning and was removed with the Mets leading in his most recent start, Tuesday against the Marlins. The current Braves roster presents only one specific challenge for him. Chipper Jones is batting .386 with 12 extra-base hits and 11 walks in 68 career plate appearances against Hernandez. Remarkably, he has produced a winning record since the beginning of the 2006 season, 38-36, while left-handed and right-handed hitters have batted .309 and .313, respectively, against him. In that period, he has produced a 1-1 record in three starts against the Braves, the victory coming in Turner Field in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old is making his third MLB start, and second at home. In his last outing, the left-hander was in line for the win against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. Taylor gave up two runs in five innings, and he exited with a three-run lead. However, the bullpen surrendered that advantage, and he was not involved in the decision. Taylor battled at Wrigley Field, getting through five innings. But he had to work out of jams, as he gave up five hits and walked three. His defense came up big for him. In his first two starts, Taylor has walked nine in 9 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While making his second start of the season against the Marlins, Lowe will attempt to be more effective than he was on April 15, when he allowed them four earned runs and issued five walks in just five innings. The veteran sinkerballer hasn't issued more than three walks during any of his other five outings and he enters this contest having won consecutive starts for the first time this year. Lowe is 0-1 with a 6.06 ERA in his past three starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: On April 16 at Atlanta, Sanchez worked six innings and gave up two runs in beating the Braves. The right-hander hasn't won since. Sanchez will look to get back on the winning track at home this time against Atlanta. He has lost three straight decisions, and in his last two starts, he allowed six runs in each. Sanchez had a rough time in his previous outing, a four-inning, six-run performance against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. The four innings were a season low. He also has struggled in the first inning of his last two starts, allowing nine runs, including three homers.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens will be looking to win for the first time since April 12. The hard-luck right-hander has gone winless while allowing a total of four earned runs in his past four starts. During his rain-shortened two-inning outing against the Astros on Saturday, Jurrjens allowed his first homer in a span of eight starts, dating back to Sept. 11. In three starts against the Marlins last year, he posted a 7.80 ERA and allowed a .333 batting average.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels was scheduled to pitch the series opener against the Cardinals, but was pushed back to the opener against Atlanta instead. Hamels turned the ankle against Washington on Tuesday after he had thrown 4 1/3 scoreless innings. It has been one setback after another for Hamels, who missed time in Spring Training with an elbow injury and who got knocked out of his start April 23 against Milwaukee when he got hit in the left shoulder with a line drive. He expects better days ahead.
away_pitcher_note: Looking for his first win in a span of 16 starts, Reyes is returning to Citizens Bank Park, where he's posted a 9.24 ERA in three career appearances. While the numbers don't show it, Reyes has been more impressive this year than he was during his first two big league seasons. He's surrendered 10 runs during his first three starts, and seven of those have scored in the sixth inning of games that he limited the opponent to one run through the first five innings.  Reyes was 0-4 with a 7.65 ERA in four starts against the Phillies last year.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton finally put together the pitching performance everybody had been waiting for Monday in St. Louis, where he allowed four hits and one run in six innings. Blanton had an 8.41 ERA after his first four starts, but cut that mark down to 6.84. Blanton said some improvements to his mechanics helped him Monday, and he is optimistic he can carry them into his start against the Braves
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez has lost his past two starts while encountering most of his trouble during one inning. After limiting the Mets to one hit through the first five innings on Monday, the 32-year-old right-hander allowed a pair of two-run homers before recording his first out in the sixth.  Five days earlier he allowed six singles during a four-run fifth inning against the Cardinals. In his only previous start against the Phillies this year, he allowed three runs in six innings and was in line for a win before the Braves blew a seven-run, seventh-inning lead.

home_pitcher_note: Myers had thrown three quality starts in a row before he allowed five runs in 5 1/3 innings Tuesday against the Cardinals. It was his shortest start of the season, having gone at least six innings in each of his first five starts in 2009. Myers is 4-9 with a 4.66 ERA in 27 appearances (20 starts) in his career against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a season-high 113-pitch effort against the Mets on Tuesday night, Kawakami will be looking for his first win since proving victorious in his April 11 Major League debut. While his pitch count was high, the 33-year-old right-hander stranded nine runners though the first four innings and exited a start for the first time this year without allowing a homer. He will have to stay away from his tendency to leave pitches up while making his first career start in the offensively friendly environment of Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note:
The National League Pitcher of the Month for April was quite dominant in his first May start, against the Phillies Wednesday night: seven scoreless innings, 10 strikeouts, two hits and three walks. Now he is to face the team he missed last week because a rainout pushed back the rotation. The Twins, his former team; the Rockies, a team he never has faced; and the Braves are the only teams Santana never has beaten. He lost twice to the Braves last season despite a 2.57 ERA in 21 innings (three starts). 
He is pitching as well this season as he did at any time in his first season with the Mets. Chipper Jones, Matt Diaz and Kelly Johnson have been a challenge for him. Their combined career average in 40 at-bats against Santana is .475.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe got the win against the Marlins on Wednesday, despite a start he called "disappointing." The 35-year-old right-hander, who gave up four runs in five innings the previous time he faced Florida, was beat around for six runs in five innings and needed 102 pitches to get through it. He gave up seven hits, walked three batters and struck out six while yielding the most runs in seven starts for the Braves this season. In eight career games -- two starts -- against the Mets, Lowe is 1-2 with an 8.78 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: No strikeouts? No problem. Mike Pelfrey has won his three  most recent starts pitching to contact. He struck out no one in beating the Phillies on May 1 and again on May 7 and has one strikeout in his past three starts, covering 18 innings. A sequence of 76 batters has come and gone since his last strikeout. No matter, he is unbeaten, at least partially because the Mets score for him -- 36 runs in five starts.  Pelfrey has a 2-3 record and a 5.54 ERA in seven career appearances -- six starts -- against the Braves. He has struck out 19 batters in 37 1/3 innings against them. Chipper Jones has hit two home runs in 10 at-bats against him.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens turned in yet another solid performance against the Marlins on Thursday. The only difference is this time he actually got enough run support to get the win. The 22-year-old right-hander gave up just two runs -- both coming off solo home runs by shortstop Hanley Ramirez -- on three hits through seven innings. Jurrjens walked two and struck out four while throwing 102 pitches -- 66 for strikes. The Curacao native has now given up just nine earned runs in 40 1/3 innings this year. For his career against the Mets, he is 2-1 with a 4.00 ERA in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Niese's fourth big league start didn't produce his second big league victory Friday night. What he won was another shot at that second victory. Now he is to face the team against whom he gained his first victory last season. Niese pitched eight scoreless innings against the Braves at Shea Stadium on Sept. 13, allowing six hits and two walks. He struck out seven. He wasn't quite that effective against the Pirates on Friday, allowing two runs -- the Mets' shaky defense contributed to both -- seven hits and no walks in six innings. He struck out five. But the zero walks is what was most conspicuous to his manager.
away_pitcher_note: Despite going 0-9 with a 6.61 ERA in his past 19 Major League appearances (18 starts), Reyes will likely be given a chance to gain an elusive win against the Mets. The 24-year-old left-hander has provided indication that he's improved since last year. But in three of his first four starts this year, he's been unable to escape the damage of one big inning. He is 0-1 with a 8.74 ERA in three career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his victorious 115-pitch effort against the Phillies on Saturday, Vazquez should benefit from the one extra day of rest he'll receive entering his first start against the Diamondbacks since 2003. The only runs he surrendered in 7 2/3 innings against the Phillies came courtesy of a pair of solo homers. After allowing just one home run in his first five starts, the 33-year-old right-hander has seen each of the eight runs he's combined to allow in his past two outings come courtesy of the long ball. During his past six starts, Vazquez has worked 40 1/3 innings, recorded 57 strikeouts and issued just seven walks.
away_pitcher_note: Davis pitched well in his last time out, but did not come away with a win because his offense struggled to score off Nationals starter John Lannan. Davis allowed one run on four hits over six innings and left trailing, 1-0. In his start prior to that against the Dodgers, Davis struggled allowing four runs on five hits in lasting just 4 1/3 innings. Afterwards he said he felt like he was trying to be too fine with his pitches, which caused him to fall behind in the count.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami has shown definite improvement over his past two starts, limiting the Mets and Phillies to two runs in each start. While pitching six strong innings in Philadelphia on Sunday, the right-hander notched his first win in five starts and didn't allow a homer for the second successive start. While focusing on keeping his pitches low, Kawakami has limited some of the extra-base hits that were a problem during his first month in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Remarkably -- considering his pedigree (first-round pick in 2006 First-Year Player Draft) and spectacular Major League debut -- Scherzer remains winless in 22 games and 13 starts. He is 0-7 despite a solid 3.39 ERA, making him just another hard-luck pitcher on the Arizona staff. In his last start, Sunday against the Nationals, he allowed three homers for the first time in his budding career.

home_pitcher_note: While winning his fourth consecutive start with seven solid innings against the Mets on Monday night, Lowe provided one of his best performances of the season. The 35-year-old sinkerballer held the Mets hitless through the first 3 2/3 innings and limited them to just one extra-base hit -- a seventh-inning leadoff double. He has allowed two earned runs or less in three of his past four starts. Having pitched the previous four seasons with the Dodgers, Lowe is familiar with the Diamondbacks. He was 3-1 with a 2.05 ERA in five starts against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: Garland got shelled by the Reds on Monday, yielding seven runs on 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings. He constantly left balls up in the zone, and Cincinnati made him pay. The D-backs had won Garland's past four starts, three of which were quality outings, including his seven shutout innings May 5 in San Diego. The durable right-hander has now failed to get into the fourth in either of his two losses while pitching into the seventh in his five other starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe was scheduled to pitch Sunday but was pushed back to Monday when the Braves' series finale with the D-backs was rained out and will be pitching on six days of rest. While winning his fourth consecutive start with seven solid innings against the Mets on Monday night, Lowe provided one of his best performances of the season. The 35-year-old sinkerballer held the Mets hitless through the first 3 2/3 innings and limited them to just one extra-base hit -- a seventh-inning leadoff double. He has allowed two earned runs or fewer in three of his past four starts. While with the Dodgers last season, Lowe went 2-1 with a 3.26 ERA against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: About the best that can be said for Marquis is he's not facing the Astros. Already having poor numbers against many of that team's best hitters, Marquis gave up 10 hits and nine runs in 3 2/3 innings in his last start, at Coors Field. The Braves were Marquis' original Major League club, but he hasn't fared that well at Turner Field -- 8-10 with a 4.53 ERA in 50 games.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens was pushed back a day after Sunday's rainout and will be pitching on six days of rest. Jurrjens' run of tough luck was extended on Tuesday, when he held the Mets scoreless until surrendering a two-run single with one out in the eighth inning. One inning later, the Mets tied the game, giving him a no-decision. Jurrjens has gone 1-2 with a 1.95 ERA during his past six starts. He was 2-1 with a 3.48 ERA in three starts against the Rockies last year.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Hammel pitched solidly for the first time at Coors Field by giving up four runs -- one earned -- on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings. However, he was the hard-luck loser. Hammel was able to locate his fastball and mix in some good sliders and curveballs against the Astros. Hammel has never faced the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez completed his second straight impressive outing in Friday night's 4-3 win over the D-backs, but ended up with a no-decision when Arizona tied the game in the ninth inning. He allowed just two earned runs and struck out 10 in seven innings. The strikeout total gave Vazquez 39 career games with double-digit strikeouts. Vazquez is winless in four starts at Turner Field this season. This will be Vazquez's first start against the Rockies since June 8, 2004, when he pitched for the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has sizzled, striking out 22 in 15 innings over his last two starts. The only drawback was the Rockies haven't hit well behind him. They lost 3-1 at Coors against the Marlins in the first game, when he fanned a career-high 12 in eight innings. He struck out 10 in seven innings against the Pirates in his last start but left trailing, 1-0 (the Rockies won it, 3-1, with a ninth-inning comeback). De La Rosa has had consistently strong fastball command throughout the season. Against the Pirates, he had supreme confidence in his changeup. He has never pitched at Turner Field, and the only time he faced the Braves he struck out three and walked two in two scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: With Jo-Jo Reyes being moved to the bullpen, Medlen will attempt to continue the dominance he's shown while going 4-0 with a 1.07 ERA in the six starts he's made for Triple-A Gwinnett this year. Medlen hasn't started since May 11, but threw in relief on Saturday. The 23-year-old right-hander possesses a live fastball, an above-average changeup and the ability to consistently locate his slider. He began his rapid rise toward the Majors after joining Double-A Mississippi's rotation midway through the 2008 season.
away_pitcher_note: Cook had a wet and painful experience Saturday at Pittsburgh. He pitched a strong first inning but gave up four runs on four second-inning hits, and didn't return after a rain delay. To top it off, he received treatment for a sore back. the poor outing came after Cook had posted a 2.67 ERA in the previous four outings. No one expects Cook to miss a start with the back issue, but the Rockies are monitoring it.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami had a solid outing Saturday night against the Diamondbacks, but was saddled with the loss as Atlanta lost, 12-0, at Turner Field. The Japanese right-hander went five innings while giving up three runs on five hits. After struggling early, he retired the last eight men he faced. Kawakami has had command issues this season, averaging five walks per nine innings. Although he only walked one batter against the D-Backs, the 33-year-old rookie was burned by four extra-base hits. This will be his first career start against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday against the White Sox at Rogers Centre, Halladay allowed two runs in seven innings for his eighth win of the season. Only one of the runs was earned, as Halladay committed a fielding error that allowed Chicago second baseman Chris Getz to get on base, and Getz eventually came around to score. Both runs were scored in the first inning. Halladay allowed six hits and one walk, striking out eight. He pounded the strike zone, throwing 77 of his 103 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Grasping his role as the Braves ace, Lowe has pitched at least seven innings and allowed less than three runs in four of his past five starts.  While limiting the Rockies to two runs and three hits in eight innings on Monday night, the 35-year-old right-hander lost his bid to win five consecutive starts. Lowe is 3-4 with a 4.94 ERA in nine career starts against the Blue Jays. But he's 1-1 with a 2.49 ERA in his past three outings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Janssen has been waiting a long time for this start. The 27-year-old right-hander missed the entire 2008 season after undergoing surgery on his right shoulder, and an unrelated shoulder issue cost him a chance of making Toronto's Opening Day roster during Spring Training. In five starts in the Minors this year, Janssen posted a 0.76 ERA between stints with Class A Dunedin and Double-A New Hampshire. Janssen last pitched in the Majors in 2007, when he posted a 2.35 ERA in 70 games as a setup man for the Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens of late has been nothing short of unhittable for the Braves. The 23-year-old right-hander improved to 4-2 and lowered his ERA below 2.00 with another quality start against the Rockies on Tuesday. In that outing, Jurrjens went seven innings while allowing just three hits and one earned run and recording eight strikeouts. Last season, Jurrjens tossed a gem against the Blue Jays, going eight shutout innings and allowing just three hits. He now has six quality starts in his past seven outings.
away_pitcher_note: Richmond fashioned arguably the strongest outing of his career on Monday, holding the White Sox without a run on five hits over seven innings in Toronto. After a late collapse by the Jays' bullpen, though, Richmond walked away with a no-decision. The 29-year-old rookie right-hander finished with seven strikeouts and only one walk in the effort. Richmond's performance was an impressive turnaround from his previous outing, during which he gave up five runs in just 1 2/3 innings in a loss to the Yankees on May 13. Richmond has never faced the Braves in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is coming off his best effort of the season, a six-inning two-hitter last Wednesday at San Diego. Both hits, however, generated runs as the Padres prevailed, 2-1. It was Sanchez's third consecutive losing decision but also just his second quality start of the year. Sanchez has struggled against Atlanta, going 0-2 with a 7.04 ERA in three appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez finally recorded his first win at Turner Field this season in an abbreviated outing during the Braves' 12-3 win over the Rockies on Wednesday. The Braves' offensive outburst gave Vazquez's arm a welcome reprieve. He threw just 71 pitches on Wednesday after averaging 111 pitches per game over his previous three starts. Vazquez has been stingy with runs of late. Including his five innings with no earned runs against the Rockies, Vazquez has given up two earned runs or fewer in each of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has struck out 10 or more hitters in three games this season, including his most recent outing last Thursday at San Diego. He received a no decision in that one despite allowing one run and four hits in seven innings. Lincecum has thrived in his limited number of appearances against Atlanta, going 4-0 with a 2.70 ERA in four career appearances, including 2-0, 1.72 last year.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen looks to shake off a disastrous Major League debut against the Rockies on Thursday. In that outing, Medlen pitched just three-plus innings, allowing five earned runs on three hits, five walks, a hit batter, a balk and two wild pitches. Medlen posted superb numbers in Triple-A Gwinnett before getting called up to Atlanta. For Gwinnett, he was a perfect 5-0 with a 1.19 ERA. This will be the first road start of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Rebounding from a three start stretch in which he was 1-2 with an 11.05 ERA and a .403 opponents' batting average, Johnson yielded one run and six hits in 5 1/3 innings last Friday at Seattle. This will be the 45-year-old's third attempt at career victory No. 299. Johnson has been relatively so-so against Atlanta, posting a 5-5 record with a 4.33 ERA in 12 career appearances against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday night against the Blue Jays, Kawakami provided the kind of outing that the Braves had in mind when they signed him. The 33-year-old rookie outdueled 2003 American League Cy Young Award winner Roy Halladay, throwing eight innings of shutout ball while allowing just three hits and striking out seven. Perhaps most importantly, Kawakami completed a start without walking a batter for this first time this season. The Japanese import seemed to get stronger as the game went on, maintaining his low-90s fastball into the eighth inning. This will be Kawakami's first start against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Haren had one of his poorest outings his last time out, against his former team in Oakland. The right-hander allowed five runs on nine hits over seven innings. The five runs came courtesy of four Oakland homers, the most Haren had ever given up in a single game. Ironically, Haren said he had very good stuff in the game, but missed his spots, and when he did the A's made him pay. Haren's start before this one lasted just three innings, thanks to a rainout in South Florida. That could have contributed to Haren being somewhat rusty and not sharp against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Lowe continued to eat innings put the Braves in a position to win, going 7 1/3 innings and earning his sixth win of the season during Saturday's victory over the Blue Jays. The Braves' ace pitched his 2,000th career inning during that game, which saw him allow just two runs on five hits. Lowe has now allowed two runs in each of his past three starts. Pitching for the Dodgers, Lowe went 5-1 with a 2.05 ERA against the Diamondbacks last season.

home_pitcher_note: Garland did a good imitation of a tight-rope walker in his last start against the A's at Oakland-Alameda Coliseum. The right-hander allowed nine base runners in the first five innings of the outing, yet somehow managed to keep the A's off the board in that span. Garland tempted fate once too often and allowed three runs in the sixth as the A's beat the D-backs, 6-2. All three of the runs came on Landon Powell's first big league homer. Garland said after the game that he simply did not have his good command and the ball did not feel good in his hand. Signed as a free agent to replace Randy Johnson in the rotation, Garland has success when he's able to keep the ball down near the knees. When he gets it up near the belt he runs into trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Although it isn't obvious from his stat line, Jurrjens wasn't as sharp in his Sunday start against the Blue Jays as he has been in recent starts. Jurrjens went six innings and allowed just two earned runs, but surrendered eight hits and two walks on 102 pitches in a no-decision. He had gone at least seven innings in his previous three starts. On the season, Jurrjens has been among the league's best starters. He has allowed more than two runs in just one start and has won his last two decisions. Jurrjens last pitched against the Diamondbacks on August 9 of last year, going six innings and earning a win.

home_pitcher_note: Davis has found it hard to get a win lately despite pitching well. In his last outing, he seemed well on his way to a win against the Padres. Davis allowed just one run through seven innings and the D-backs had built a 7-1 lead. However, things fell apart for the D-backs in the eighth as the bullpen imploded and allowed five runs to pull the Padres to within 7-6. One inning later, Chad Qualls blew just his second save of the year and the D-backs wound up losing, 9-7, in 10 innings. Davis is in the final year of a three-year contract extension he signed after coming over in a trade prior to the 2007 season.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez has allowed five earned runs or more in three of his past six outings and allowed two earned runs or less in the other three starts that encompass this span. Making his recent inconsistencies more maddening is the fact that the majority of the struggles encountered during each of those three losses were experienced in the fifth or sixth innings. While working seven innings and getting a no-decision during his May 15 start against the Diamondbacks, the 32-year-old right-hander allowed two earned runs and registered 10 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer had to go 22 games and 13 starts before getting his first big league win, but the right-hander now has two in his last three starts. Last time out against the Padres, he was dominating through seven innings as Arizona built a 6-0 lead. Scherzer tired in the eighth and gave up a homer and single to lead off the frame before being removed. The bullpen struggled, allowing three more runs to score and pull the Padres to within 6-4. Despite a heart-stopping ninth, which he watched from the training room, Scherzer picked up the win as the D-backs held on, 6-5. The right-hander struck out 10 in the game and did not walk a batter. He picked up his first big league win May 16 against the Braves in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen's control has hurt him during his first two career starts. After throwing just 43 of 80 pitches for strikes during his Major League debut on May 21, the 23-year-old right-hander returned Tuesday and issued just two walks in 5 1/3 innings against the Giants.  The most costly walk was issued to Tim Lincecum with two outs in what would become a four-run second inning. Medlen's inability to retire Lincecum provided further proof that he's allowing his nerves to get the best of him during pressure situations.  He ended Tuesday's outing by retiring the final 11 batters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Looking to improve his control, Kawakami has recently focused on attacking the strike zone early in the count.  This approach worked on May 22, when he threw first-pitch strikes to 22 of the 27 batters he faced and held the Blue Jays scoreless over eight innings.  But with an average fastball that is occasionally flat, this approach could also prove costly against an aggressive lineup. The 33-year-old right-hander struggled with his control on Wednesday, when he issued four walks and allowed nine hits in 5 2/3 innings against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: This was supposed to be Carlos Zambrano's start, but he's serving a six-game suspension for his antics in last Wednesday's game against the Pirates. Instead, Wells will try for his first win. The rookie right-hander has thrown three straight quality starts, but has yet to get a "W." In his last outing Thursday against the Dodgers, he gave up two runs on eight hits over seven innings and struck out seven. He threw 111 pitches, 70 for strikes. That's a good ratio.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe proved to be his biggest critic after his last start, saying he "pitched poorly" against the Diamondbacks on Thursday at Chase Field. The big right-hander gave up a season-high 10 hits in seven innings in the loss. He was charged with five runs, but only three earned in the hard-luck loss. He still has pitched at least seven innings in four of his last seven starts. He still ranks among the league leaders in wins, innings pitched and games started.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly leads the Cubs in wins and quality starts (seven) after beating the Dodgers, 2-1, in his last start. He gave up four runs, including a homer by Matt Kemp that landed in the basket rimming the left-field bleachers. When he pitches seven or more innings, Lilly is 2-2 with a 1.55 ERA in four starts. He will miss Wrigley Field, as four of his six wins have come at home.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander received the run support he had been seeking all season but struggled in the 88-pitch outing against the Diamondbacks in his last time out. Against Arizona, Jurrjens was charged with eight hits and five runs in five innings pitched. He had pitched at least six innings in his four previous starts and seven of his last eight before the outing in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Zambrano's first start back after serving his six-game suspension. The right-hander was penalized for his antics on May 27, when he argued a close call at home plate, threw a baseball into left field then hurled his glove. Zambrano took his frustrations out on a Gatorade dispenser in the Cubs dugout. As far as pitching goes, he's one win away from No. 100 in his career and needs four K's to tie Bill Hutchinson for sixth on the team's all-time strikeout list. Before he was ejected, Zambrano gave up two runs on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander received the run support he had been seeking all season but struggled in the 88-pitch outing against the Diamondbacks in his last time out. Against Arizona, Jurrjens was charged with eight hits and five runs in five innings pitched. He had pitched at least six innings in his four previous starts and seven of his last eight before the outing in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo struck out the side in the first inning and finished with nine strikeouts in Sunday's 5-2 win over Cincinnati. The 23-year-old started stellar, retiring eight of the first nine batters via strikeout, but struggled with his command and was pulled after 5 1/3 innings. He allowed seven hits and two runs -- one earned -- while walking two. Gallardo made his only career start against the Braves in September 2007, when he received a no-decision after allowing two runs on three hits over seven innings while striking out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez had a strong outing last Saturday against the D-backs, even though he didn't get the win at Chase Field in his first start there in four years. The right-hander allowed two runs (one earned) on seven hits, walked one and struck out seven in 6 1/3 innings. Vazquez pitched the 2005 season for the D-backs and was traded to the White Sox the following offseason. After three years in Chicago, Vazquez was traded to the Braves this past offseason. His last start at Chase Field was on Sept. 25, 2005, and his last win came five days earlier. Vazquez had allowed five earned runs or more in three of his past six outings and allowed two earned runs or fewer in the other three starts that encompass that span.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan had to battle in his start at Florida on Monday, throwing 51 pitches in the first two innings and 68 pitches through the third. But he limited the damage to two Marlins runs in five innings despite allowing 10 Florida baserunners (seven hits, three walks) by stranding a runner in scoring position in the second, third and fifth innings. Suppan left with a 4-2 lead, but his short night further taxed an overworked bullpen that lost the lead before recording the first Marlins out in the sixth. Suppan is 2-5 with a 4.65 ERA in seven career starts against the Braves but was excellent against Atlanta last season, going 2-1 with a 1.71 ERA in three starts, including a win at Turner Field last Aug. 1 in which he twirled seven shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Tommy Hanson will make his highly-anticipated Major League debut on Saturday when the Braves take on the Brewers at Turner Field. The MVP of the Arizona Fall League and the No. 24 prospect in MLB.com's 2009 pre-season Top 50 Prospects list, Hanson is widely regarded as one of the best young pitching prospects in the game. The 6-6 right-hander has dominated at Triple-A Gwinnett this season, posting a 1.49 ERA while striking out 90 batters in 66 1/3 innings. Hanson will start in place of his roommate and friend Kris Medlen, who will move to the Braves' bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers desperately needed Parra to pitch deep into his start at Florida on Tuesday to spare a battered bullpen, and he didn't do it. Not only did he set dubious career highs in allowing 10 runs and 11 hits, Parra only made it through the fourth. His ERA has jumped from 4.82 to 6.75 over his last three starts, all losses. The Brewers are one of only three teams in baseball to use just five starting pitchers this season (the Giants and Pirates are the others) and the Brewers appear committed to allowing Parra to work out his kinks in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Since tossing eight scoreless innings against the Blue Jays on May 22, Kawakami has once again proven to be mediocre.   After surrendering a leadoff homer to Alfonso Soriano on Tuesday night, he pitched effectively before allowing the Cubs to produce a two-run sixth inning. The 33-year-old right-hander hadn't allowed a homer in his previous six starts. The Braves will continue to monitor his shoulder which has fatigued while he's adapted to the schedule of a five-man rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Duke stretched his streak of pitching at least seven innings to five straight starts as he gave up just one run in seven innings in his last start on Tuesday. He threw only 90 pitches as he outdueled the Mets' Johan Santana. Duke has won three of his last four decisions, with the only loss coming when he pitched eight innings and surrendered only two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe earned a no-decision on Wednesday against the Cubs despite pitching at least seven innings for the fourth straight game. The big right-hander allowed two runs on five hits and retired 11 of the last 13 hitters he faced. Wednesday was the third time this season Lowe allowed three earned runs or fewer and failed to earn a victory. He has enjoyed much success against the Pirates in his career, winning all six games he has started against Pittsburgh and posting a 2.72 ERA.
away_pitcher_note:
Despite being handed four first-inning runs, Ohlendorf wasn't able to earn the win in his last start. He lasted only 4 1/3 innings as he gave up five earned runs on nine hits against the Mets. The no decision kept Ohlendorf winless in his last three starts. The right-hander is facing the Braves for the first time in his career.
He's 2-3 with a 5.12 ERA on the road this season, giving up 31 hits in 31 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: While allowing nine earned runs during his past two starts, Jurrjens has encountered the first rough stretch of the season. He had allowed three earned runs or less during his 10 starts preceding this mini-slump. The 23-year-old right-hander surrendered a season-high nine hits, but still worked seven innings against the Brewers on Friday night.  The outing resulted in his first loss since April 27. One of his tough-luck losses occurred on April 17, when he limited the Pirates to one run and four hits in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The recently acquired right-hander is making his 2009 Major League debut after going 7-2 with a 2.26 ERA (18 earned runs in 71 2/3 innings) in 11 starts for the Triple-A Gwinnett Braves. Morton was 4-8 with a 6.15 ERA in 16 appearances, 15 starts for Atlanta in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez encountered some bad luck on Saturday, when he limited the Brewers to two runs over six innings and found himself on the wrong end of a shutout. He is 1-3 with a 4.18 ERA in six home starts and 3-1 with a 2.87 ERA in six road starts. The 33-year-old right-hander, who ranks among the National League leaders in strikeouts, has won just once while allowing two earned runs or fewer during each of his past four starts at Turner Field. He notched his first win of the season on April 19, when he scattered five hits over six scoreless innings against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm, who lost to the Astros two starts ago despite allowing only two runs (one earned) in seven innings, was just little less impressive outing in his last start against Houston. The left-hander went seven innings again this time, giving up four runs and striking out four. The biggest difference, though, was that he earned the win, his first in his last eight starts. Maholm won his first outing against the Braves this season, throwing seven innings of shutout ball and giving up four hits. He is 1-1 in his career against Atlanta with a 1.80 ERA over three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Berken has experienced a lot in his first three Major League starts. He has pitched well and lost and pitched so-so and won, but he was hit hard by the A's in his last appearance, giving up nine runs on seven hits over 3 1/3 innings. There's little question that Berken has the stuff to be a Major League pitcher; he just may have to learn the hard way.
away_pitcher_note: After proving perfect and dominant during the first three innings of his Major League debut on Sunday, Hanson struggled to command his fastball and surrendered three two-run homers. The hard-throwing right-hander, who is considered one of the game's top pitching prospects, needed 31 pitches to complete his first three innings and 60 to complete his final three. With a plus slider and an effective curve, he can be dominant if he can consistently get ahead in the count. Hanson's fastball rests around 95 mph and was clocked as high as 97 mph during his debut against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Hill didn't even get out of the first inning in his last start, pushing the Orioles to an early deficit behind a few walks. Hill has either been really good or really bad this season and has yet to fall in the middle. The southpaw is still getting loose after losing much of Spring Training to an elbow injury. Baltimore needs Hill to pound the strike zone and get away from his walk-heavy tendencies.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami saw the bullpen hand over his bid for his fourth victory of the season on Monday against the Pirates, giving him the no-decision. After allowing three runs on four hits over six innings, Kawakami left the game with a 6-3 lead. Unfortunately for Kawakami, the bullpen surrendered that lead in the seventh. In that outing, Kawakami was victimized a pair of triples in the sixth that led to both of his runs. His control, which has been problematic at times this season, was solid as he threw 60 of his 95 pitches for strikes and surrendered just one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Bergesen has had three straight strong starts, and he threw eight shutout innings against Seattle in his last outing to earn the victory. The right-hander has pitched at least seven innings in three straight starts and hasn't allowed more than two earned runs since May 24. Bergesen has allowed more than one home run in just one of his first 10 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe wasn't his sharpest against the Pirates on Tuesday, but he was good enough for his seventh win of the season and his seventh career win against Pittsburgh in as many tries. On Tuesday, Lowe pitched into the eighth inning for the fifth straight game. He was hit hard early, surrendering five hits and three runs in his first four innings, but settled down over the last three frames. Lowe is 7-2 in his career against the Orioles, but hasn't faced them since 2004 when he was pitching for the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Harang got back on track after a few rough starts with a very good effort against the Nationals on Wednesday. He threw 7 2/3 shutout innings, staying out of trouble the entire time. Harang had given up homers in his last eight appearances, but Washington didn't hit the ball hard, much less have a shot at a homer. Manager Dusty Baker said after the Reds pulled out a 4-2 victory in 12 innings that Harang had been "lights-out."
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens took the loss on Wednesday against the Pirates despite giving up two runs on just four hits in six innings. The young right-hander struggled in the early innings with control, which led to him throwing 111 pitches in just six innings. Last year, Jurrjens was shelled in his only career start against the Reds. He lasted just 4 1/3 innings while allowing six runs on nine hits and walking six. Despite three starts in a row that Jurrjens hasn't been his sharpest, his ERA is still below 3.00.

home_pitcher_note: Owings has pitched better than his record indicates, suffering some tough losses. He got burned again in Thursday's 3-2 loss in Washington, leaving after 5 1/3 innings with a 2-0 lead, but the bullpen couldn't hold it. He had control problems that night, giving up four walks and hitting two despite giving up just one run on four hits. Owings threw 102 pitches but said that he's learning with every start and is getting better.
away_pitcher_note: Like teammate Jair Jurrjens on Wednesday, Vazquez fell victim to the Braves' lack of run support on his way to a tough no-decision on Thursday. The native of Puerto Rico tossed eight outstanding innings, surrendering just two hits and striking out 12 Pirates. Unfortunately for Vazquez, one of those hits was a solo home run and the Braves offense was unable to give him the win. In his April 24 start against the Reds, Vazquez got the win after pitching six innings and allowing just one earned run on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: In his second big league start, Maloney took a 4-1 loss to the Royals on Friday, when his lineup notched just three hits while Luke Hochevar threw a complete game with only 80 pitches. That meant the margin of error was mighty slim. The left-hander pitched six innings and gave up four earned runs and six hits with two walks and five strikeouts. It was a pair of home runs allowed with two outs that hurt the most, especially Alberto Callaspo's two-run shot in the sixth after the runner on first was picked off but reached second base safely. On the next pitch, Maloney hung a slider to Callaspo and paid for it.
away_pitcher_note: The Braves' top pitching prospect, who made his Major League debut June 7 against Milwaukee, has been anything but dominating in his first two outings. Atlanta manager Bobby Cox and catcher Brian McCann, however, aren't concerned, because Hanson has been unflappable and able to adjust his repertoire on the fly depending on the situation he's facing. Case in point: his fastball was hammered in his debut, so Hanson mixed in more changeups in his last outing against the Orioles on Friday. The results weren't indicative of the hype that followed Hanson from Triple-A -- 5 2/3 innings pitched with nine hits and five walks allowed -- but he ground out his first victory.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander's frustrating season continued last Saturday against the Phillies, when he was pounded for seven hits and four runs over four innings. Matsuzaka has some troubling numbers. He's given up 51 hits over 31 innings, and opponents are hitting .372 against him. Matsuzaka hasn't pitched six innings in any of his seven starts. He won his only previous start against the Braves, giving up nine hits and three runs over eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Braves' Japanese import is on a string of three straight no-decisions, hasn't won in four starts and has been victimized by poor run support. Atlanta has scored only 22 runs for him during 13 starts and the right-hander can be a little wild early. He isn't prone to allowing home runs -- a first-inning shot by Baltimore's Adam Jones in his last start Saturday was only the second he's surrendered in his past eight starts -- but Kawakami labored in his last outing, throwing 53 of his 104 pitches in the first two innings. He needs to throw first-pitch strikes and control the count to be successful.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett's run of seven consecutive quality starts came to an abrupt end in his last outing in Philadelphia, where he was pounded for 11 hits and seven runs -- six earned -- over six innings. Beckett is 3-0 with a 3.55 ERA in six Fenway starts this season. Opponents are hitting .245 against him. Lifetime against the Braves, Beckett is 6-7 with a 2.45 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This should be an interesting homecoming for Lowe, who hasn't pitched in Boston since playing a key postseason role for the 2004 World Series champion Red Sox. Recognized as a big-game pitcher, the veteran sinkerballer will be looking to erase the disappointment he encountered on Sunday, when he allowed seven earned runs and lasted just 2 1/3 innings against the Orioles. He had been 6-2 with a 3.50 ERA in his previous nine starts. In the 46 starts he's made at Fenway Park since becoming a full-time starter in 2002, Lowe has gone 28-10 with a 3.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield continues to shine amidst the controversy surrounding the crowded Boston rotation. The 42-year-old knuckleballer picked up his ninth win of the season last Tuesday at Fenway Park, allowing two runs on six hits over six innings against the Marlins. A 13-game winner in Interleague Play, Wakefield is 3-4 lifetime against Atlanta with a 5.06 ERA in 13 appearances.
away_pitcher_note: With a lengthy rain delay limiting him to two innings against the Red on Tuesday, Jurrjens should be well rested as he attempts to end his three-game losing streak. While going 0-3 with a 4.20 ERA in his past three starts, the 23-year-old right-hander has continued to be saddled with limited run support.The Braves have totaled 37 runs while he's still been on the mound during his 14 starts this year. Jurrjens has gone 2-0 with a 3.54 ERA during his four previous starts in day games this season.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez has encountered nothing but bad luck, as the Braves have scored three runs or fewer during each of his past five starts.  While going 0-2 with a 2.54 ERA in his past four outings, the 32-year-old right-hander has limited opponents to a .173 batting average and .206 on-base percentage.    The durable veteran has completed eight innings in each of his past two starts and exited with a loss.   He is 0-1 with a 5.93 ERA in his past five starts against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did notch his ninth quality start in his last game against the White Sox, but he also walked six over six-plus innings. He took the loss, and of his 104 pitches, only 51 were strikes. That's not a good ratio. It was the 14th time in his career the right-hander has walked six or more in a game, and the first since July 25, 2008. Dempster has gone six or more innings in all but one start this year. He was 1-0 last year against the Braves, but is just 2-10 lifetime.

home_pitcher_note: Inconsistent command has been an issue as Hanson has allowed nine walks during the 11 2/3 innings he's completed while proving victorious in his past two starts. Armed with a plus-fastball and a plus-slider, the highly regarded prospect has shown the ability to pitch out of jams and make quick adjustments.  After using two strikeouts to escape a bases-loaded jam with one out during Thursday's second inning against the Reds, he threw 25 of his next 37 pitches for strikes and ended the six-inning effort without allowing a run.
away_pitcher_note: It appears Wang showed enough in his last start to earn at least one more chance. He surrendered three runs in five innings in a loss to the Nationals on Wednesday in an outing manager Joe Girardi said was encouraging despite the result. If Wang had faltered again, he probably would have been replaced with Phil Hughes, and it's likely his status in the rotation is still on a start-to-start basis.

home_pitcher_note: With the opportunity to face the Yankees, Kawakami will once again have the chance to prove he's a big-game pitcher. His finest performance occurred on May 23, when he tossed eight scoreless innings against Roy Halladay and the Blue Jays.   Then he produced similar dominance on Friday, when ignored the pressure of facing Daisuke Matsuzaka by limiting the Red Sox to two hits and two earned runs in six innings. In his past nine starts, the 33-year-old right-hander has gone 3-2 with a 3.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After clashing with catcher Jorge Posada in his previous start, Chamberlain found a better flow with rookie catcher Francisco Cervelli on Thursday, scattering seven hits while walking four and striking out six. He held the Nationals to three runs in six innings, but the Yankees scored none and Chamberlain took the loss in a 3-0 defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe will be making his first start against the Yankees since beating them at Yankee Stadium in Game 7 of the 2004 American League Championship Series. While allowing three runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Red Sox on Saturday night, the 36-year-old sinkerballer lost a second consecutive start for the first time this year. But while limiting the Red Sox to one hit through the first four innings, he was much more efficient than he'd been five days earlier, when he allowed the Orioles a season-high seven runs in just 2 1/3 innings. He is 3-1 with a 2.75 ERA in his past five home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Andy Pettitte in Atlanta? Brings back visions of Game 5 of the 1996 World Series, in which Pettitte fired 8 1/3 shutout innings to outduel John Smoltz. And while Pettitte may not be the same pitcher he was then, the Braves aren't the same team, either. Regardless, both parties have improved in recent weeks -- Pettitte firing seven innings of one-run ball in Miami last Friday, the Braves boosting their offense with a trade for Nate McLouth. In nine previous regular season games against the Braves, Pettitte is 5-1 with a 3.13 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens' latest experience with misfortune occurred on Sunday, when his own error allowed the Red Sox to score three unearned runs in the first inning. A seventh-inning rally spared the 23-year-old right-hander from losing a fourth consecutive start. Over the course of his last four starts, he's gone 0-3 with a 3.80 ERA. The Braves have scored a total of three runs during the past 21 innings that Jurrjens has pitched. While offensive support has been minimal, the young hurler has also hurt himself with inconsistent command during the early innings of his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett is in the midst a dominant stretch that affirms precisely why the Red Sox traded for him prior to the 2006 season. Boston's ace made quick work of the Braves last Saturday at Fenway Park, firing a five-hit shutout for his seventh career win against Atlanta. He threw 94 pitches in the contest, the lowest total among the righty's six career complete games. Over his past six outings, Beckett is 4-1 with a 1.44 ERA and 42 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez finally received adequate run support on Monday night, when he tossed 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Cubs and ended a three-game losing streak. Having received a total of 10 runs during the past 42 innings that he's pitched, the 32-year-old right-hander hasn't received the All-Star attention that his statistics would normally garner.  He entered Tuesday leading the Majors with 112 strikeouts and has allowed two runs or fewer in seven of his last nine starts.  Vazquez has allowed three earned runs or less in three of his past four starts against the Red Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Wakefield pitched well enough to pick up his 10th win of the season Sunday at Fenway Park against the Braves, but the normally reliable Red Sox bullpen faltered in the late innings before Boston pulled out a walk-off win in the ninth. The knuckleballer scattered nine hits over 6 2/3 innings, allowing four runs. Saturday's start in Atlanta will mark the 382nd of his Red Sox career, tying Roger Clemens for the most in club history.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson continued his recent trend of creating trouble for himself and then pitching out of it.
