In his only start against Atlanta at Citi Field, though, Pelfrey limited the Braves to two runs on six hits in seven innings. The lefties in the Braves' lineup have excelled in their careers against Pelfrey, as Adam LaRoche is 4-for-4, Brian McCann is 11-for-23 with a home run and Chipper Jones is 6-for-15 with two long balls.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson retired the first 10 Phillies batters he faced on Friday night but was then damaged by the power of Ryan Howard, whose two homers accounted for the three runs the Braves right-hander allowed in seven innings. Four starts into his return from Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery, Hudson finds himself still searching for consistent control. Still, two blown saves are all that separate him from winning each of his first three starts.

home_pitcher_note: On Saturday, right fielder Ian Desmond made a costly mistake in the seventh inning and it would spoil a great outing by John Lannan, who found himself in a pitchers' duel with former Nationals hurler Tim Redding. Lannan lasted seven innings and gave up three runs on five hits. He threw just 74 pitches and should have allowed fewer than the three runs he gave up.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the first of Vazquez's final three chances to gain the two wins he'd need to match the career-best win total that he set in 2001. The veteran right-hander has gone 3-0 and surrendered just two earned runs in the 23 innings that he's completed during his past three starts. His latest stellar effort came on Saturday, when he limited the Phillies to three hits in seven scoreless innings. This will be his first start against the Nationals since 2005.

home_pitcher_note: Mock has lost four decisions in his past five starts. He didn't get a decision in the other one. He's allowed 21 runs in 27 innings over those starts. He yielded four runs on nine hits over seven innings in his last outing, a 7-2 loss to the Mets. Mock's first two appearances this season were in relief against the Braves. He gave up the only run in a 1-0 Atlanta win on April 22.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson encountered some rare struggles on Sunday, when he surrendered four runs and seven hits in five innings against the Phillies. The 23-year-old right-hander entered the game with 17 consecutive scoreless innings. In addition, during his previous four starts combined he had surrendered just two runs. Having already thrown 42 more innings than he completed last year, the rookie hurler is nearing the portion of the season when fatigue could prove to be a factor. He has allowed just two runs in the 13 2/3 innings he's completed against Washington this year.

home_pitcher_note: With concerns about the right shoulder inflammation he battled during the early days of Spring Training in the past, Jurrjens is looking show why so many believe his future is so bright. away_pitcher_note: Dempster got off to a slow start last season, going 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA in his first five starts. The right-hander is determined to change that this season. home_pitcher_note: Widely regarded as one of the game's top young pitchers, Hanson made his much-anticipated Major League debut in early June and then spent the next four months living up to tremendous expectations. Armed with four plus pitches, including a slider that has been compared to the successful one that John Smoltz displayed, Hanson recoded 91 strikeouts and issued 26 walks in the 86 2/3 innings that he completed after the All-Star break.  This will be his first career start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wells was the surprise of 2009. The right-hander was called up May 8 and never looked back. He led NL rookies in starts and finished second in wins and innings pitched. A converted catcher, Wells is still learning.

home_pitcher_note: Even with the presence of his star-studded rotation mates, Sanchez is as good a choice as any to start San Francisco's home opener. Only an eighth-inning fielding error separated Sanchez from a perfect game that night. Sanchez finished the exhibition season with plenty of momentum. In his final three starts, he recorded a 0.55 ERA (one earned run) with eight hits allowed, five walks and 15 strikeouts in 16 1/3 innings. "I've got my confidence, and my stamina's there," said Sanchez, who's 1-2 with a 5.30 ERA in five career outings against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson made seven starts after returning from Tommy John surgery last year and enters this year with the belief that his arm is stronger than it has been at any point over the past eight years.  The former A's ace returns to the Bay Area to make his season debut with the hope of prolonging his recent success against the Giants. Since going 0-3 with a 7.50 ERA against them during a three-start stretch against that extended from 2003-06, he has opposed them three times and gone 2-0 with a 3.91 ERA. He is 1-2 with a 3.86 ERA in four career starts at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: The 31-year-old will make his regular-season debut for the Giants, the fifth Major League team he has played for. Wellemeyer believes that he has regained the stuff he maintained in 2008, when he was 13-9 with a 3.71 ERA for St. Louis. He lost that sharpness, he said, by throwing too much in the 2008-09 offseason and slumped to 7-10 with a 5.89 ERA last year. Wellemeyer has started only one regular-season game at AT&T Park and owns no record in seven career appearances (including one start) against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing five earned runs in six innings against the Cubs on Opening Day, Lowe didn't get the results he was targeting after overhauling his delivery during the offseason and finding some success during Spring Training. All of the damage he incurred came courtesy of a pair of home runs. But the veteran sinkerballer was able to consistently keep his pitches down in the zone and consequently, he recorded nine groundball outs. He is 5-5 with a 3.10 ERA in 15 career starts against the Giants. But he has allowed just one run in his past 16 innings against them and 4-1 with a 2.13 ERA in his last nine starts against them.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants' ace looked every bit like the two-time reigning National League Cy Young Award winner that he is in Monday's season opener at Houston, surrendering four hits, walking none and striking out seven in seven shutout innings. Lincecum has thrived against Atlanta, posting a 5-1 mark with a 2.72 ERA in six career outings against the Braves. That included a memorable game at Turner Field in August 2008 when Lincecum, feeling discombobulated in the middle innings, began pitching from the stretch to regain his coordination and effectiveness. Somewhat surprisingly, Lincecum has been only slightly more successful at home (21-8, 2.84 ERA) than on the road (19-9, 2.97). His 90 lifetime appearances are evenly split between home and away.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami enters his second Major League season more comfortable with his surroundings and armed with a two-seam fastball that he began toying with after last year's All-Star break. The 34-year-old right-hander provided some optimism when he posted a 3.42 ERA in his final 21 starts last season. He allowed three earned runs in 5 2/3 innings when he faced the Giants in San Francisco in May and then limited them to one run in five innings during a July start against them in Atlanta. With the two-seamer, he is hoping to induce more ground balls and consequently pitch deeper into games. He pitched into the seventh inning in just six of his 25 starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: Correia is coming off a vexing loss to Arizona on Wednesday. He allowed three home runs in six innings, nearly matching the number of home runs he allowed in the second half of last season (5). Correia worked fast, got eight ground-ball outs and allowed seven hits and four runs in six innings with no walks and six strikeouts. But it was when he elevated pitches to Kelly Johnson (two home runs) and Chris Young that he got into trouble. Correia led the Padres in victories (12), innings (198) and starts (33).
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens seemed to be constructing an impressive season debut before the Cubs tallied two unearned runs during a 43-pitch fifth inning on Wednesday night. He is 1-0 with a 1.32 ERA in two career starts against the Padres. Pitching around four walks while making his most recent start against them on Aug. 25, he allowed just one earned run and worked 7 2/3 innings.

He allowed three runs on seven hits, and until walking two in the seventh inning, issued one walk to that point. This will be his third start against the Braves. Richard is 0-1 with a 5.14 ERA in two previous starts against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson's season debut was marred by the two solo homers that he surrendered during Thursday's 2-0 loss to the Cubs. This stretch dates back to Aug. 2, when the Southern California native limited the Padres to two earned runs and five hits in a victorious six-inning effort at PETCO Park.

home_pitcher_note: Latos, 22, who is considered the prized arm of the organization, allowed four runs in six innings in his first start of the season on Saturday in Denver against the Rockies and earned a no-decision in a game that lasted 14 innings. One of the home runs, a solo shot to Chris Iannetta, was considered a bad pitch, as he tried to come inside to the Rockies catcher only to have the pitch tail back out over the plate. Latos displayed a fastball in the mid-90s fastball and a changeup that ran in the 85-mph range with darting action down in the strike zone that gave hitters fits at times.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson looked dominant during Friday's season debut against the Giants.  He faced the minimum through six innings and then induced three consecutive groundouts after San Francisco put runners on second and third with nobody out in the seventh inning.   The 34-year-old right-hander has said his shoulder feels stronger than it has in the past few years. Consequently he has been able to extend it further and create better action on his pitches. away_pitcher_note: Hammel had one bad inning in which he gave up four runs Saturday night, but he pitched seven innings and received a no-decision in the Rockies' 5-4, 14-inning loss to the Padres at Coors Field. That inning featured a momentary loss of fastball command, but his fastball and slider worked the rest of the time. Hammel threw strikes on 60 of his 100 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami experienced some seventh-inning misfortunes while constructing one of the better starts of his career during Sunday's season debut against the Giants.
