Utilizing his two-seam fastball to induce 11 ground outs, Kawakami needed just 65 pitches to complete the six-inning effort. Last year, high pitch counts led him to pitch into the seventh inning in just six of his 25 starts.  Kawakami, who has posted a 3.40 ERA in his past 22 starts, will be making his first career appearance against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez faces a high standard in each outing. He went six innings and gave up two runs, one earned, in Sunday's 4-2 victory over the Padres at home, but the question is could he have gone farther. Actually, Jimenez was in shape to pitch deeper in the game until losing his location to several batters in the sixth. Still, Jimenez, who reached 100 mph early in the game, proved that he's hard to beat, even when he's not at his most efficient. He has 13 strikeouts in 12 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off the worst start of his young career, Jurrjens will look to rebound and also prove that the drop in velocity that he displayed on Monday in San Diego wasn't a sign that he's still experiencing problems with the right shoulder that plagued him at the beginning of Spring Training. While allowing a career-high eight earned runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Padres, Jurrjens struggled to command a fastball that was routinely clocked around 87-88 mph, 3-4 mph lower than normal. The 24-year-old right-hander, who had allowed two earned runs or less in 27 of his previous 35 starts, has since thrown a pain-free bullpen session. Jurrjens went 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two starts against the Rockies last year.
away_pitcher_note: Smith pitched his best game in over a year to win the series opener against the Mets in Coors Field Tuesday.  Having spent all of 2009 in the Rockies' Minor League system after coming to Colorado in the Matt Holiday trade, Smith earned his first win since his 2008 rookie campaign with the A's. He allowed six hits and two walks over seven innings while striking out eight, and raised his game from "competitive" in his first start of the season to "dominant" in the follow-up.  He was aggressive in the strike zone and he was able to locate all of his pitches, enabling him to execute his game plan and build a foundation for his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson has been inconsistent with his command while issuing seven walks and registering 14 strikeouts in the 11 1/3 innings that have encompassed his first two starts. After being doomed by a pair of solo shots in his April 8 season debut, the 23-year-old right-hander came back on Wednesday and limited the Padres to one run in six innings.   Hanson is 7-3 with a 2.54 ERA in his past 13 starts.   Two of his losses during this span have come courtesy of the Phillies, who tagged him for five earned runs in seven innings that were completed in rain-interrupted games.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick's last outing couldn't have been much worse -- 1 2/3 innings, six hits, six runs, three walks and only 23 total strikes to 14 hitters. The 25-year-old right-hander hasn't exactly secured anything since he took over for the injured Joe Blanton to start the season. Despite a solid Spring Training, Kendrick has struggled with his command and the location of his off-speed pitches. He'll be happy not to see Washington again, although Atlanta's lineup won't be any easier. With Blanton due off the disabled list shortly, Kendrick's time in the rotation is likely limited, and questions already arose about whether he would even make his next start. But the Phillies want him to be an option as a starter down the road, so they may be more patient with him.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson felt he battled a tight strike zone while issuing five walks (highest total since 2006) and allowing two earned runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Padres on Thursday. This marked the first time since Aug. 25, 2007 that he completed a start that didn't include a strikeout. As shaky as he was against the Padres, Hudson proved every bit as dominant six days earlier when he limited the Giants to two earned runs and three hits in seven innings.  The veteran right-hander went 4-2 with a 2.68 ERA in his first six career starts against the Phillies. But in his past nine starts against the reigning National League champs, he is 0-4 with a 4.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay said in Spring Training that he didn't mind being compared to Cliff Lee this season. So far the comparisons are more than a little interesting. Lee went 3-0 with a 1.13 ERA in his first three starts for the Phillies last season. Halladay has the identical record and ERA in his first three starts for the Phillies. Things figured to get a little tougher for Halladay on Wednesday, facing a Braves lineup that seems to be more potent than the lineups Halladay has faced in Washington and Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe's perfect start to the season has been aided by the fact that the Braves have scored at least seven runs in each of the first three games that he started. The veteran sinkerballer has uncharacteristically allowed three home runs in the first 17 1/3 innings that he has completed this year. He had completed 83 2/3 innings before he allowed his third homer last year. Lowe is 5-0 with a 2.08 ERA in his past six starts against the Phillies dating back to the 2006 season. In his three starts against them last year, he worked 19 2/3 innings and allowed just three earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer has been unable to avoid the big inning in his first two starts. He allowed five runs in the first inning in his last start Saturday against the Marlins, but threw five scoreless innings after that. Of course, five runs is five runs and the Phillies lost the game, 5-1. But with J.A. Happ hurting and Kyle Kendrick struggling, the Phillies really need a better effort from Moyer.

home_pitcher_note: Maine produced a no-decision in his only home start this season. In 34 starts at Shea Stadium and Citi Field in the previous three seasons, he won 17 of 26 decisions and produced a 3.56 ERA. His 38 road starts in the same period produced a 15-15 record and 4.62 ERA, and he has been ineffective in two road starts this season -- 0-1 record, 12.38 ERA and 20 baserunners in eight innings. His renewed emphasis on his fastball served him well for four innings in his most recent start, against the Cardinals Sunday, but the fourth home run against him in 14 innings essentially ended his workday. Alfonso Soriano has two home runs but no other hits in 17 career at-bats against Maine.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami proved to be effective while utilizing his sinker against the Giants during his season debut. But while opposing the more patient Rockies lineup on Saturday, he left too many pitches up in the zone and fell behind in the count too often.  The Japanese right-hander allowed four runs on eight hits in five innings against the Rockies.  He needed 103 pitches to complete the outing and just 65 pitches to complete the six-inning effort against the Giants. In five appearances (three starts) against the Mets last year, Kawakami went 1-2 with a 2.19 ERA.   His finest effort against them occurred on Aug. 20, when he limited them to one run and seven hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Niese's three starts have produced results that were respectively good, bad and indifferent. The best came most recently, Monday against the Cubs at Citi Field. It produced a no-decision though he threw five shutout innings and wasn't charged with a run until after he had been removed with two out in the sixth. The run was unearned. He struck out seven, equaling his career high. Niese has surrendered one home run in 16 2/3 innings, and that was on the road. But he is allowing more hits, 25, than he'd like. Left-handed hitters have a .364 slugging percentage in 11 at-bats against him, hardly an ample sample. Right-handed hitters' slugging percentage is .516 in 62 at-bats. He has two career starts against the Braves. One was a victory, the other a no-decision. His ERA in 12 2/3 innings against them is 3.55.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens quieted some concerns about his right shoulder on Sunday afternoon when he regained his velocity and limited the Rockies to three runs in a season-high eight innings. Just five days earlier in San Diego, he was displaying a fastball that rested between 87-89 mph and allowing a career-high eight runs in just 3 1/3 innings. His rebound effort against the Rockies was marred by solo shots in the seventh and eighth innings. But for the most part, the 24-year-old right-hander had the successful form that enabled him to allow two earned runs or fewer in 26 of his 34 starts last year. Jurrjens went 4-0 with a 1.60 ERA in his five starts against the Mets last year.

home_pitcher_note: After Pelfrey defeated the Cubs Tuesday, the Mets had won six games, and he was responsible for half the victories and the team's lone save. Pelfrey, who has pitched at least six innings in eight straight starts, hasn't allowed a run in 19 innings, equaling his longest career shutout streak. Against the listless Cubs, he surrendered merely three hits, none in the first four innings, and walked three, none in the last four. His improving cutter produced four of his six strikeouts.  He also became the first pitcher to win two starts with a save in between in a five-day period since 1988 when John Candelaria achieved that arcane feat for the Yankees. He has a 2-5 record and a 6.09 ERA in nine starts and one relief appearance against the Braves. Brian McCann has a .444 average and one home run in 27 career at-bats against Pelfrey. Chipper Jones has eight walks, two home runs, four other hits and a .333 average in 26 plate appearances against the Mets starter.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson left Tuesday night's 102-pitch effort against the Phillies frustrated by the belief that he was either tipping his pitches or proving to be too predictable. The 23-year-old right-hander allowed two earned runs in just 4 2/3 innings and one of the primary reasons he compiled a high early pitch count came via the 23 pitches the Phillies fouled. Hanson's command hasn't been as sharp as it was last year, but he still hasn't allowed more than two earned runs in any of his first three outings. During his only previous start against the Mets last year, Hanson allowed just three hits in seven scoreless innings.
summary: 2010-04-25 - Atlanta Braves @ New York Mets (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Very little went right for Lohse in his last start, and he'll be looking to correct not only location mistakes, but some questionable pitch selections from that game. Lohse typically pitches off his fastball, but in Arizona he did what's often called "pitching backward" -- working off his other pitches and then going to the fastball as a change of pace, as it were. His best start this year was at Busch Stadium, and he's consistently been a good bit better at home than on the road since joining the Cardinals in 2008, so there's reason to think he'll be just fine his next time out.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson returns to the scene of his only career home run with the hope of bouncing back from the tough-luck loss he suffered on Wednesday against Roy Halladay and the Phillies. En route to his first loss of the season, the 34-year-old right-hander compiled a high early pitch count (61 pitches through three innings) and was damaged by the two Jayson Werth doubles that led to the only two runs he surrendered in six innings. Hudson's past two outings haven't been as impressive as his season debut against the Giants. But his velocity and crispness of his breaking pitches appear to back up his belief that his surgically-repaired right arm is as strong as its been in the past five years. He is 2-1 with a 5.96 ERA in his past four starts against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: As long as nobody hits Carpenter with a pitch, he should have an excellent game. He's pitched well his past two starts after an ugly one at the end of the season's first week. The only real hiccup occurred in his last outing when he let his anger over being hit affect his concentration. Carpenter's focus is one of his most critical attributes on the mound, and when it's compromised, he's a lesser pitcher. That very rarely happens, and it's not likely to happen again in this game. Carpenter has a 6.31 ERA in seven career starts against Atlanta, but that's a much better-looking 4.20 when you only count his tenure as a Cardinal.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe has struggled to find the consistency he expected after refining his delivery and encountering some success in Spring Training. Still, with the help of strong offensive support, he did not suffer his first loss until Thursday, when he allowed the Phillies five runs -- four earned -- and six hits in five innings. Lowe has issued 14 walks and allowed opponents to post a .268 batting average in the first 22 1/3 innings he has completed this season.  Lowe is 1-6 in seven career starts against the Cardinals, and during his most recent outing against them -- on Aug. 6, 2008 -- he allowed 13 hits and eight runs in just 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia might not have been as sharp as his first two outings, and still pitched effectively enough to earn a win, if the opposing pitcher wasn't two-time reigning Cy Young Award winner Tim Lincecum. Garcia allowed seven hits, more than he allowed through his first two appearances combined, and allowed just two earned runs. Put to the test when errors were made behind him, Garcia remained composed and was able to avoid the big inning. That bodes well for the young pitcher in the future. The Giants scored two runs on errors and another on a wild pitch. The fourth scored on a dribbler to first base where the runner just beat Albert Pujols to the bag. Twice he induced double-play grounders to end innings with runners in scoring position.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami has pitched effectively in two of his first three starts, but still finds himself in search of his first win of the year. He hasn't pitched into the seventh inning yet and during his two good outings he was undone by two-run, sixth innings. Regarded as a serviceable back-of-the-rotation starter, the 34-year-old right-hander allowed three earned runs and six hits in six innings against the Mets on Friday night. This will be the first career appearance against the Cardinals for the Japanese right-hander, who has allowed opponents to hit .284 this year.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright pitched brilliantly in his last start, against the Giants, but that's been true of all four of his previous starts this year. He took a shutout into the eighth inning before giving up a couple of runs and losing to Barry Zito. He's been feeling good all year, and even without a good offspeed pitch, he was able to shut down the Giants. He hasn't allowed a home run in his past three starts and has pitched deep into all of them, going at least seven innings. He's 4-0 with a 1.50 ERA in seven appearances (four starts) against the Braves, with a .216 batting average against.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the regular season, Jurrjens allowed two unearned runs on three hits over five innings against the Chicago Cubs. In the three starts since, the righty has struggled mightily, allowing 14 earned runs in 18 innings while picking up two losses. Jurrjens has fared well against the Cardinals in his career, despite a 1-2 record, with a 2.14 ERA in 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The big right-hander has followed up his outstanding rookie season (11-4, 2.78) with a strong start to his sophomore campaign. After four starts, Hanson has a 1-2 record but an impressive 2.14 ERA and his last start was arguably his strongest. He allowed one unearned run on five hits and struck out eight in his five-inning rain-shortened complete game loss to the Mets on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Myers makes his fifth start for the Astros and is coming off his first win of the season, beating the Pirates on Sunday by allowing 11 singles and two earned runs in six innings. Myers has struggled against the Braves in his career. He's appeared in 28 games vs. Atlanta (21 starts) and is 4-9 with a 4.52 ERA. He's 3-3 lifetime at Turner Field with a 5.25 ERA in 12 games, including eight starts. He's 0-4 against the Braves since his win against them, which occurred in 2006. Myers has given up 35 hits and struck out 18 batters in 26 innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson has rebounded well from the Tommy John surgery that limited him to seven starts in 2009. The right-hander allowed two earned runs in each of his first three outings before giving up three earned runs on six hits over six innings against the Cardinals on Monday night.
away_pitcher_note: Left-hander Wandy Rodriguez was scratched from his scheduled start Friday in Atlanta because of back spasms, but is ready to go Saturday. Rodriguez said his back began giving him issues last Saturday, when he pitched 7 1/3 innings and got his first win of the season by beating Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe struggled in four of his first five starts and has seen his ERA rise steadily since limiting the Giants to one earned run over six innings in his April 10 start. On Tuesday against the Cardinals, the 36-year-old right-hander allowed five earned runs on five hits over 5 2/3 innings with four strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Norris was roughed up in his last start, Tuesday against Cincinnati, allowing six hits, five earned runs and four walks in five innings. This will be his 15th career start and 16th appearance in a Major League game. He's 7-5 with a 4.79 ERA since he joined the Majors late last year and has struck out 77 batters and allowed 78 hits in 73 1/3 innings. Norris has never faced the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez, who tossed seven-plus innings of one-run ball against the Cubs on Tuesday, entered the season on a mission: He had a lot to prove because he felt teams had forgotten about him this past offseason. Hernandez didn't sign with Washington until Feb. 24 and wasn't happy that other free agents signed before him. It didn't help that he was coming off a season in which he was a combined 9-12 with a 5.44 ERA for the Mets and Nationals. Hernandez said that he was still recovering from a right knee injury that he suffered back in 2005. For the next four years, Hernandez never went on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami hasn't yet lived up to the expectations he produced while posting a 3.42 ERA in his final 21 starts last year. While he hasn't allowed more than four runs in any of his first four starts, he has been unable to provide a solid outing since proving efficient during a 65-pitch, six-inning, season debut against the Giants.   High pitch counts have prevented Kawakami from pitching beyond the sixth inning in any of his past three starts.  He issued four walks and surrendered five hits in just 4 1/3 innings against the Cardinals on Wednesday. Kawakami went 1-1 with a 5.28 ERA in three starts against the Nationals last year.

home_pitcher_note: Atilano had another solid outing, and it helped the Nationals edge the Cubs, 3-2, at Wrigley Field on Wednesday afternoon. He lasted six innings and gave up two runs on six hits. It marked the seventh straight game in a which a Nats pitcher had a quality outing. Atilano showed that he could get out of tough jams in a big way. In the fifth, Chicago had the bases loaded with one out, but Marlon Byrd popped up to first baseman Adam Dunn, and Mike Fontenot hit a ground ball to Dunn, who threw to Atilano for the third out of the inning.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his strongest outing of the season, Hanson will look to continue his dominance against the Nationals. While going 2-0 with a 2.28 ERA in four starts against them last year, the 23-year-old right-hander surrendered just one earned run in three of those outings. While pitching a season-high eight innings on Friday night, Hanson allowed the Astros just two runs and utilized an aggressive approach that helped him  throw first-pitch strikes to 22 of the 28 batters he faced. High pitch counts had prevented Hanson from pitching into the seventh inning in any of his previous four starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: After Olsen gave up six runs in two innings against the Rockies in an early season game, it looked as if his season was headed south. But over the last two games, he's shown that there's plenty of productivity remaining in his left arm. He's pitched a combined 13 shutout innings against the Dodgers and Marlins to drop his ERA to a more respectable 4.36. Six of those innings came last Friday at the Marlins as the Nationals finished their most successful April since the franchise moved from Montreal, and gave Olsen his first victory over his former team. Olsen understands well that he does not have the consistent velocity to be a strikeout pitcher, so he thrives mainly when he can mix up his pitches and keep the ball down in the strike zone. He also knows he must use his offspeed pitch in surprise situations. That's been the formula that's worked so well for the last two games.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson battled through some early discomfort with his mechanics and off-speed pitches before righting himself and limiting the Astros to just one run in 6 2/3 innings on Saturday. The veteran right-hander retired 10 of the final 12 batters he faced and would have pitched longer had he not been affected by some of the cramping issues he occasionally experiences amid humid settings.   Hudson is 8-1 with 1.55 ERA in 13 career starts against the Nationals. He has allowed one run or fewer in 10 of these outings and the only outing that he surrendered more than two runs came on July 18, 2008, five days before he was sidelined by the elbow discomfort that forced him to undergo Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer benefitted from an offensive outburst against Johan Santana and the Mets, but he pitched solidly enough to earn his third win of the season --- six innings, five runs on six hits. He gave up two early home runs, including a 3-run shot by David Wright in the first inning, and his struggles this season have typically been caused by one or two bad innings in his starts. If he can avoid that, his numbers may turn around. The 47-year-old left-hander is 5-9 with a 5.18 ERA in his career against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe ended a two-game losing streak on Sunday, when he limited the Astros to one run and six hits in five innings.  The 36-year-old sinkerballer has benefited from the fact that the Braves have scored seven or more runs in four of his first six starts. During his April 22 start against the Phillies, Lowe surrendered five runs -- four earned -- in five innings. A botched double play hurt him during a three-run, third-inning that evening.  Over the course of his past four outings, Lowe has allowed opponents to hit .282 and compile a .333 on-base percentage.  He is 4-0 with a 1.60 ERA in five career starts at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton came off the disabled list and pitched well against St. Louis on Monday, until three runs in the seventh spoiled his night. The right-hander, who started the year on the DL with a strained oblique, threw 94 pitches and allowed 10 hits, four runs, one walk and four strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings. The numbers are misleading -- Blanton had allowed only one run through six innings before a pinch-hit home run by Nick Stavinoha opened up the scoring. He went 1-1 with a 5.23 ERA in five starts against Atlanta last season.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen was assigned this spot start on Wednesday after Jair Jurrjens was placed on the disabled list. Medlen, who allowed two earned runs and four hits in the 2 1/3 relief innings he worked during an April series against the Phillies, will be making his first start since July 12. The versatile reliever threw a season-high 44 pitches during a three-inning appearance against the Cardinals on April 29. The Braves are hoping that Medlen will be able to complete four or five innings before reaching an assigned pitch count that will likely rest between 70-75.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels answered more than a few questions with his dazzling start against St. Louis on Tuesday, in which he took a 1-0 lead into the ninth inning. He gave up the game-tying RBI double and was replaced without receiving a decision, but it was a dominating performance in a tight game. He struck out eight with two walks and eight hits allowed. Hamels had his best velocity in years, and he mixed in his cutter and curveball effectively. He had struggled in previous starts to find consistency, but has battled against aces Adam Wainwright and Tim Lincecum his past two starts. He had 18 strikeouts of his last 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami will be looking to notch his first win of the season while facing a potent Phillies offense that he handled in successful fashion last year. During the two starts he made against the reigning National League champs, the Japanese hurler went 1-0 with a 3.65 ERA. Unfortunately, Kawakami has been able to build upon the promise he created during the latter part of the 2009 season. He has allowed opponents to hit .298 and compile a .342 on-base percentage against him this year.

home_pitcher_note: It took him six starts and nearly a month, but Doug Davis finally notched the first win of his second tour of duty with the Brewers. He held the Dodgers to three runs in 5 1/3 innings on Wednesday, and the Brewers scored some late insurance runs for an 11-3 win that was closer than the final score indicated. Davis continues to be plagued by some bad luck; opponents are batting .452 against Davis on balls in play this season. The Major League average is in the neighborhood of .300.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson has spent the early portion of this season learning that opposing hitters are taking an aggressive approach against him early in the count. After allowing three earned runs in the first two innings against the Nationals on Wednesday night, the 23-year-old right-hander displayed better command and surrendered just one more run in the six-inning effort. Hanson allowed three two-run homers in his Major League debut against the Brewers last year. He went 0-1 with a 5.54 ERA in two starts against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was one out away from a tough-luck loss in Los Angeles on Thursday before his Brewers teammates bailed him out. He lasted only five innings, but allowed only one earned run, and that without the benefit of a hit. Bush walked the leadoff hitter for the second straight game, then issued another walk before Dodgers first baseman James Loney cashed in with a sacrifice fly. Two unearned runs scored in the second inning before Bush cruised through three more innings. He has been very good in his career against the Braves, going 1-0 with a 1.71 ERA in three starts, with 14 strikeouts in those games versus two walks in 21 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has allowed two earned runs or fewer in five of his first six starts and limited opponents to a .226 batting average. The veteran right-hander's seven-inning effort against the Nationals on Thursday was marred by a pair of solo home runs. By pitching into the seventh inning in each of his past three outings he has provided further indication that he has recovered from the Tommy John surgical procedure that sidelined him most of last year. Hudson is 2-1 with a 2.90 ERA in four career starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: If it's a sunny afternoon and the shadows are in play at Miller Park for this game, Gallardo could be very tough. He has reached double-digit strikeouts in three of his last four starts -- the first Brewers pitcher ever to do so -- and has won all four of those outings, most recently a 3-2 win in Arizona on Friday in which Gallardo struck out 10 batters in five innings. The Braves, of course, were the Brewers' opponent on a sunny day in May 2004, when Ben Sheets used a glare-aided curveball to notch 18 strikeouts, a franchise record.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe certainly looked distressed after allowing the Phillies seven runs and 11 hits in five innings on Friday. The veteran right-hander entered this season with the hope that his offseason adjustments would allow him to avoid the frustration he experienced during the latter portion of the 2009 season. But his stats through the first seven starts of this year look very similar to the ones he posted during his last nine outings last year. Opponents have compiled a .293 batting average and .371 on-base percentage against him. He is 3-1 with a 3.25 ERA in seven career starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Last time out, Kawakami took his sixth straight loss to open the season, allowing five runs on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings at Philadelphia. Kawakami has struggled to an 0-6 record with a 6.17 ERA through his first six starts of 2010, allowing at least two earned runs in each of his starts. Kawakami's best start was his first, but he did not receive enough run support in the Braves' 6-3 loss at San Francisco on April 11. In one previous career start against Arizona, Kawakami took the loss. He went just five innings, allowing three runs on five hits while striking out four and walking one.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has been the team's best starter over the last month and has gone 2-1 over his last four starts with an ERA of 2.43. He has been more aggressive in the strike zone and throwing all of his pitches with command (11 walks in 44 innings). It's the first stretch of success for Kennedy at the big league level since 2007, when he had an ERA of 1.90 in three starts for the New York Yankees. He developed a two-seam fastball during Spring Training to go along with his sinking four-seamer. Kennedy was supposed to be the lesser-known quantity in the blockbuster three-team trade in the offseason with Edwin Jackson being the dependable innings eater, but Kennedy, who took the loss on Saturday against Milwaukee in his last outing despite giving up two earned in seven innings, has been the more consistent of the two.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson's last outing was one of the best in his young career as he matched a career-high with eight scoreless innings while striking out eight and giving up just four hits. With the win, Hanson improved to 3-2 on the year with a 2.30 ERA. Hanson has been the Braves' most consistent starter this season, pitching at least five innings in all but one start and allowing two runs or fewer in six of seven. His worst start came just prior to the one in Milwaukee, when he allowed four runs on nine hits in six innings against the Nationals. In one career start against the D-backs, Hanson is 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA, allowing two runs on six hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander has pitched well and should have a few more wins if it weren't for a leaky bullpen. He has gone seven innings in three starts, giving up two earned in two of them, and is 0-1 in those three outings. Overall has four starts with two earned runs or fewer, but he is just 1-1 in those games with the victory coming in his first start of the season against Pittsburgh. Lopez, pitching for his fifth organization since making his big league debut with San Diego in 2000, is a hard-nosed pitcher in that he doesn't have overpowering stuff but he never gives into hitters and battles like it is the last time he will ever pitch in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson was not especially sharp in his last outing, when he tied a career high with six walks over six innings. He did earn the win, however, improving his record to 3-1 on the season and lowering his ERA to 2.64 after allowing just one run on six hits. The right-hander continued his strong start to the 2010 campaign, which has seen him allow no more than three runs in his first seven starts. In six career starts against the D-backs, Hudson has been dominant, going 4-0 with a 1.61 ERA. He has allowed just nine runs -- eight earned -- on 34 hits in 44 2/3 innings against the D-backs.

Lowe produced one of his finest starts of the season on Wednesday, when he limited the Brewers to two runs in six innings. It marked the first time that he has completed six innings since April 10. The veteran sinkerballer has gone 2-3 with a 6.41 ERA in his past five starts. Opponents have hit .309 and reached base at a .358 clip against him during this span. Lowe went 2-1 with a 6.94 ERA in five starts against the Mets last year. This ERA was damaged on Aug. 18, when he allowed them eight earned runs in just 3 2/3 innings. He surrendered three earned runs or fewer in each of the other four outings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey did not reach the sixth inning for the third time in his last four starts Wednesday against the Nationals. He struck out the side in order in the first inning, but never looked comfortable on the mound after that, settling for his second consecutive no-decision. The Braves are next on the schedule for Big Pelf, a team he beat on April 25, 1-0. Pelfrey didn't allow a run against Atlanta, but five walks accelerated his pitch count and he was out of the game after the fifth inning. He is 3-5 with a 5.58 ERA for his career against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Medlen will be making his second start of the season in place of the injured Jair Jurrjens.  During his first start, the versatile right-hander limited the Phillies to one run and nine hits in 4 1/3 innings. He managed to throw 88 pitches, despite the fact that he hadn't thrown more than 44 in any of his previous 12 relief appearances this year. Medlen has shown good control while recording 19 strikeouts and issuing three walks in 22 innings. This will be his first career start against the Mets. In four career relief appearances against them, he has worked 6 1/3 scoreless innings and surrendered six hits.
away_pitcher_note: Featuring one of his better changeups of the season, Santana held the Marlins to one unearned run last Wednesday in Miami, allowing six hits and striking out five. But Marlins starter Josh Johnson matched him pitch for pitch, preventing Santana from earning a decision. He will look to earn his first victory in four starts this Tuesday in Atlanta, a place that has treated him kindly over the years. In three career starts at Turner Field, Santana has a 1.71 ERA. He was 1-2 with a 1.33 ERA overall against the Braves last season.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami is still looking for his first victory of the 2010 campaign after again coming up short on Friday night against the D-backs. Although Kawakami recorded a season-high seven strikeouts, he lasted just 4 1/3 innings, tied for his shortest outing of the year. Kawakami's struggles have only increased recently. In his last four outings, he has pitched just 20 1/3 innings with an ERA of 6.64. High pitch counts have prevented Kawakami from lasting more than 6 2/3 innings this season. Still, he hasn't been afforded much help offensively from his teammates. In Kawakami's six losses, the Braves have not scored more than three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Harang was a 4-3 loser to the Cardinals on Friday and ended his quality-start streak at three. While the right-hander didn't have a great outing, he wasn't lousy, either. His downfall was a pair of two-run homers by Albert Pujols and Ryan Ludwick -- both were wall-scrapers that barely cleared the fence in right field. For the game, Harang gave up four earned runs on eight hits over six innings, walking two and striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson will look to rebound against Cincinnati after allowing a season-high five runs against the D-backs on Saturday. Most of the damage came during a four-run fifth inning -- the most runs Hanson has allowed in an inning since the sixth inning of his Major League debut. Hanson surrendered just one other run in the six innings he completed on his way to a season-high 10 strikeouts. The 23-year-old righty has pitched into the seventh inning in three of his past four outings. During his past four starts, he has recorded 30 strikeouts and walked just three.
away_pitcher_note: Leake is the first Reds pitcher to begin his big league career 4-0 wince Santo Alcala and Pat Zachary in 1976. He has six quality starts in seven games this season. In a 4-3 win over the Cardinals on Saturday, the 22-year-old gave up two earned runs and four hits over six innings, walking three and striking out five. Leake used his fastball early and threw strikes against the aggressive St. Louis hitters but then altered his game plan ahead of their adjustments and came back with more offspeed pitches later in the game. "He's a crafty pitcher," Cardinals second baseman Skip Schumaker said. "He kept the ball down, he used all his pitches and he was very effective because he changed speeds. When he had to, he made pitches to get out of the inning. There's a reason why he skipped the Minor Leagues."

home_pitcher_note: The bullpen took away what should have been Ohlendorf's first win of the season on Sunday. Ohlendorf was quite efficient, needing only 69 pitches to get through six innings. However, manager John Russell pulled the right-hander when he issued a four-pitch walk to lead off the seventh. Ohlendorf said he could have gone longer, but the six-inning start was still the longest of his three this year. He limited Chicago to one run on four hits and three walks. Ohlendorf allowed three runs on eight hits in six innings against the Braves last year in his first career start against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: The month of May couldn't be going much better for Hudson. The right-hander has accumulated three wins with a dominating 1.63 ERA in 27 2/3 innings. In his most recent effort on Sunday against the D-backs, the 34-year-old produced a pitching masterpiece, allowing one run and three hits while striking out six. After walking six batters against Washington on May 11, Hudson maintained his control on Sunday afternoon -- surrendering just one base on balls. Even Hudson's bat has been sizzling more than usual lately. In May, Hudson has been hitting .364, (4-for-11), with two doubles.

home_pitcher_note: Just as Morton looked to be finding a groove, the right-hander took a step back in his outing on Monday. Yes, he was pitching against a potent Phillies lineup in a hitter-friendly park, but that doesn't excuse Morton from still serving up too many hittable pitches. The right-hander continues to have a hard time getting out of jams and has been prone to giving up a big inning in most of his losses this year. Half of his eight starts have now ended in four or fewer innings. Morton, who was drafted by the Braves in 2002, will be making his second career start against his former team. His first, which came last June, lasted just one inning due to a tight hamstring.
away_pitcher_note: With Lowe no longer relying as much on his sinker, the quality starts are beginning to pile up. In his last two starts, the 36-year-old has pitched 13 innings with a 3.46 ERA. During his first seven, he worked 38 innings with a 6.46 ERA. But after surrendering seven runs in five innings during a May 8 start against Philadelphia, the righty knew he needed to switch up his pitching. He completed an effective six innings of two-run ball in his next start against Milwaukee and followed that with three runs in seven innings against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Duke shook off a six-game winless streak to pick up his third of the season in a solid six-inning effort against the Phillies on Tuesday. Pitching against one of the league's more formidable lineups and in one of the more hitter-friendly parks, Duke limited Philadelphia to one run and came up with some big pitches when he needed to late in his outing. The left-hander found his sinker to be a reliable pitch throughout the night and likely would have pitched deeper if he hadn't needed 45 pitches to get through the fifth and sixth. Duke is 2-3 with a 4.43 ERA in seven career starts against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen's matchup with Johan Santana on Tuesday may have looked like a mismatch on paper, but the 24-year-old righty more than held his own, completing 6 1/3 innings of two-run, two-hit ball. Although Medlen has started just two games this season as a fill-in starter for the injured Jair Jurrjens -- who will be out until late June -- he has continued to excel in his transition from the bullpen. Manager Bobby Cox has been cautious while stretching Medlen out, as he hurled 88 pitches against the Phillies on May 8 before throwing 90 on Tuesday night. Still, even in limited action -- including his time as a reliever -- Medlen hasn't surrendered more than two runs in an outing this year.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander was at his best in his last start, tossing seven shutout innings at St. Louis on his way to a victory. Sanchez scattered four hits and threw a season-high 119 pitches. He walked two and struck out a season-best eight. At home, the right-hander has struck out 22 and walked six in 25 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: A bullpen implosion prevented Kawakami from picking up his first win of the season, but even more concerning news was a second blister on his right foot and a strained back. Still, Kawakami believes he will make his next scheduled start and will look to build upon his second-longest outing of the season, in which he completed six shutdown innings against the Reds on May 19. Kawakami was 1-3 with a 5.90 ERA (12 earned runs in 18 1/3 innings) against Florida last season.

home_pitcher_note: Slow start. Stronger finish. That basically sums up Robertson's last start. Unfortunately for the left-hander, he gave up four runs in the first two innings of his previous outing. While he rebounded with four straight scoreless frames, he was on the losing end at St. Louis. Robertson is 2-2 with a 3.91 ERA in four May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson was bailed out by a historic comeback Thursday, when he failed to make it out of the second inning after eight of the 16 batters he faced scored. His ERA ballooned from 2.88 to 4.18 in what turned out to be a 10-9 Atlanta win. In his only career start at Sun Life Stadium last Sept. 3, Hanson tossed five innings of two-hit ball, giving up just one run before the Atlanta bullpen collapsed in an 8-3 loss. That came just 12 days after the 23-year-old's only other career start against the Marlins, when he struck out seven hitters in seven innings and gave up three runs on four hits. Hanson was the winner of that 4-3 contest.

home_pitcher_note: Erase what happened in Chicago and move on. That's what Nolasco said he would do after allowing eight runs in 5 1/3 innings against the White Sox. It was the most runs he's allowed since yielding a career-most 10 runs on Aug. 12, 2009 vs. the Astros. Nolasco chalked the game up as making some mistake pitches that the White Sox didn't miss.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has been dominant this month, going 4-0 over five starts and 35 2/3 innings with an ERA of 1.26. The right-hander continued his dominance Friday in Pittsburgh, allowing just three hits over eight innings in a 7-0 Atlanta win. Hudson has even been flashing his bat, recording five hits this month and driving in a run during each of his last two outings. The 34-year-old is 6-1 with a 2.67 ERA in nine career starts at Sun Life Stadium, where he last pitched Sept. 1, a 4-3 Braves win that saw him go 5 1/3 innings, giving up two runs off six hits while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Three weeks ago, on May 7, Lowe surrendered more runs in a game than he had since Aug. 18 of last season. The righty sinkerballer conceded seven runs and 11 hits against the Phillies and decided it was time for a change in his pitching approach. Since then, in his past three starts, the 36-year-old has averaged six innings, five hits surrendered and an overall ERA of 3.50.  Lowe is still struggling at times with high pitch counts -- throwing 99 pitches in five innings during his latest outing against the Pirates -- and has yet to complete more than seven innings in a start this season.
away_pitcher_note: Duke had another terrific outing Sunday, giving up no earned runs over seven innings while striking out five and walking none in the Pirates' 3-2, 10-inning win over the Braves. That came on the heels of going stride-for-stride with Roy Halladay in a win over Philadelphia. Over his past two outings, the southpaw is 1-1 with a 0.69 ERA. Duke is 1-0 lifetime with a 4.00 ERA in four starts at Turner Field, though his most recent outing in Atlanta, last June 8, did not go smoothly. The 27-year-old was taken deep three times, giving up six earned runs on 11 hits and getting the no-decision in a 7-6 Pittsburgh loss.

home_pitcher_note: Making just his third start of the season Sunday in Pittsburgh, Medlen pitched strongly before running into trouble in the sixth inning, giving up two earned runs and walking away with a no-decision in the Braves' 3-2, 10-inning loss. Medlen struck out two and walked none, giving up seven hits and hitting one batter. The right-hander got the win in relief against the Pirates last June 8 at Turner Field, tossing three shutout innings and allowing just one hit while striking out three. The 24-year-old is 1-0 with a 2.08 ERA against the Pirates in his two career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Burres' wildness caught up to him against the Reds on Monday, when he allowed four walks, five hits and five runs (four earned) in a 7-5 loss at Cincinnati. On the season, he's struck out 23 and walked 21 -- not a great ratio -- and his ineffectiveness led him to walk the first two batters of what would become a five-run inning that knocked him out of the game in the fourth. Afterward, Burres said he lost the feel of the ball, and, considering he was doing all he could just to get the ball across the plate, he knew he was in trouble with his first pitch of the fourth inning.

home_pitcher_note: After another misfortunate start against the Marlins on May 25, Kenshin Kawakami became the first Braves starter to lose his first seven decisions to start a season since 1985. Recently, however, it's been more tough luck than anything. Against the Diamondbacks on May 14 and against the Marlins on Tuesday, the righty was afforded little run support. And in his best chance for a win, against the Reds on May 19, the Braves bullpen faltered. The 34-year-old has an ERA of 3.31 in his past three starts and hasn't surrendered more than five runs in an outing this year.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Maholm was fantastic, allowing just six hits and no runs in seven innings against the Reds in a game the Pirates eventually won, 2-1. Maholm left with the lead, but Pittsburgh's bullpen couldn't hold it and he got the no-decision. Afterward, he called himself effectively wild, but he was also efficient, tallying 89 pitches in seven innings. Against the Braves, Maholm has performed quite well in his career. He's only 1-1 in four starts, but he's allowed only four runs in 27 innings (a 1.33 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Other than conceding a career-high eight runs in just 1 2/3 innings against the Reds on May 20, Hanson has had electric stuff this season. In fact, if that forgettable outing is factored out, the 23-year-old righty has a 2.89 ERA. Further, he has completed at least six innings in five of his past six starts and hasn't walked more than five batters in an outing all season. This control has enabled Hanson to develop into one of the NL East's most dependable starters. Against the Marlins during his last start, this efficiency was on full display in a six-inning, 89-pitch outing.
away_pitcher_note: It might just be a coincidence. It might not be. But one thing is certain through Joe Blanton's first five starts this season: He looks like Cy Young through the fifth inning before imploding after that. He has a 1.80 ERA (five earned runs in 25) innings in the first through fifth innings this season. He has a 14.46 ERA (15 earned runs in 9 1/3 innings) in the sixth and seventh innings. Blanton needs to be able to pitch deeper in games, regardless of the reason. He gets a chance against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson wanted to come out for the fifth inning on May 27 against the Marlins. So what if there had just been a 77 minute rain delay? The 34-year-old has been nearly unhittable in six starts this month. He's won four and has a stunning ERA of 1.59. Take away his rain-shortened start against the Marlins, and the righty has thrown at least six innings in each of his five other starts this month. Hudson matched that six-inning plateau against the Phillies on April 14, but also allowed two runs -- giving him the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lost in the midst of a scoreless streak that reached three whole games after Thursday's loss to the Mets was another solid outing by Hamels, in which he gave up three runs (only two earned) in 6 1/3 innings. Hamels had a chance to give up just one earned run in seven innings, but Placido Polanco bobbled a chance at turning an inning-ending double play in the seventh, which put runners on first and second with one out and eventually allowed two runs to score. In five May starts, Hamels is 3-1 with a 2.45 ERA. In his only game against the Braves this season, the 26-year-old gave up three runs in five innings on May 9.

home_pitcher_note: Evidently, something changed for Derek Lowe and his pitching approach after his last start against the Phillies on May 7. On that day, the 37-year-old sinkerballer surrendered seven runs and 11 hits in five innings. Afterward, Lowe admitted to relying on his go-to pitch, the sinkerball, way too much. He vowed to make changes, and recently, things couldn't be going much better for him. Since his disappointing outing against the Phillies, Lowe has won three of four starts with a 2.88 ERA. He's completed seven-inning starts on two occasions and has kept his pitch count below triple digits each time.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick wasn't hit particularly hard early, but he still struggled to get through his first three innings, as he needed 67 pitches to get into the fourth. Charlie Manuel said Kendrick's main problem is that he needs to establish a better tempo on the mound, something the Phillies' skipper told him in the middle of this start. Kendrick apparently paid attention. The 25-year-old started to get going after the third, as he retired 10 of the last 11 batters he faced and finished giving up just two unearned runs in six innings. The two runs came when Kendrick short-armed a throw to first on a soft grounder in the first inning. Kendrick has yet to record a quality start in back-to-back outings despite having three previous chances to do so this year.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda has taken losses in his past two outings, but his most recent start on Saturday against the Rockies was his worst of the season. He lasted four innings and allowed five runs on 10 hits, walking one but also striking out just one. Kuroda has owned the Braves in two career starts, allowing two runs and eight hits with four walks and 10 strikeouts in 15 innings. Pitching at home hasn't made much of a difference to Kuroda this season: his ERA is 3.62 at Dodger Stadium and 3.48 on the road, with five starts made at each.
away_pitcher_note: With Braves pitcher Jair Jurrjens out until late June with a strained left hamstring, Medlen has continued to be invaluable in his switch from the bullpen to the rotation. In four starts, the 24-year-old has an ERA of 3.25 while completing 22 1/3 innings. Manager Bobby Cox has stressed the need to stretch out Medlen's pitch count, and thus far, the right-hander has hovered close to 95 pitches. Medlen hasn't been overpowering with his repertoire of pitches -- instead preferring to let opposing batters put the ball in play. However, the righty did have a season-high six strikeouts against the Mets on May 18.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw's ERA going into May 9 was 4.99. He's lowered it to 2.95, and though his last start -- two runs in five innings to the Rockies on Sunday -- wasn't his best, Kershaw had turned in four straight quality starts previous to it. His 72 strikeouts have him close to the league lead, and he struck out 10 Braves in the only start he ever made against them on Aug. 8, 2009. He went seven scoreless innings and allowed two hits and one walk in a game the Dodgers lost, 2-1.
away_pitcher_note: After becoming the first Braves pitcher to lose his first seven starts to begin a season since 1985, Kawakami once again look poised to earn his first victory of the year against the Pirates on May 30. But after allowing a game-tying two-run home run in the seventh inning, Kawakami again left with a no-decision. Still, the 34-year-old has performed extremely well lately. In his past three starts, the right-hander has completed 18 2/3 innings with a 2.41 ERA. Kawakami hasn't won since last Aug. 31, but his start against the Pirates tied his longest outing of 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Even when things have gone badly for Billingsley lately, they've gone well. He gave up three home runs in the first two innings on Monday, but the D-backs took away only four runs from them. Billingsley settled in and went a season-high eight innings without allowing another run, and in all-or-nothing fashion, struck out the side in the first and second innings. He finished with 11 strikeouts, another season high. He took a no-decision that game after winning his last four in a row and five of his previous six. Billingsley had an even 3.00 ERA in six May starts, and struck out 38 batters to 10 walks.
away_pitcher_note: After issuing three walks and throwing half of his first 38 pitches for balls during the first two innings of Monday's game against the Phillies, Hanson couldn't figure out what was wrong with his pitching mechanics. Teammate, roommate and fellow starter Kris Medlen told Hanson to raise his arm and stay on top of the ball. The 23-year-old right-hander did and completed 6 2/3 innings, allowing one run and just three hits. Overall, though, the month of May was a struggle at times. Hanson started six games and completed 35 1/3 innings, conceding 35 hits with a 5.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Ely's success has been mystifying, and it's been nothing but consistent. The rookie right-hander has gone at least seven innings in his last two outings and three of his last four. His last start was a showdown with Dan Haren, where Ely tossed seven shutout innings and allowed just two hits and two walks and struck out five. He didn't get a decision in that game, and took a loss in his previous outing, where he allowed just one run to the Cubs but the Dodgers scored none. The opposition has a .267 batting average on balls put in play, the lowest BABIP against any Dodgers starter aside from Carlos Monasterios, who's more of a fill-in anyway. So there could be some luck involved for Ely -- but it hasn't run out yet.
away_pitcher_note: Even with a second straight start being interrupted by a rain delay, Tim Hudson still couldn't be stopped. The 34-year-old starter won his fifth straight outing, completing six innings while allowing five hits and two runs against the Phillies on Tuesday. Even more remarkable, the right-hander hasn't conceded more than three runs in any start this season. If not for rain hampering a start in Florida, Hudson's shortest outing of the year would be 5 2/3 innings. And since May 1, Hudson has been nothing short of incredible. He has a 5-0 record in 45 2/3 innings with a 1.79 ERA. Heck, Hudson even has a five-game hitting streak.

home_pitcher_note: Haren gave a gutty performance his last time out against the Dodgers when he threw a career-high 126 pitches while holding Los Angeles scoreless for eight innings. The right-hander, though, came away with no decision after Matt Kemp hit a walk-off homer for the Dodgers in the 10th. Prior to the start, Haren had struggled mightily. In his start prior that he allowed eight runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Rockies, So far in 82 innings, he has allowed 16 homers.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe is coming off his best start of the season, an eight-inning, one-run performance against the Phillies on Wednesday, and has won four of his last five starts, including the last three straight. He also struck out a season-high seven in his last start. Lowe was walking batters at nearly the same rate he was striking them out, but he seems to have gotten a handle on that the last two starts. Going into his second-to-last start, a seven-inning, one-run game against the Pirates on May 28, Lowe had 33 strikeouts and 28 walks. He's struck out nine and walked two since.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson enters his 13th start of 2010 coming off his best outing thus far. Last Wednesday, the D-backs' No. 2 starter shut out the Dodgers for nine innings. He allowed just three hits and struck out six but didn't factor into the decision. After a rough start with his new club, the right-hander is 2-1 with a 2.27 ERA over his last four starts. Seeking continued success, Jackson makes his first start against the Braves. In two career relief appearances versus Atlanta, he yielded one run over three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen moved into the rotation from the bullpen when Jair Jurrjens went down at the end of April, but he's making a case to stay. He said he had all his pitches working the best they have all season in his last start, a career-high 7 1/3 innings at Dodger Stadium. Medlen allowed three runs, two earned, struck out four and walked none in the 4-3 win, his second straight victory. Medlen pitched well in his only career start against the D-backs in 2009, allowing four hits and one run in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has notched quality starts in six of his past seven starts, but the latest effort wasn't exactly "quality." On Friday against the Colorado Rockies, the D-backs' No. 3 starter yielded six runs on five hits over six frames. While he wasn't helped by a teammate's crucial fielding error -- hence the three unearned runs -- Kennedy did allow three Rockies home runs, the last of which put Arizona in a 6-3 hole. Kennedy admitted after the game that he missed location with his fastball at times. Because his changeup is such an integral part of his repertoire, command of the fastball is a significant indicator of Kennedy's success. He will have the opportunity to get back on track against the Atlanta Braves. In his lone career start against Atlanta on May 14, Kennedy allowed three runs (all earned) on seven hits over 6 1/3 frames; he struck out five but didn't factor into his team's decision.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami became the first Braves pitcher in 85 years to lost his first eight decisions out of the gate in his last start, against the Dodgers. But Kawakami has gone at least six innings in his last four starts, all of which which were quality starts except for the last, when he let up five runs in 6 1/3 innings. His strikeout rate is low, at about 4.5 batters per nine innings, but he has struck out twice as many (36) as he has walked (18). The D-backs roughed Kawakami up on May 14, knocking him out after 4 1/3 innings and three runs allowed. Oddly enough, he struck out a season-high seven in that game.

home_pitcher_note: In his D-backs debut Saturday, opposing the Colorado Rockies, Willis pitched into and out of trouble for six innings. What really matters: He held the potent Rockies lineup scoreless. The lefty's final line: five hits, four walks and three strikeouts. Despite the win and the ovation he received from the faithful at Chase Field, Willis appears to still have issues with his command. Forty-six of his 106 pitches landed outside of the strike zone, and his increased pitch count forced his exit. Manager A.J. Hinch said that while Willis can be "effectively wild," he had far too many three-ball counts. Willis will make start No. 2 in a D-backs uniform against the Atlanta Braves. Given his days in the National League East as a Florida Marlin, he is 6-5 with a 4.92 ERA in 18 career starts versus the Braves
away_pitcher_note: Hanson bought 40 tickets for friends and family Saturday in Los Angeles, and there were plenty more people than that in the stands when he took the mound close to home, and he didn't disappoint. Hanson tossed his third straight win and third straight quality start in a game that was, until the seventh inning, a pitcher's duel. He went six innings, allowed two runs and struck out six. Hanson hasn't lost since the D-backs beat him on May 15, when he let up five runs on seven hits in seven innings. He also struck out a season-high 10 in that game. Hanson's been much better on the road, posting a 2.19 ERA in six starts compared to a 5.40 mark in as many starts at Turner Field.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had a solid outing against Oakland last time out to bring the Twins out of a downward slide. He pitched seven innings and gave up one run on five hits. He had 10 strikeouts in that game, tying his season- best that he set on April 27 against Detroit. Liriano has been good at keeping the ball in play this season, allowing only two home runs in 11 games. He has had more success against left-handed batters, holding them to a .179 average. That is compared to his .274 average against right-handed batters. The left-hander has walked only 21 batters through 72 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson's last outing on Sunday against the Dodgers was perhaps his worst outing of the season, and still, the 34-year-old yielded only three earned runs while completing seven innings. The right-hander has been just that good during his 2010 campaign. And recently -- especially since May 1 -- you'd be hard-pressed to find a pitcher who's been better. In his last eight outings, Hudson has completed 52 2/3 innings with a 2.05 ERA. And if not for rain shortening his start against the Marlins on May 27, Hudson would have completed at least 5 2/3 innings in every outing this season.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn had a tough outing against Oakland on Sunday, preventing the Twins from recording a sweep. He gave up five runs on 10 hits through 2 2/3 innings in that game. He had no strikeouts. He has pitched a combined 6 1/3 innings in his past two starts. In his past 10 games, he has given up five runs in half of them. He has a 14.21 ERA through the first two weeks of June after finishing May with a 5.86 ERA. His strength comes in his ability to not allow walks. He has given up only 14 this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe's past start severely skewed his recent pitching numbers. In four innings against the D-backs, the righty allowed seven earned runs and eight hits. But in his previous five outings before that one, the 37-year-old was 4-1 with a 2.45 ERA. Further, the righty continued his career-long characteristic of eating up the innings -- completing 33 innings during that period. Lowe has yet to complete a scoreless outing this season, but he does have three starts where he surrendered just one run. The forgettable D-backs start and a poor showing on May 7 against the Phillies have skewed upward Lowe's ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey was impressive in his last start against Kansas City on Tuesday. Slowey pitched seven innings, giving up no runs on three hits. He put no runners on base through the first four innings. He also had three strikeouts. Slowey is 5-2 in his past 10 starts and has given up only 23 runs in that span. He has an ERA of 0.64 in two June starts and hasn't allowed more than two runs in game since his May 17 outing against Toronto, in which he gave up three. He hasn't walked more than one batter since his May 9 start against Detroit, in which he walked two.
away_pitcher_note: In his most recent outing on Tuesday against the Twins, Medlen was forced to leave early due to a left shoulder injury that occurred when he slid into home plate. Prior to his exit, the 24-year-old completed five innings while allowing four earned runs. He's continued that trend during his last five starts. In them, Medlen has completed 30 1/3 innings with a 3.86 ERA. In three of those starts, he surrendered just two runs in each. Medlen's season-high innings total is 7 1/3 innings on June 1 against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Despite completing arguably his finest performance of the season on Wednesday against the D-backs, Kawakami was still unable to pick up his first win of the season. The right-hander completed six innings of scoreless ball, while allowing just four hits. However, his string of bad luck continued, as the Braves offense was fairly futile -- scoring just one run. Still, the 34-year-old has been impressive lately. In his past five starts he has completed 31 innings with a 2.90 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Price became the first American League pitcher to win nine games with his victory against Toronto on Wednesday night. The left-hander is the fastest Tampa Bay pitcher to get nine wins and lowered his ERA to an American League-best 2.23. At just 24 years old, Price is the youngest pitcher to lead either league in wins and ERA this early in the season since 1987. Price's last start wasn't his best. He didn't have enough command of his fastball to pound the strike zone like he wanted to, but he still battled to pitch six innings and give up just one run on four hits and five walks. Price will be making his 13th start of the season Tuesday and the first of his career against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Since surrendering eight runs in what was likely the worst start of his career on May 20 against the Reds, Hanson has been throwing extremely well. His past four starts have entailed a total of 24 completed innings with a 2.63 ERA. The 23-year-old has struck out 22 batters during this stretch, as well. The only concern for Hanson right now might be his high pitch count totals. In his last three starts, he's thrown well over 100 pitches in each -- culminating with his most recent outing against the D-backs on Thursday, in which he tossed 121 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Davis bounced back from a shaky last outing with what manager Joe Maddon called his best start of the season. The young right-hander threw seven innings and pitched into the eighth inning for the first time all season against the Blue Jays on Thursday night, giving up three runs on seven hits and one walk while striking out seven batters. Davis was aggressive with his fastball, and he had excellent command over all his offspeed stuff as more than 71 percent of his pitches went for strikes. Despite the quality start, Davis became the only Rays pitcher with a losing record as Tampa Bay's lineup couldn't get enough runs across the plate. This will be Davis' first Interleague appearance of his young career.

home_pitcher_note: He hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in a start this season. And since May 1, it would be hard to find a starting pitcher hotter than Tim Hudson. The Braves right-hander has a 5-1 record and a 2.08 ERA since the calendar changed, ushering in the month of May. When Hudson has struggled, as his three starts in June might meagerly suggest, he's still been tremendous. During those past three outings, the 34-year-old has completed 21 innings with a 3.00 ERA. That ERA is still lower than anyone else's in the Braves starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Shields had his worst outing of the season Friday night against the Marlins when he allowed 10 runs on nine hits and three walks in 3 1/3 innings to take his fifth loss of the season; he has now lost his last four starts. He has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth innings. He is a master at using his fastball command to set up one of the best changeups in baseball. Shields once struggled on the road, but he is 4-2 with a 3.43 ERA in six starts away from home this season.

home_pitcher_note: After perhaps his worst start of the season, on June 7 against the D-backs, Derek Lowe emphatically rebounded in his most recent outing against the Twins on Saturday. The sinkerballer completed 7 1/3 innings, allowing six hits and two earned runs. Still, such an effort shouldn't come as too much of a surprise. In the right-hander's other forgettable start of 2010, on May 7 against the Phillies -- he allowed seven earned runs and 11 hits in five innings -- Lowe responded in his following outing. During that game against the Brewers, he conceded two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Done in by heat, humidity, bad stuff and Cincinnati bats, Bannister was hammered for 11 runs (nine earned) on 10 hits, including three homers, on Saturday night. He lasted only into the fourth inning, as his five-start winning streak came to an abrupt end. Although Bannister has been improving his ground-balls-to-fly-balls ratio this year, he's still plagued by the home run ball, giving up 14 and at least one in 11 of his 13 starts. Bannister has faced the Braves just once before, pitching one scoreless inning for the Mets in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Since making his first start in the Braves rotation on May 8 to replace the injured Jair Jurrjens, Kris Medlen has excelled. The righty has allowed as many as four earned runs just once. In the rest, he's conceded three or fewer. During the 24-year-old's most recent outing, he completed a career-high eight innings, allowing three earned runs and four hits. Manager Bobby Cox said early on that the Braves would continue to stretch Medlen out throughout his time in the rotation. But now, he can't go much further. He's worked into the eighth inning in two of his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke changed the mechanics on his windup a bit last Sunday at Cincinnati, and the results were startlingly good. He pitched a complete game, struck out 12 and won a five-hitter, 7-3. The change was a matter of bringing his glove up face-high consistently on his windup, instead of stopping lower, as he was doing on some pitches this season. Greinke got through the game on just 105 pitches (77 strikes) and looked every bit like the pitcher who won the AL Cy Young Award in 2009. His slider, normally his out pitch, and all his other deliveries were on target. He walked no one.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami has posted a 3.00 ERA in his past six starts and completed at least six innings in five of those outings. But he has suffered three losses during this stretch and stands as the only starting pitcher in franchise history to lose the first nine decisions of a season. With Jair Jurrjens on target to return from the disabled list at the end of the month, this could be one of Kawakami's last chances to prove he deserves to remain in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Although Davies was charged with six runs in three-plus innings against the Astros last Tuesday night, he escaped a loss as the Royals rallied to win. He had a tough time keeping his fastball down and the Astros teed off four five straight hits in the fourth inning, four of them within a five-pitch span. Davies gave up six hits and two walks and his ERA jumped from an already high 5.48. This will be a homecoming for Davies, who pitched for Atlanta before being traded to the Royals on July 31, 2007. He's never faced the Braves before.

home_pitcher_note: Danks will look to continue his recent success, as he has won his past two starts. In his most recent outing, a 7-2 victory against Pittsburgh, Danks allowed two runs on four hits in eight innings.  It was his ninth quality start of the season. Danks has never faced Atlanta in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Since allowing a career-high eight earned runs in 1 2/3 innings against the Reds on May 20, Hanson has gone 4-0 with a 2.03 ERA. The tall right-hander had little trouble while scattering three hits over seven scoreless innings against the Rays on Wednesday. He is 4-0 with a 0.75 ERA in four career Interleague starts, producing scoreless efforts against the Yankees, Red Sox and Rays over that span. In his seven road starts this season, Hanson has gone 4-1 with a 2.34 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In Buehrle's most recent start, he pitched strong in the White Sox's 5-4 win against Pittsburgh.  Buehrle allowed two runs on six hits with six strikeouts in 7 1/3 innings.  He left the game in the eighth inning with his team leading 5-1, and though three Pirates runs off three pitchers brought Pittsburgh within a run, the White Sox held on to deliver Buehrle the win.  Buehrle is 1-0 against Atlanta with a 3.38 ERA.  In his one matchup against the Braves, he gave up three runs on eight hits in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has seemingly regained the dominant form that he possessed for the A's during the early years of this century. The 34-year-old right-hander, who missed most of the 2009 season while recovering from Tommy John surgery, has allowed three earned runs or less in each of his past 14 starts. In his past 10 outings, Hudson has gone 6-1 with a 2.00 ERA and limited opponents to a .216 batting average. He is 3-2 with a 5.19 ERA in seven career starts against the White Sox. But in his three career starts at U.S. Cellular Field, he is 0-2 with a 13.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd is coming off one of his best starts of the season, a 2-1 White Sox victory against the Nationals on June 18.  In that game, Floyd allowed one run on four hits in eight innings.  He also had five strikeouts and one walk.  Alex Rios' RBI single in the 11th inning propelled the White Sox to a win.  In four career games against Atlanta, he is 1-1 with a 9.95 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Other than allowing two seven-run efforts in his past nine outings, the veteran sinkerballer has been fantastic on the mound. In his other seven starts during that stretch, Lowe has allowed three earned runs or fewer in each. During his last two outings, the 37-year-old has completed six innings in each while allowing just five earned runs total. Though his strikeout totals have never been extremely high, Lowe continues to have good control, walking nine batters in his past five starts combined. The right-hander leads the Braves in wins on the year.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander continues to impress and make the most of his time in the starting rotation with Jair Jurrjens out until late June with a hamstring injury. Medlen hasn't surrendered more than four earned runs -- which he did just once -- in eight of his starts this season. His past two outings were fairly respectable. In each the 24-year-old allowed three earned runs but pitched at least 6 1/3 innings, as well. Medlen is more of a contact pitcher, though during his last two starts, he did strike out five batters in each.
away_pitcher_note: A year after Detroit selected Oliver in the second round of the Draft, and mere months after Oliver began his pro career in the Arizona Fall League, the Tigers will call up the 22-year-old lefty to take over just-demoted Rick Porcello's rotation spot. With a consistent mid-90s fastball and an improving slider, Oliver steadily improved as his Double-A season continued at Erie, where he went 6-4 with a 3.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts over 77 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 2010 season has been a struggle for Kawakami, who has yet to win a game this season. He's come fairly close on numerous occasions, only to see a fluke hit or bullpen lapse derail his win attempt. But recently, the right-hander hasn't made things easy for himself. He left his past start against the Royals after just two innings, having surrendered four earned runs. In his outing before against the Rays, Kawakami allowed five runs. Before his shortened start against the Royals, the 35-year-old had thrown 100 or more pitches in each of his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: A temporary return to facing National League hitters has done a world of good for Scherzer, the former Diamondbacks rookie who has won back-to-back starts against NL foes in the past week and a half. He allowed one run on four hits over seven innings against his old squad last Sunday in Detroit. Combine that with his victory over Washington last week, and he has struck out 17 batters over his past 13 innings. Monday's off-day gives him an extra day of rest coming into this outing, which could be a blessing after he used up 118 pitches against the Diamondbacks and 112 in dealing with the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: After starting the month of June in dominating fashion during his first three outings, Hanson allowed the most runs of his career on Tuesday against the White Sox. The right-hander will look to rebound from that forgettable 3 2/3 innings in which he surrendered nine runs.
away_pitcher_note: While there wasn't much good news coming out of Verlander's drubbing by the Mets at Citi Field Tuesday, it's two-fold coming into Atlanta. First, he used up just 61 pitches before a 58-minute rain delay knocked him out with two runners on and nobody out in the third. Second, he'll be pitching on his standard four days of rest, which he says he actually prefers over an extra day because it fits his between-starts routine better. The stats support his point, especially this year: He's 5-1 with a 2.21 ERA on four days rest, 3-4 with a 5.20 ERA with any more rest than that. away_pitcher_note: Narveson has allowed only two runs in 12 career innings against the Braves. Keep an eye on leadoff man Michael Bourn, who's 4-for-8 with a walk in his previous nine plate appearances against Narveson.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly wasn't pleased with his last outing, mainly because he walked six in six innings. But he pitched well enough to earn a victory over the Astros om Friday night, allowing just one run in six innings of a 3-1 win. He struck out five.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander limited Arizona to only four hits in 7 1/3 scoreless innings in his last start. He pitched with confidence and poise, and the club hopes he can have the same approach the next time he takes the hill.
