summary: 2014-03-17 - Atlanta Braves @ Houston Astros (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo will set a club record with his fifth straight Opening Day start, one shy of Ben Sheets' mark for career Brewers openers. Gallardo is aiming to bounce back from a 2013 filled with personal and professional trials.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a stellar rookie season during which he posted a 2.81 ERA in his final 27 starts, Teheran has been given his first career Opening Day assignment. Opponents hit .199 against him in seven afternoon starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse was the Brewers' best starting pitcher in 2013 but will start the second game of 2014. After signing at the end of Spring Training last year, he led the team with 20 quality starts, a 3.35 ERA and 198 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wood flashed his tremendous potential as he posted an 0.90 ERA in five August starts last year. The 23-year-old southpaw creates deception with a funky delivery and primarily uses a knuckle curve as his secondary pitch.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers considered holding Garza for Game 4 of the season in Boston, but opted instead to maximize his starts over the season. His $50 million, four-year deal is the richest in club history for a free agent.
away_pitcher_note: Harang signed with Atlanta after being released by the Indians on March 24. After struggling through the first five months of last season with the Mariners, he posted a 3.52 ERA in four September starts with the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann was scratched from his scheduled start on Thursday because of flu-like symptoms, but was in the initial starting lineup as of Friday morning.
away_pitcher_note: After receiving a surprise promotion to Atlanta in September, Hale allowed one earned run in the 11 innings that encompassed his only two career starts. The Princeton University grad will be making his first career road start.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg fanned 10 batters, but he surrendered four runs against the Mets in his 2014 debut on Monday. He owns a 3.68 ERA in 13 career starts against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Both of the two runs Teheran surrendered during his season debut in Milwaukee came during a rocky fourth inning. The young right-hander posted a 2.25 ERA in the final four starts he made against the Nationals last year.

home_pitcher_note: Jordan makes his season debut vs. the same team he ended 2013 against, the Braves. Jordan notched a quality start vs. Atlanta last September, giving up two unearned runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wood surrendered a home run on his first pitch of the season and then did not allow another run during his stellar seven-inning season debut in Milwaukee. He showed the same promise as when he posted a 0.90 ERA in five August starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: Harang gets the start in Atlanta's home opener just two weeks after being released by the Indians. The veteran hurler provided a welcome surprise when he limited Milwaukee to two hits in 6 2/3 scoreless innings on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Though Colon technically threw a quality start in his Mets debut, it was not enough to avoid his first loss. He has only faced the Braves three times in his career, but is 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA in those games and 2-0 with a 0.64 ERA at Turner Field.

home_pitcher_note: Santana will be making this season debut exactly one month after the Braves first contacted him with the hope the veteran right-hander would replenish their depleted starting rotation. He has a 3.82 ERA in 31 career starts against NL teams.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler struck out six batters in the first three innings of his season debut against the Nationals on Thursday, but could not scratch out a victory. Next up are Wheeler's hometown Braves in Atlanta, where he made his big league debut last June.

home_pitcher_note: Hale once again displayed an effective sinker in his season debut, as he tossed five scoreless innings against the Nationals. The suburban Atlanta native has allowed one earned run through his first three career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Mejia's debut was hardly efficient, with eight strikeouts and five walks leading to 101 pitches in six innings. But the Reds only scored once off Mejia, who vindicated the Mets' decision to carry him over Daisuke Matsuzaka on the Opening Day roster.

home_pitcher_note: Despite not having a good feel for his slider, Teheran allowed just two runs and three hits over seven innings against the Nationals on Saturday. He has a 2.32 ERA in his past five starts against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Roark stepped in for a sick Jordan Zimmermann, pitching six innings and allowing two runs on six hits and striking out five in a season-debut win over the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Wood takes the hill hoping for more run support in his second start against the Nationals. He took a tough loss against Washington on Sunday despite giving up only two runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Jordan recorded a no-decision, pitching 6 1/3 innings and allowing one run on six hits in Sunday's 2-1 victory against the Braves. Jordan will face Atlanta for the second time in less than a week.

home_pitcher_note: Harang has given up just one run in his first two starts, totaling 12 1/3 innings. He faced the Nationals as a member of the Mets on Sept. 12, 2013, and struck out 10 batters in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Gonzalez pitched six shutout innings as he helped the Nationals blank the Marlins, 5-0. Gonzalez threw a lot of pitches early, but he settled down and retired the final 10 hitters before leaving the game.

home_pitcher_note: He allowed seven hits, four runs, one walk and one home run Wednesday in a loss to Milwaukee. He struck out nine Brewers, picking up eight with his changeup. The nine strikeouts were the second most of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Santana gave up only three hits in eight scoreless innings during his Braves debut, a 4-3 win against the Mets on Wednesday. His first 20 pitches against New York were strikes, setting a Major League record.

home_pitcher_note: Lee allowed eight hits, three runs and struck out eight in six innings Thursday against the Brewers. Lee didn't get the run support he needed, and therefore had to take an early exit as the Phillies needed a pinch-hitter.
away_pitcher_note: Hale struggled to command his sinker as he allowed four earned runs and lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Mets on Thursday. His sinker could prove to be a valuable weapon in the offensive-friendly Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lee allowed eight hits, three runs and struck out eight in six innings Thursday against the Brewers. Lee didn't get the run support he needed, and therefore had to take an early exit as the Phillies needed a pinch-hitter.
away_pitcher_note: Despite struggling to get a feel for his slider, Teheran has notched three straight quality starts to open 2014. Teheran owns a 5.79 ERA against the Phillies in four career outings that include three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett learned Monday he has an inguinal hernia, but he said he plans to pitch with the injury the remainder of the season. He has walked 14 in 16 innings so far, which is a ratio that must improve.
away_pitcher_note: Wood has eclipsed the 100-pitch mark in back-to-back starts but managed to give up only three earned runs in 12 innings between the two outings. He has surrendered leadoff homers in the first inning of two of his three starts.

home_pitcher_note: With a short bullpen, the Mets desperately needed length from Niese on Saturday in Anaheim. He obliged with a remarkably efficient 7 1/3 innings, needing only 96 pitches to record 22 outs.
away_pitcher_note: Harang recorded his three quality starts in three tries this season. His two earned runs allowed in his first three starts marks his best start to a season since he did the same thing as a rookie in 2002.

home_pitcher_note: Colon's last outing was one of the worst of his 17-year career. Four of the 11 hits that Colon gave up went over the fence at Angel Stadium, resulting in nine earned runs. Next up are the Braves, whom Colon shut out over seven innings on April 8.
away_pitcher_note: Santana is coming off consecutive strong starts including six innings of four-hit baseball in which he allowed one run and matched a career-high 11 strikeouts. Santana now has 12 starts in which he has reached double figures.

home_pitcher_note: Still searching for the efficiency he showed in Spring Training, Wheeler was nonetheless much better last time out in Phoenix, giving up two runs in 6 1/3 innings. He has delivered two quality starts in three tries this season, despite his 4.67 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hale struggled to command his sinker as he allowed four earned runs and lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Mets on April 10.

home_pitcher_note: After matching a career high while allowing the Nationals 10 hits on April 11, Teheran tossed a three-hit shutout against the Phillies on Wednesday. He has thrown 110-plus pitches in two of his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler stepped up and stopped the bleeding, beating the Nationals in his last outing to snap Miami's eight-game losing streak. In seven shutout innings, he allowed one hit. His 112 pitches were one shy of a personal high.

home_pitcher_note: Wood will be looking to rebound from the tough-luck loss he took while notching a season-high eight innings on Thursday in Philadelphia. He has completed at least seven innings in three of his first four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez comes off a dominating performance with a no-decision vs. Washington, striking out 10 and allowing three unearned runs in seven innings. Lifetime on the road, he is 3-7 (4.00). Against the Braves, he is 1-1, 2.08.

home_pitcher_note: Harang was lifted from Friday's start against the Mets after throwing 121 pitches over seven hitless innings. The 35-year-old veteran has carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning during two of his first four starts of this season.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi has worked at least six innings in each of his four starts. He gave up three runs (one earned) in six innings in his last outing, vs. Seattle. The right-hander is 1-1 (2.79 ERA) in five career starts at Turner Field.

home_pitcher_note: Santana has proven to be the solid addition the Braves envisioned when they signed him in March to replenish their injury-depleted rotation. His early success has been aided by the confidence he has regained in his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Following three poor starts to begin the season, Bailey turned in his first strong outing and was rewarded with plenty of help for an 8-2 win over the Cubs on Sunday. He worked six scoreless innings while scattering six hits and striking out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Hale might have earned himself one more big league start with the determination he showed during Sunday's six-inning effort in New York. Two of the three runs he surrendered came as a direct result of defensive miscues.
away_pitcher_note: Leake allowed four runs on eight hits and a walk in seven innings Monday against the Pirates. His outing was marred by one ill-fated pitch to Ike Davis, who belted a grand slam in the fourth inning.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran has spent this season's first month legitimizing his bid to become an ace. Still, he could prove to be even better as warmer temperatures provide an opportunity to gain a more consistent feel for his nasty slider.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto is on a roll with back-to-back complete games in two starts vs. the Pirates. His 21-inning scoreless streak ended Tuesday. He is the first Reds pitcher since Tom Browning in April 1994 to hurl consecutive complete games of three hits or fewer.

home_pitcher_note: Simply dominant is the best way to describe Fernandez of late. He struck out 14 Braves in a 1-0 win in his last start. His last two outings, he has given up three runs (no earned) with 24 strikeouts and no walks in 15 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wood will seek revenge as he opposes Jose Fernandez for the second time in a week. The Atlanta southpaw has worked eight strong innings in his past two starts. He'll be pitching with two extra days of rest.

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi will get a second crack at Atlanta five days after he received a no-decision against the Braves. He gave up one unearned run in six innings, recording his fourth quality start in five outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Harang continues to be one of the best stories in baseball, striking out a season-best 11 in six innings against the Marlins in his last start. His 0.85 ERA is the best by a starter in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: Alvarez has allowed just two runs in his last two starts, a span of 15 innings. The right-hander followed up a two-hit shutout against Seattle by giving up two runs vs. the Mets. He struck out four in each game.
away_pitcher_note: Santana won his third straight decision on April 25, but he struggled near the end, giving up four runs on four hits and a walk against the final nine batters he faced. He gave up a season-high nine hits and struck out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Minor will be making his much-anticipated season debut after dealing with the effects of a Dec. 31 urinary tract procedure. His 2.90 ERA since July of 2012 ranks fourth among all Major League starters.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum might prefer to don the road grays. He's 0-1 with a 6.59 ERA in three home starts, compared to 1-0, 5.25 in two road outings. Opponents are batting .333 off Lincecum, compared to .248 last year.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran has produced two of the finest starts of his young career within his last three starts. Clayton Kershaw and Jose Fernandez are the only pitchers who have bested the 2.54 ERA Teheran has produced since April 23, 2013.
away_pitcher_note: Erratic this season, Vogelsong refused to revel in his excellence last Sunday against Cleveland. "It's been back and forth," Vogelsong said. "... I'm not going to get overly excited about one good start after a really bad one."

home_pitcher_note: After completing consecutive eight-inning efforts that resulted in 1-0 losses, Wood produced one of the worst starts of his career on Tuesday. His command deserted him as he allowed the Marlins seven runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: After winning his first two decisions, he has lost three straight. He gave up five runs, four earned, in five innings in his last start, a 5-4 setback to the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Harang hopes to rebound from a rough end to an otherwise stellar April. His 0.85 ERA climbed more than two runs as he surrendered nine earned runs on 10 hits in 4 2/3 innings against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Miller won half of his April starts despite struggling to maintain consistent command of his pitches all month. Homers (seven) and walks (21) have hurt him, though Miller has found a way to still keep his club in games.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching in place of Ervin Santana, who needs a few extra days to rest a bruised thumb, Floyd will be making his first start since undergoing Tommy John surgery last year. He'll get similar spot starts until a rotation spot opens.
away_pitcher_note: Lyons is making his third start of the season after a brief stint in the bullpen. He's allowed six earned runs in 12 innings as a starter, compared to one in three innings as a reliever.

home_pitcher_note: Minor gave up two solo home runs and not much else in his season debut on May 2. He hopes to improve his command of his offspeed pitches, which he left out over the middle of the plate in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright was roughed up for the first time this season in his last start Friday against the Cubs, who snapped his 25-inning scoreless streak with a six-run outburst. He allowed more hits (10) than in his previous three starts combined (9).

home_pitcher_note: Teheran notched his MLB-best seventh quality start in seven outings in his most recent turn, taking a hard-luck loss against the Giants. He fanned seven and surrendered a season-high three earned in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hammel posted his sixth quality start, but did not get a win. He admitted to having a tough time with his command in the outing against the Cardinals, and gave up seven hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Santana returns to the mound after the Braves skipped his most recent start to give his bruised right thumb more time to heal. He recorded a quality start in his most recent turn, but walked a season-high three batters.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija is winless in his last 13 starts. In his last outing, he went nine innings vs. the White Sox, struck out seven, got a hit and scored a run. Said manager Rick Renteria: "What a great outing -- gritty, gutsy, everything you could ask for."

home_pitcher_note: Harang bounced back from a rough outing in Miami to deliver six solid innings against the Cardinals on Monday. He's allowed two earned runs or less in six of his first seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson struck out nine over seven innings and did not walk a batter vs. the White Sox. He said he was inspired by Jeff Samardzija's nine-inning effort the night before. Jackson's nine K's were the most since he fanned nine Giants on April 14, 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has been searching for consistency all season. Though the Giants are 5-2 in his starts, he has allowed four earned runs or more in three starts and three earned runs or fewer in four outings.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd exceeded expectations as he delivered seven strong innings in his first start in more than a year last Tuesday. His command was better than many other pitchers have experienced after initially returning from Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong has surrendered two earned runs in 20 1/3 innings over his last three starts. That's a 0.89 ERA, compared to 7.71 in four outings before that span. His 2.50 ERA in three home starts contrasts with his 5.30 ERA in four road assignments.
away_pitcher_note: Two solo home runs accounted for the only runs Minor surrendered in his May 2 season debut against the Giants. His two-seam fastball proved inconsistent and he struggled in two-strike counts on Wednesday against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has not yet capitalized on his pitcher-friendly home grounds. He's 1-2 with a 5.87 ERA at AT&T Park, yet has gone 3-1, 1.39 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran was at the top of his game as he allowed one hit over eight innings and retired 18 of the final 19 Cubs he faced on Friday. Solo home runs have accounted for each of the five runs he's surrendered over his past 39 innings.

home_pitcher_note: For the fourth time in eight starts this season, Lynn allowed three or more runs in an inning his last time out. It cost him a three-run lead and the Cardinals a win. He is now winless in his last four games after winning his first four.
away_pitcher_note: After getting a chance to rest a bruised right thumb that affected him in his previous two starts, Santana tossed seven scoreless against the Cubs on Saturday. He has allowed less than two runs in four of six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miller has not made a dominant start this season. Walks (27 in 44 2/3 innings) continue to be a large problem, and he has yet to pitch into the seventh inning. He gave up two runs in five innings in a start at Atlanta on May 5.
away_pitcher_note: Harang has continued to exceed the expectations that were present when he signed with the Braves on March 24. He allowed nine earned runs against the Marlins on April 30. But he's produced a 1.44 ERA in his other six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia will come off the disabled list to make his first start since May 17, 2013. He has recovered from shoulder surgery and pitched five innings in a Triple-A game Monday. He will be limited to a pitch count of about 90-95.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd has shown impressive command during the two starts he has made since returning from Tommy John surgery. Two hits recorded on 0-2 pitches doomed him as he allowed three seventh-inning runs against the Giants on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: As Minor tossed 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Giants on Tuesday, he impressed with the confidence he had in all of his secondary pitches. He had relied too heavily on his fastball in his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta has pitched even better in May than he did in April. He's allowed just three earned runs over 21 innings (1.29 ERA) with 14 strikeouts and three walks in three May starts, lowering his ERA to 2.05.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran struggled with location in his last start, a 10-4 loss to San Francisco. In his shortest outing of the season, he left the game after just 41 pitches and told reporters he had trouble finding the grip on the ball.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo has hit a rough patch his last three starts, in which he has a 5.50 ERA. Perhaps a matchup with the Braves will do the trick: he's 5-1 with a 1.79 ERA in eight career starts against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Santana is looking to rebound from his worst start of the season against the Cardinals on Friday. Command was a challenge for the right-hander and the five runs and 10 hits allowed were both season highs.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse improved to 5-1 with seven innings of three-run ball in his last start Friday against the Cubs. He allowed all three runs in the first three innings and cruised the rest of the way.

home_pitcher_note: Harang was a tough-luck loser against the Cardinals on Saturday. He pitched six strong innings and gave up three runs with only two earned. Harang was a victim of four bunt hits that led to a couple of St. Louis runs.
away_pitcher_note: Garza's first-inning struggles continued in his homecoming to Wrigley Field. He surrendered three runs in the opening frame to the Cubs on Saturday, but he retired 18 of the final 20 to finish strong over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Through his first three starts, Floyd has avoided the inconsistencies and command issues pitchers often experience when they first return from Tommy John surgery. He's limited right-handed hitters to a .194 batting average.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles had bordered on dominant for the entire season until Saturday night, when he walked a career-high eight and yielded six runs over 3 1/3 innings in a loss to the Padres. He said his control was off, no injuries or anything.

home_pitcher_note: Minor has confidently used his offspeed pitches in any count, as he has allowed just two runs in 12 2/3 innings over his past two starts. Half of the 10 runs he's allowed this year have come via home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio has become the king of the workmanlike performance this year. He gave up nine hits, including two home runs, and four in six innings Sunday at home against the Padres, but left with a lead. Colorado won in 10.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran bounced back from a rough outing to record his second shutout of the year on Tuesday. He allowed one run in seven innings against the Rockies last April to begin a 37-start stretch in which he's posted a 2.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Morales held the Giants to five hits and three runs in six innings on Tuesday night, and went blow-by-blow with Madison Bumgarner. Morales, as has been the case when he pitched well, had an effective cut fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Santana allowed more runs in his past two starts (11) than he had in his previous six starts of this season combined (9). Command issued plagued him against the Brewers on Wednesday, when he allowed his first grand slam.
away_pitcher_note: The wiry righty will try to break out of his mysterious early-season slump. This is Buchholz's first career start against the Braves. Lifetime in Interleague Play, he is 4-0 with a 4.40 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Harang has exceeded all expectations while allowing two earned runs or fewer in eight of his first 10 starts. He struggled during his stint with Seattle last year and has a 4.56 ERA in 56 starts against AL clubs.
away_pitcher_note: The ace will try to recover from a rough outing in his last start, when he gave up seven runs over the first two innings. In two career starts against the Braves, Lester is 1-1 with a 2.77 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey has been Boston's most consistent starter this season. In his last start against the Rays, he fired seven-plus shutout innings, walking one and striking out three.
away_pitcher_note: Through four starts, Floyd has thus far avoided the command inconsistencies that often plague pitchers coming back from Tommy John surgery. He has notched 24 strikeouts and issued five walks in 25 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy has been spotty of late, giving up five runs or more in his last three starts. Last time out, Peavy failed to hold a 5-0 lead and took a no decision in Boston's 15-inning loss to the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Minor has once again fallen victim to the long ball. Seven of the 13 runs he has allowed this year have come via home runs. But five of the six homers he has allowed have been solo shots.

home_pitcher_note: A rainout at Washington on Tuesday pushed Koehler back a few days. He was set to pitch Wednesday, but now faces Atlanta. His last start was a rough one. Koehler allowed seven runs on nine hits in a loss to the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing a career-high 128 pitches in his second shutout of the season on May 20, Teheran threw just 93 pitches in six scoreless innings Sunday, and has posted 15 consecutive shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: At last, Turner was able to celebrate a win. It came in his most recent start, when he threw 6 1/3 shutout innings against the Brewers. Turner had gone 17 straight starts without a win, since he beat the Braves on July 10, 2013.
away_pitcher_note: Since posting a 1.99 ERA through six starts, Santana has allowed 16 runs in his last 17 1/3 innings. He has walked seven in his past two starts after issuing nine free passes in his first seven games.

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi has won back-to-back decisions for the first time this year, having beaten the Phillies and Nationals. The right-hander goes for three straight against another division rival, Atlanta. He beat the Braves on April 30.
away_pitcher_note: Harang has posted a 3.29 ERA and 3.73 K/BB ratio this season as a pleasant surprise for Atlanta. In his last start, Harang earned a no-decision after allowing two runs on seven hits with seven strikeouts over six frames against Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd has allowed two earned runs or fewer in three of his first four starts since returning from Tommy John surgery. He found greater comfort with his changeup during last week's start against the Red Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Ramirez will be recalled from Triple-A to make the start. After a 1-0 start to 2014, Ramirez was winless in his next five outings, posting a 1-4 record with a 6.00 ERA this season. He was sent down to Triple-A after his May 7 start.

home_pitcher_note: One NL evaluator recently referred to Minor as the smartest pitcher in Atlanta's rotation. Solo home runs have accounted for most of the damage incurred by the southpaw, who has benefited from the improvement of his curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Iwakuma (3-2, 3.09 ERA) has fallen victim to the long ball (four homers allowed) in his last two outings, losing both after a strong start to May. He gave up five runs in six innings in a loss to the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy's ERA jumped from a season-low of 4.67 on May 21 to 5.20 after his last two outings, in which he gave up a combined 10 runs and 18 hits while struggling to avoid big innings.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran recorded his Major-League leading 11th quality start when he limited the Marlins to only two runs in 7 1/3 innings last Friday. Miami's two-run first snapped Teheran's streak of 15 straight scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Miley picked up the loss after giving up four home runs to the Reds in his last start, but he has also been mowing down batters. Despite a no-decision and a loss, the left-hander has struck out 20 hitters in 13 innings in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Santana put a nightmarish stretch behind him in his most recent turn, recording his first quality start since May 10. Since compiling a 1.99 ERA in his first six starts, Santana is 1-2 with a 7.83 ERA in his last four outings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has won all four of his big leagues starts this year. Last time out against the Rockies in Coors Field, he allowed just one run over six innings. He is not overpowering and his changeup is his best pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Harang has given up two runs or fewer in eight of 10 starts, a trend that falls in line with his 3.20 career ERA in 101 1/3 innings against Arizona. He walked four on Sunday after walking a combined seven in his previous seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: A 24th-round Draft pick in 2010 who has developed into a front-line pitcher at Triple-A Colorado Springs, Bergman will make his Major League debut against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd has given up three earned runs or fewer in every start, but two unearned runs off errors cost him against the Mariners on Tuesday. His 10 hits allowed, however, were his most since May 27, 2012.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio struggled with command of both his fastball and his breaking ball Thursday vs. the D-backs. He was consistently behind in the counts, and when he missed, he missed high, resulting in two homers among 11 hits and seven run in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Minor has allowed two earned runs or fewer in five of his seven starts. Since surrendering six homers in his first five starts, he has prevented opponents from going deep in his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Matzek's road has been a winding one since the Rockies selected him 11th overall in the 2009 Draft, but manager Walt Weiss believes he's ready. Matzek battled control issues in the Minors and didn't get above Class A until last year.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has produced a 1.23 ERA in the four starts he's made since allowing a season-high four earned runs on May 14. He takes his MLB-leading ERA into Coors Field, where he allowed one run in seven innings last year.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin, who missed the first month because of a right shoulder strain, found his sinker and curveball in his last start, but faltered in the seventh and was credited with six-plus innings, three runs. He wants to go deeper.
away_pitcher_note: Santana allowed just one unearned run in seven stress-filled innings on Saturday. Opponents have hit .316 with a .369 on-base percentage in his past five starts. He allowed seven runs in his only previous Coors Field start.

home_pitcher_note: While many continue to expect his magic to expire, Harang has allowed two earned runs or fewer in 10 of 13 starts. But he'll now be challenged by the Angels, who recorded 35 hits and 20 runs in 17 1/3 innings against him last year.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson will make his first career start against the Braves on Friday at Turner Field, looking to build upon a 7 1/3-inning performance on Sunday against the White Sox. Wilson won his first Interleague start this year with seven innings vs. the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd bounced back from his roughest start of the season by allowing just three hits in 6 2/3 innings at Coors Field on Monday night. He has allowed two earned runs or fewer in five of his seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Richards is on a roll in his last two starts, tossing 15 innings, allowing one run while striking out 13 and walking none. He lowered his ERA from 3.65 to 3.09, a mark in the top 10 of the league.

home_pitcher_note: Minor will be looking to rebound after matching a career-high eight runs in just four innings on Tuesday at Coors Field. The Rocky Mountain air seemed to affect his curveball, which has been a key pitch for him this year.
away_pitcher_note: Santiago earned a no decision Tuesday in his first start since being recalled. He threw six shutout innings and striking out eight A's, lowering his ERA from 4.82 to 4.15 in the process. He will start on four days rest for the first time in a month.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran ranks in the NL in ERA, innings, strikeouts, shutouts, and opposing batting average. He is out to avenge his last start -- seven earned runs and 10 hits, both season highs -- in Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: He has not allowed a run in 16 2/3 consecutive innings. He also has a 0.40 ERA (one earned run in 22 2/3 innings) in three starts this month and a 1.78 ERA (10 earned runs in 50 2/3 innings) in his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has one win and two no-decisions in his last six outings after a 4-0 start, allowing at least five runs four times. But he's had great success against the Phillies, allowing one earned run in 13 innings in two career starts.

away_pitcher_note: After allowing five home runs over his previous two starts, Nelson was a ground-ball machine against the Tigers on Tuesday, with no fly balls hit to the outfield over his final five innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will face the Braves for the first time in his seven-year career. This will be the southpaw's ninth start of the year -- his most in a season since 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Perez generated some momentum as he worked five strong innings in his first Major League start on Wednesday vs. the Rays. Along with relying on his sinker, he showed an ability to miss bats with both his changeup and curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw continues to try to work back to his Cy Young form from 2014, as he already has as many losses this year (three) as he did in last year's campaign. He's had success against Atlanta, though: Braves hitters are a combined .151 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Since struggling in his final three April starts, Teheran has allowed one run or fewer in three of his past four starts. He pitched a season-high seven innings on Thursday vs. Milwaukee, he commanded his fastball and displayed an effective slider.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke lowered his ERA to a stingy 1.48 after a no-decision vs. San Diego. Catcher A.J. Pierzynski has owned Greinke in his career, however, as the veteran is hitting .404 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Wood missed his scheduled start Friday night after coming down with a stomach virus. The lefty, who tossed 7 strong innings for a win on May 16, will look to continue fine-tuning his mechanics.

home_pitcher_note: Heston has a 12.91 ERA in his last two starts, but this has been overlooked largely because the Giants won both games. His record is much better on the road (3-1) than at home, but his ERA at AT&T Park (2.77) is far better than away from it (5.79).
away_pitcher_note: With an expanded repertoire that now includes both a sinker and a cutter, Miller has proven to be one of the game's most dominant pitchers this year. He has limited opponents to a .144 batting average in his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson has yielded five earned runs or more in three of his nine starts. His ratios of strikeouts to walks (1.73) and home runs per nine innings (1.3) are personal worsts. His ERA would set another unwanted precedent if it remains above 4.86.
away_pitcher_note: While shying away from his changeup recently, Foltynewicz has produced better whiff rates with his curveball and slider. The rookie's command proven to be much better than expected when he joined Atlanta's rotation earlier this month.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum surrendered three homers in his previous outing after allowing just one in 47 2/3 innings beforehand, but picked up the win. He holds a career 2.76 ERA in 15 starts against the Braves, striking out 103 in 98 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Though he has produced promising results through his first two career starts, Perez has encountered frequent trouble. He has induced timely ground balls with his sinker. His curveball and changeup weren't as effective his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: If Bumgarner arranged to pitch on the last day of May, it wouldn't be surprising. He's 9-1 in May decisions over the last two seasons, more than any other pitcher in this particular time span.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has battled inconsistent command throughout this frustration-filled season. He has allowed at least 10 hits in three of his past six starts. Left-handed hitters have produced a .456 on-base percentage against him.

home_pitcher_note: Bradley has struggled since getting hit in the face by a line drive and spending two weeks on the DL. In three starts since being activated he is 0-2 with an 11.81 ERA. In the three starts before the injury, his ERA was 1.45.
away_pitcher_note: Wood, who is coming off his finest start of the season, seems to have distanced himself from his early-season woes. He has regained confidence in his changeup and curveball since recently making a couple of mechanical adjustments.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter has allowed four runs over 10 innings in his last two starts after a rough three-start stretch that saw him allow 18 earned runs in 14 1/3 innings. In his last home start, he allowed nine runs in just 1 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Miller has allowed two earned runs or fewer in each of his first 10 starts. He limited opponents to a .155 batting average in May. Solo homers have accounted for three of the six runs he's allowed in his past 39 innings.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had an up-and-down May. He allowed four runs or more four times in six starts, but also had a nine-inning outing. He makes his first career start against the Braves in search of more consistency in June.
away_pitcher_note: During his past two starts, Foltynewicz has shown why many believe he has the potential to be a legitimate frontline starter. The rookie hurler has commanded his plus fastball and benefited from an improved curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Perez has excelled since moving into the starting rotation, going 1-0 with a 1.00 ERA in three starts. The rookie faces the Pirates for the first time, looking to give up one or zero runs for the fourth straight start.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has acquitted himself well in two starts -- both wins -- since coming off the DL after hip surgery. He threw seven innings Saturday in San Diego, allowing two runs (one earned) on three hits, with 16 of his 24 outs coming on ground balls.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran looks to find some consistency after an up-and-down May, in which he had a 2-1 record and a 5.03 ERA in six starts. He has had success against the Pirates in the past, going 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in four appearances (three starts).
away_pitcher_note: Locke's rotation incumbency gets a stiff test in Turner Field, where in two starts he has allowed nine runs in 9 2/3 innings. He had a 10 2/3-inning shutout string before allowing seven runs in four innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has been on a roll of late, with his only three starts of seven innings or more this season coming the last three times out, all of which were wins. He is 0-1 in his career against the Pirates, but has a 2.87 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Cole returns to the scene of his postseason clinching effort of Sept. 23, when he held the Braves to four hits and two runs in seven innings in his only Turner Field start. He has made 16 straight starts without walking more than two men.

home_pitcher_note: Miller is coming off of his shortest start of the year, a 4 1/3-inning effort at Arizona. He allowed a season-high four runs and issued six walks. Even with that bump in the road, Miller has posted a 1.89 ERA in 71 1/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy beat the Mets the last time out, his first victory since May 6. He has scuffled with mechanics this season but found a few fixes, particularly with his release point. He struck out eight against the Mets and had four pitches working for him.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz's last start against the Diamondbacks was the first time since his season debut (May 1) that he was unable to record at least seven strikeouts. He fanned five and allowed four earned runs to bring his ERA to 4.29 through seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Shields is the first Padres starter to begin a season with a 7-0 mark since Andy Hawkins did so in 1985 on his way to an 11-0 start. Ten of his 12 starts have been quality starts and the team is averaging 7.17 runs per game while he's pitching.

home_pitcher_note: After three starts of at least five innings and no more than one run allowed, Perez struggled to command his fastball Friday against the Pirates. It led to his worst start of his brief big league career: four runs and five walks in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ross picked up his first road win of the season the last time out against the Reds, going five innings in a start that was shortened due to rain. It was the seventh consecutive start where he's allowed three or fewer runs.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran credited added aggression with the velocity increase that helped him complete a season-high 7 1/3 innings his last time out. The Braves want him to get back to using his four-seamer and slider as his primary weapons.
away_pitcher_note: After being hurt by poor defense and poor run support early in the season, Cashner has struggled the last two times out with command. He's allowed a combined 12 earned runs on 19 hits in his last two starts. He walked five the last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Colon has faced the Braves twice already this season, going 2-0 with a 4.15 ERA. Freddie Freeman has been Colon's nemesis, going 7-for-16 (.438) lifetime against him, though none of Freeman's 14 career home runs against the Mets have come off Colon.
away_pitcher_note: Wood allowed his emotions to get the best of him as he allowed three fifth-inning runs and was ejected for arguing balls and strikes during Sunday's start against the Pirates. He's produced a 2.00 ERA over his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom was named the co-National League Player of the Week along with Clayton Kershaw. In his last start against the D-backs, he allowed three runs (two earned) on five hits and three walks with 10 strikeouts in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Miller bounced back from his worst start of the year with a seven-inning, one-run performance against the Padreson Monday. He struck out six San Diego batters and walked just one, lowering his ERA to 1.84.

home_pitcher_note: Gee's been in and out of the rotation, but slots in to make a spot start on Sunday. In six starts this season, he's 0-3 with a 4.46 ERA in 34 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz had another "learning" start his last time out, against the Padres, allowing five runs in 5 2/3 innings. After the game, he admitted to executing his off-speed pitches poorly. Seven of the 12 hits he allowed came off his slider.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello was dealt his fourth straight defeat on Wednesday, after the O's tagged him for five runs and 10 hits in 5 1/3 innings. He has pitched to a 7.03 ERA across those four losses.
away_pitcher_note: Perez worked through three long innings against San Diego on Wednesday but settled down in the fourth and showed the moxie that Braves evaluators have raved about to get through seven innings, allowing just one unearned run.

home_pitcher_note: Location has become an issue recently for Miley, who has scattered 24 hits, including four home runs, over his past three starts. Two of those outings only lasted four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has regained his aggressive approach and relied more heavily on his four-seam fastball in his past two outings. He was strong through seven innings in each and then faltered in the eighth.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has pitched more effectively recently, but he surrendered a career-high two homers in Friday's loss to the Mets. The lefty's recent success has been influenced by the confidence he has regained in his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Kelly's struggles vs. Toronto continued on Friday, when he allowed four runs in six innings. The righty has a 7.64 ERA in three starts vs. the Blue Jays this year. He is 1-0 with a 1.46 ERA in two career starts against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Three one-out hits in the seventh inning led to the three runs Miller was charged with during Saturday's start against the Mets. The right-hander has allowed two runs or fewer in 10 of 13 starts and has a 1.59 ERA in five home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Inconsistency remains the trend for Buchholz. Since firing eight shutout innings against the Twins on June 2, he has given up eight runs and 18 hits in a pair of subpar outings.

home_pitcher_note: Wisler, the heralded pitching prospect the Braves acquired in a trade with the Padres, will make his Major League debut Friday after being called up Thursday night. In 12 starts with Triple-A Gwinnett this year, Wisler has posted a 4.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: deGrom faces Atlanta for the second time in a week. But lately, it hasn't mattered who the reigning NL Rookie of the Year faces. deGrom is averaging 9.4 strikeouts over his last five starts, and hasn't lost any of his last six.

home_pitcher_note: Perez is as the only Major League starting pitcher (min. 5 starts) who has posted a sub-2.50 ERA while surrendering an on-base percentage of at least .300. His sinker has helped him produce an effective 54 percent ground-ball rate.
away_pitcher_note: For just the second time in his young career, Syndergaard will take on an NL East opponent when he faces the Braves. His first divisional outing against the Phillies also happened to be his best of the year: 7 1/3 shutout innings with six strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran has been trying to find his identity while attempting to regain confidence in his four-seam fastball. His inconsistent two-seam fastball has proven to be a liability against left-handed batters, who have produced a .399 OBP against him.
away_pitcher_note: Of all the teams Harvey has faced at least twice, the Braves have the lowest batting average against him (.119). Harvey also won his only career start at Turner Field, striking out 13 on the same day as Zack Wheeler's debut in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg returned from the DL in time for this start, his first since May 29. He made one start for Double-A Harrisburg while rehabbing from a stiff neck, yielding one run on four hits over five innings while fanning six on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Wood has seemingly turned things around while allowing exactly one earned run in four of his past six starts. An improved sinker and changeup has led to more ground balls than he produced earlier this season.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has started twice against the Braves this season, going 1-0 while allowing 16 hits and six runs over 13 innings. He's struck out nine and walked four in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: Though Miller hasn't been as dominant as he was in May, he's allowed just one earned run in two of his past three starts. He's posted a 0.73 ERA in four career starts against the Nationals, but hasn't faced them this year.

home_pitcher_note: Fister's first start back from the DL was impressive, with the numbers -- four runs in the sixth -- slightly skewed by the defense behind him. He's started twice against the Braves in his career and allowed seven earned runs in 12 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wisler passed his first test, as he needed just 88 pitches to complete eight strong innings against the Mets in his Major League debut on Friday. A highly regarded prospect, he primarily relies on his fastball and slider.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano was on the wrong side of a no-hitter Saturday, giving up five runs on seven hits as he lost to Max Scherzer and the Nationals. He's actually been worse at home (2-4, 4.35 ERA) than on the road (2-2, 2.30) this season.
away_pitcher_note: Perez has earned the nickname Magic Man as he has managed to post a 2.14 ERA, despite allowing opponents to produce a .324 on-base percentage in his first seven starts. A ground-ball pitcher, he allowed two homers his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Morton yielded nine runs on eight hits and a walk while recording two outs against the Nationals on Sunday. The good news for Morton is he's pitching at PNC Park, where he's allowed only two runs over three starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran halted his struggles as surrendered just one hit over seven scoreless innings in his last start. But he had the fortune of facing a right-handed-heavy Mets lineup. Left-handers have compiled a .396 OBP against him.

home_pitcher_note: After a couple of encouraging starts, Locke allowed four runs (two earned) in four innings Tuesday vs. the Reds. He is 1-1 with a 6.08 ERA in five career starts against the Braves, who drafted him in the second round in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Though he surrendered a season-high 10 hits against the Nationals on Tuesday, Wood completed seven innings for the fourth time in his past seven starts. He has produced a 2.72 ERA during that span.

home_pitcher_note: Miller hasn't recorded a win since May 17, but continues to pitch well. He's allowed just six earned runs over his last four starts combined. His last outing was a seven-inning, one-run performance against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann will face the Braves for the second time in less than a week. On June 24, Zimmermann pitched eight scoreless innings, but didn't figure into the decision. The Nationals won the game in extra innings.

home_pitcher_note: After an impressive MLB debut, Wisler will be looking for redemption in his third career start. The 22-year-old right-hander struggled against the Nationals on Thursday, surrendering six runs (four earned) on nine hits.
away_pitcher_note: Fister is 4-1 with a 2.18 ERA in six career starts against the Braves. In those six starts, Fister has a 0.97 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: Banuelos has gone 6-2 this season at Triple-A Gwinnett while posting a 2.29 ERA in 82 2/3 innings. Before his most recent start (3 IP, 3 ER, 4 BB), the Braves' No. 11 prospect had posted a 2.03 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer, who threw the second no-hitter in Nationals history, has taken a perfect game into at least the sixth inning in each of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Though Teheran has struggled mightily on the road, he has produced a 2.35 ERA in seven home starts. His inability to consistently command his sinker has led to left-handers compiling a .408 on-base percentage against him this year.
away_pitcher_note: Morgan gets a second chance at a second impression with this start after his last start was abbreviated and eventually cancelled due to rain. Morgan allowed one run in 5 2/3 innings in his Major League debut on 6/21.

home_pitcher_note: Wood considered Sunday's impressive effort in Pittsburgh to be his finest start of the season. He commanded his fastball on both sides of the plate and displayed an effective curveball while matching a season-high eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Correia pitched OK in Game 1 of Sunday's doubleheader against the Nationals, allowing seven hits, three runs (one earned) and three walks, striking out four in 5 1/3 innings. Sloppy defense extended a few innings for him.

home_pitcher_note: Miller looks to bounce back from his worst start of the season against the Nationals, and the Phillies might give him some optimism there. The last time Miller faced them, he threw a shutout and struck out eight batters.
away_pitcher_note: Each time Hamels starts for the Phillies it could be his last, as he is a candidate to be traded before the July 31 non-waiver Trade Deadline. He put in a good performance Tuesday against the Brewers, allowing two runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has pitched much better lately than the box scores indicate, good news for a team that may try to trade him later this month. "If you get distracted, you're not doing the things you need to do to win," Lohse said.
away_pitcher_note: Wisler got some quick revenge against the Nationals in his last start, throwing 5 1/3 shutout innings and striking out six batters, thanks largely to a sharp slider. In three starts since being called up, Wisler has posted a 2.60 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cravy will fill in for the injured Matt Garza and make his second career start. He was impressive in his Major League debut June 2 against the Cardinals, pitching seven innings and allowing just one run on four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Banuelos' excellent MLB debut Thursday was cut short due to cramps and dehydration, but before exiting, the lefty showed a plus changeup and struck out seven Nationals hitters through 5 2/3 shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has put together a string of three straight quality starts. Last time out Fiers held the Reds to 3 hits in seven scoreless innings to pick up the win. It was his first win since June 12.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran is coming off his fifth home win of the season, where he allowed one run in seven innings against the Phillies. He'll try to improve the command of his fastball in his next start, as that has been an issue for him throughout the season.

home_pitcher_note: Homer-prone for much of the year, Kendrick made a forward step in his last start -- a no-decision against the D-backs, when he made it through 5 2/3 innings with three runs allowed.

Germen, claimed off waivers from the Cubs on July 7, will be making his first career start after 60 relief outings with the Mets and Cubs. David Hale was the original scheduled starter, but he pitched Thursday following a rain delay.
away_pitcher_note: Miller bounced back from his worst start of the season by taking on Cole Hamels, and shutting out the Phillies through 6 1/3 innings Sunday. Miller is just 5-4 this season despite a 2.07 ERA thanks to minimal run support during his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Dating back to June 25, De La Rosa has given up just three runs in 18 innings, all while dealing with a lingering cut on his left middle finger.
away_pitcher_note: Wisler has helped the Braves win three of his first four career starts. His 0.90 ground-ball/fly-ball ratio might not play well at Coors Field. But he's shown an ability to miss bats when he commands his slider.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis is coming off his worst career start, as he gave up a career-high 10 runs in 2 1/3 innings. It's a small sample size, but Bettis' career numbers versus Atlanta aren't great either. In six frames, he's surrendered 8 runs, 10 hits and 6 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Wood's start in Thursday’s series opener was limited to just two pitches because of a long rain delay. He’s at his best when he commands his curveball, so it will be interesting how he fares in his first Coors Field experience.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran's inconsistent first half was marred by his inability to command his two-seam fastball and the lack of confidence he had in his four-seamer. Still, he posted an impressive 2.04 ERA in eight home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks says he's simplified things, and it's working. The right-hander has not given up a run over 22 1/3 innings, and has gone three straight starts without giving up a run. This will be his first career start against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Banuelos is nearing his innings limit, but the Braves want him to make at least one more start before possibly ending the season as a reliever. His changeup has helped him hold opponents to just one run over his first two career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lester finished the first half with his sixth straight loss, and hasn't won in his last 10 starts since May 16. He hasn't gotten much support as the Cubs have scored three runs in his last six outings.

home_pitcher_note: Miller concluded him impressive first half with a frustration-filled outing at Coors Field. The All-Star hurler has allowed two earned runs or fewer in 14 of his 18 starts. He has posted a 1.94 ERA in eight home starts.
away_pitcher_note: For the fourth time in five games, Arrieta lasted seven innings as he became the first Cubs pitcher since 2008 to earn 10 wins before the All-Star break. He picked up the win in six of his past seven games, allowing 13 runs across that span.

home_pitcher_note: Wisler is making his first start since July 11, when he held the Rockies to just two runs over six innings while recording a career-best seven strikeouts in Coors Field. He's posted a 3.10 ERA in five MLB starts.
away_pitcher_note: On July 11, Beachy made his first Major League appearance since Aug. 20, 2013, coming back from his second Tommy John surgery. Facing Milwaukee, he allowed three earned runs over four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wood will try and get the taste of his last start out of his mouth on Tuesday. In his most recent outing against the Rockies -- his worst of the season -- Wood allowed seven earned runs in 5 2/3 innings and raised his ERA to 3.76.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Anderson's 19th start of the season, the injury-plagued lefty's best total since he made 19 for the A's in 2010. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in six straight outings, with a 2.48 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran is coming off his shortest home start of the season, and will now look to find some rare success on the road. Teheran's ERA away from Turner Field in 2015 is 6.95, and lately his slider has been his only consistent pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger's last start was interrupted by a power outage at Nationals Park. In his only previous start against the Braves, he allowed five earned runs and 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cooney has not recorded a decision in any of his first five Major League starts, but he did shut out the Mets over 5 2/3 innings in his last outing. Cooney has allowed six earned runs over 22 innings since being recalled.
away_pitcher_note: Banuelos has not allowed more than one earned run in any of his first three career starts. But shaky command limited him to 88 pitches and 4 2/3 innings his last time out. The rookie has impressed with his changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez’s first start of the second half was delayed a few days after he was summoned to cover the final four innings of Sunday’s 18-inning game. This will be his first career appearance against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Miller will be making his first career start against the Cardinals, who drafted him in 2009 and employed him through the end of last season. The right-hander has posted a 5.16 ERA in his last four road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha became the NL’s third 11-game winner in his last start, but he has allowed five runs in each of his last two outings. This will be Wacha’s first career start against the Braves, who have seen him in relief twice before.
away_pitcher_note: Each of the four runs Wisler surrendered against the Dodgers on Monday were tallied within four pitches in the fifth inning. The rookie has shown good poise and an effective slider through his first six career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman lost after allowing four runs on six hits -- including two home runs -- and two walks with four strikeouts in six innings against the Yankees on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Wood’s 3.11 road ERA in 12 appearances trumps his 4.99 ERA in seven starts at Turner Field this year. He’s only faced two Orioles previously, but Travis Snider had his number last year, going 3-for-6 with a home run and a double for the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez struggled, lasting just 2 1/3 innings and giving up seven earned runs against the Yankees. He has a 4.89 ERA in his last seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran was tagged with a loss but struck out a career-high 11 batters in his last outing as he continued a solid July. His ERA is 2.81 in four starts during the month after allowing six runs in two of his three outings to end June.

home_pitcher_note: The righty was dominant again as he turned in his second straight quality start on Friday night. Tillman has allowed just one earned run in 15 second-half innings.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz will return to the Majors to start in place of the injured Manny Banuelos. This will be his first appearance since he was optioned just before the All-Star break to focus on his power pitches with Triple-A Gwinnett.

home_pitcher_note: Harang (left foot plantar fasciitis) had been scheduled to make a rehab start Wednesday in Triple-A, but needing pitching help, the Phillies skipped that completely and decided to have him start Thursday against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Miller is looking for his first win since throwing a two-hitter against the Marlins on May 17, but the winless streak is not because of inefficiency. The Braves have scored three runs or fewer in his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Buchanan is in the Phillies’ rotation for the third time this season, but this time is taking Cole Hamels’ spot. Hamels’ long Phillies career is at its end with the Phillies and Rangers agreeing to a trade late Wednesday night.
away_pitcher_note: Prior to going on the DL, Perez made eight starts and 11 appearances for the Braves across May and June, during which he amassed a 2.88 ERA over 50 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nola has been impressive in his first two starts since being promoted from Triple-A. He had allowed just two runs and thrown just 74 pitches through seven innings Sunday against the Cubs. Teammates have liked his poise.
away_pitcher_note: Wisler is 4-0 in night games and is coming off a seven-inning start against the Cardinals in which he allowed just two runs. The rookie has not allowed more than four runs in any of his seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morgan makes his seventh start of the season. He has allowed three runs or fewer in six of those starts, but he has pitched six or more innings just three times. The Phillies would like to see Morgan get a little deeper into games going forward.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran will have yet another opportunity to halt the struggles he has encountered while producing a 7.24 ERA in 11 road starts. His fastball has had more life since the All-Star break, but he’s allowed two homers in both of his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Braves know Foltynewicz has the stuff to project as a reliever. But they want to give him a chance to prove to be a starter. His start on Wednesday against the Orioles provided some hope he's moving in the right direction.
away_pitcher_note: Cain has alternated subpar outings with decent ones. If that pattern holds, he'll be due for a strong performance at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: A lack of run support has left Miller winless while producing a respectable 3.19 ERA over his past 13 starts. The All-Star hurler has also allowed a season-high 11 hits in two of his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy has seemingly gained strength and stamina with each start. This will mark his sixth start since recovering from lower back pain and missing most of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Perez ended a month-long stint on the disabled list on Friday and surrendered four runs before he recorded his first out. The rookie relies heavily on a sinker that has helped him as he has frequently encountered scoring threats.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner matched a season-worst by allowing six runs Friday at Texas. He's coming off a July in which he finished 3-2 but posted a 4.85 ERA, his highest of any month this year.

home_pitcher_note: Wisler had another learning experience in his most recent start against the Phillies, where he allowed seven runs on eight hits through 4 2/3 innings. Specifically, Wisler's slider didn't look as sharp as it had in previous outings.
away_pitcher_note: Urena is trying to make his case to be a member of the '16 rotation, and he'll get his second start since being recalled on Friday. He allowed four earned runs and took a loss Saturday, and also pitched a scoreless inning of relief on April 14.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran is coming off one of his best starts this year. He held a lefty-heavy Phillies lineup to two runs over seven innings, while striking out seven. Teheran credited fastball command for the success, and he didn't walk a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez won in Atlanta on April 22, 2014, when he tossed eight scoreless innings and allowed just three hits. The righty is 3-0 at home this season, while he's 1-0 in two road starts. He won his last road outing on July 22 in Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz gave up four home runs in four innings his last time out, after hanging sliders over the plate and missing up throughout the start. Keeping his mid-to-upper 90s fastball down and under control has been a lingering issue.
