home_pitcher_note: The rookie southpaw’s fastball command has improved over his past two starts, but he still had to pitch around four walks while allowing three solo homers Tuesday at Coors Field. He has not used his slider in either of his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo unveiled a two-seam fastball three weeks ago to go with a four-seamer, changeup and slider. He used the two-seamer the most over his six scoreless innings Tuesday and allowed two hits. His quick command of his four pitches has impressed.

home_pitcher_note: Seven of the nine hits Foltynewicz allowed at Coors Field on Wednesday were recorded with two strikes.  His inability to consistently command his slider and curveball has been the difference as he’s struggled in three of his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Albers made his 2017 debut against the Orioles in place of the injured James Paxton. He held Baltimore to one run over five innings, good enough to earn his first win since 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off an effective five-inning effort at Coors Field that  resulted in his first win, Sims will attempt to continue proving he has belonged.  He’s shown some potential with his curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzales hasn’t made it through the fifth inning of any of his three starts since joining the rotation in place of Felix Hernandez. Baltimore collected nine hits off the lefty in 4 1/3 innings his last turn.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey was on a roll before he surrendered three sixth-inning homers during Friday's loss to the Reds. He chalked it up to one of those nights where he has to live with the unpredictability of the knuckleball.
away_pitcher_note: Ramirez bested his former Rays teammates in his last start to earn his first win since rejoining the Mariners. Building up his workload, Ramirez has pitched six innings in each of his past two starts, allowing a total of five hits and one ER.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran was victimized by a couple defensive misfortunes as he pitched better than his line suggested Saturday against the Reds. He found success with a modified slider as he tossed seven scoreless against the Rockies on Aug. 14.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis held the Braves scoreless for seven innings on Aug. 14 in his return from a bout with testicular cancer. In two starts, Bettis has yielded 14 hits in as many innings with eight strikeouts and one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb's command has improved over his past three starts, as he hasn't missed arm side as frequently as he previously had. He's struggled to consistently create clean innings, but has had a knack for minimizing damage.
away_pitcher_note: Many Rockies pitchers have found pitching on the road easier than at home, but not Freeland, a Denver native. He has a lower ERA at Coors Field (3.30) than on the road (4.22).

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz recorded a career-best 11 strikeouts against the Marlins Aug. 6, but has struggled to command his offspeed pitches as each of his past three starts have turned ugly.
away_pitcher_note: In his last seven starts, Gray has gone at least six innings five times. He's pitched to a 3.53 ERA and opponents have just a .303 on-base percentage over that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Nola hasn’t looked himself in his last two starts after going 10 straight allowing no more than two earned runs, a Phillies record. He’s give up 12 runs in his last 11 1/3 innings picking up losses against the Giants and Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Sims won his last two starts and pitched six scoreless innings against the Mariners in his last outing. He has improved his command by being aggressive in the strike zone, and has thrown a strike on 63 percent of his pitches this year.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff has been grinding much of the season because of a slight dip in velocity. His fastball is averaging 90.4 mph this season compared to 91.6 mph the previous two.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a 4.59 road ERA, Dickey has found success away from SunTrust Park. In his last two road starts, he allowed two runs over 14 innings. He fired seven scoreless innings against the Phillies on July 30.

home_pitcher_note: Leiter silenced a hot Marlins lineup over seven scoreless innings last Friday, allowing a hit and two walks en route to his second big league win. He took a no-hitter into the sixth inning, when leadoff hitter Miguel Rojas doubled.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has a 3.24 ERA on the road this season. He struggled in his last trip to Philadelphia, giving up eight runs in 4 2/3 innings on July 28. Since that start, his command has improved. He has allowed three homers in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off a win against the Phillies in which he gave up two runs over seven innings. It also was his first win since May 24 after going 0-2 in  his previous eight starts. He's 2-2 with a 3.56 ERA in 10 starts at Wrigley this season.
away_pitcher_note: Newcomb looks to finish his bounceback August strong. Newcomb had a rough go of it in June with an ERA topping seven, but looks more like his early-season self. Newcomb faced Chicago on July 18 and allowed five earned runs across 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off a loss to the Phillies in his last start in which he gave up four earned runs over five innings, striking out eight. He faced the Braves in Atlanta on July 18 and got the win, giving up one run over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: After going seven straight starts from June 18-July 25, Foltynewicz sparkled with a sub-three ERA. His last six outings have left much to be desired as he's allowed an earned run an inning with opponents hitting .342 with a .960 OPS.

home_pitcher_note: Lester will make his first start since Aug. 17. He's been sidelined with left shoulder fatigue, which hindered him in that last outing against the Reds when he gave up seven earned runs in 1 2/3 innings. He threw 47 pitches in a sim game Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Sims is coming off the longest outing of his seven-start big league career, 6 1/3 innings against the Phillies. Sims threw his slider and curveball more than he had in any start this season, and allowed four earned. He has never faced the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery was 2-0 subbing for Jon Lester, and will get another start in the series finale. In his last two starts, Montgomery gave up one run over 13 innings. He beat the Braves on July 19 -- and hit a home run, too.
away_pitcher_note: Fried will have an opportunity to display his much-hyped curveball as he makes his first career start. The lefty made four appearances as a reliever in August. MLBPipeline ranks him as the Braves’ 10th-best prospect.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey recorded season highs in innings (eight) and pitches (121) as he limited the Phillies to a seventh-inning run on Wednesday.  The knuckleballer has allowed one run or fewer in eight of his past 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner threw arguably his most impressive outing of the season on Wednesday against the Astros, holding them to one run in eight innings. He's allowed more than two earned runs just once in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw featured an impressive slider as he proved successful while pitching for Class A Advanced Florida, Double-A Mississippi and Triple-A Gwinnett. He produced a 2.62 ERA and notched 147 K's over 123 2/3 innings in the Minors this year.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will be making his first start for Texas since being acquired from the White Sox. He is 3-1 with a 3.31 ERA in his last eight starts. This will be his first career start vs. the Braves, but he's 4-6 with a 3.59 ERA in 15 Interleague games.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw featured an impressive slider as he proved successful while pitching for Class A Advanced Florida, Double-A Mississippi and Triple-A Gwinnett. He produced a 2.62 ERA and notched 147 K's over 123 2/3 innings in the Minors this year.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will be making his first start for Texas since being acquired from the White Sox. He is 3-1 with a 3.31 ERA in his last eight starts. This will be his first career start vs. the Braves, but he's 4-6 with a 3.59 ERA in 15 Interleague games.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran has registered a quality start in three of his last four outings, and he has gotten the win in his last two. He hasn't found much success at home this season with a 6.54 ERA over 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: After a strong start to August that saw him register a win in four consecutive outings, Hamels has allowed 10 runs over 9 1/3 innings in his last two starts. He has a 4.85 ERA over his last nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Walks and longevity continue to be a concern for the rookie lefty. Newcomb hasn't recorded an out in the sixth inning in any of his past three starts, and he's walked more than six batters per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: In 13 road starts, Straily is 5-5 with a 4.62 ERA. Since the All-Star break, he is 2-4 with a 5.06 ERA. The slider has been his most effective pitch, with opponents batting .220 off it with 138 swinging strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Since allowing at least six runs over three straight starts, Foltynewicz has produced better damage control in his past two starts. He said he has regained a better feel for his offspeed pitches, primarily his slider.
away_pitcher_note: Urena went seven innings, allowing one run, in his last start -- a no-decision vs. the Phillies that broke a string of five straight starts of 6 innings or fewer. His season high is 8 innings. Urena is 1-1 in three starts vs. Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Fried showed good poise as he limited the Cubs to one run over five innings while making his first career start Sunday. The young lefty concluded three of his four strikeouts with his big curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Conley was hit hard by the Nats in his last start, yielding three runs -- on a pair of home runs -- through four innings. The lefty has allowed four homers over his last two starts, matching the four long balls he allowed in five starts prior.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer threw a season-high 121 pitches during a solid eight-inning effort in Philadelphia on Aug. 30 and then struggled mightily against the Rangers on Monday.  He’s allowed 24 homers this year, 18 of them at home.
away_pitcher_note: Versatile enough to handle a number of roles, Despaigne is making a case to be in the rotation. He threw seven innings, giving up one run in a loss on Tuesday to the Nationals. It marked his first seven-inning start since April 14, 2015.

home_pitcher_note: When he records his first out during this start, Gonzalez will reach the 180-inning mark for the season, which automatically triggers a $12 million option in his contract for 2018. He carries a career-low 2.50 ERA into this outing.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has allowed three runs or fewer in four of five starts since regaining a feel for his slider. He lasted just four innings against the Nationals in April, but he has allowed just two runs in his past two starts (14 innings) against them.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has been dealing with a few nagging injuries during the past few weeks, including a sore calf after being hit with a line drive on Sept. 2. Although the calf was sore between starts, it did not bother him during his most recent outing.
away_pitcher_note: The highly touted rookie battled command issues as he gave up six runs over four innings with four walks and six strikeouts in his Major League debut vs. the Rangers on Wednesday. He features a plus fastball and an elusive slider.

home_pitcher_note: In 17 career starts against the Braves, Roark has a 2.79 ERA, his second best of any divisional opponent (2.76 vs. Mets). In two starts this month, he has given up four runs in 13 innings, with 16 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has lost 6 straight starts, but he has been more effective as he has regained a feel for his changeup and slider over his past 3 outings. He produced a combination of 37 swings and misses and called strikes in his last start on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old rookie will look for a repeat of his previous meeting with the Mets on June 10, which was his MLB debut. He allowed one unearned run on four hits in 6 1/3 innings, with seven strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: As Montero makes a case for himself in the Mets’ 2018 rotation, he has found success while struggling with walks. Over his last three starts, Montero has walked 14 in 18 2/3 innings while allowing five runs.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander has been in a bit of a rough patch, yielding four or more runs in four of his last five starts. He'll take on a Mets club he's defeated twice this season.
away_pitcher_note: deGrom has set a goal of 200 innings this year, and at 188 1/3 with three starts remaining, he should reach it. He needs just three innings to eclipse his career high of 191, set during his first full season in 2015.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran looked like his old self in his previous start against the Nationals, pitching seven shutout innings in D.C. He'll look for an encore performance against a Mets lineup he'll be facing for the fifth time in 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Five walks in four innings sealed his fate Tuesday vs. the Cubs. The rookie has had trouble building momentum this season, routinely following up good outings with bad ones. He is 2-1 vs. Atlanta this season.

home_pitcher_note: Looking like a slightly shorter version of CC Sabathia, Gohara is the most physically advanced prospect to recently rise through the Braves’ system. His top pitches are a high-octane fastball with a swing-and-miss slider.
away_pitcher_note: To stretch himself out in preparation of the postseason, Scherzer threw 116 pitches in his last start against the Braves. It was his roughest outing of 17 as he was tagged for seven runs on seven hits and six walks in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: After spending a couple weeks in the bullpen, Sims returns to the rotation to replace an injured Mike Foltynewicz. Sims has worked into the sixth inning during five of his seven career starts.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Gonzalez’s first start in more than a week, following a rough outing against Atlanta on Sept. 12 when he gave up five runs on seven hits in five innings. He has yet to beat the Braves in three starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey’s late-season struggles have extended as he’s struggled to consistently command his knuckleball. He has posted a 6.55 ERA and allowed opponents to hit .333 over his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Roark continues to get stronger as the season progresses, and September has been his strongest month to date. In three starts this month, he owns a 2.84 ERA with 23 strikeouts and three walks over 19 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Though he still heavily relies on his fastball and curveball, Newcomb has used his changeup more frequently in his past two starts. The rookie southpaw has a 3.86 ERA over his past nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lively is making a good case to be part of next season’s rotation. He has pitched well most of the season, but also has a 3.00 ERA in his past four starts, with his last start against the A’s getting cut short at three innings because of rain.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Teheran's last chance to conquer SunTrust Park, where he has a 6.23 ERA over 16 starts. He has pitched more effectively over the past month and allowed three earned runs or less in each of his past three home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Alvarez makes his second start in the big leagues since 2015, joining the Phillies last weekend to give them a six-man rotation. He allowed four hits, four runs, two walks and two home runs in five innings vs. the A's. He struck out four.

home_pitcher_note: Already touted as the most impressive prospect the Braves have brought to the Majors within their rebuild, this CC Sabathia clone can baffle hitters with his slider and a fastball that sits in the upper 90s.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta allowed two homers in the first five pitches he threw Monday against the Dodgers, but settled in after that and allowed just those two runs in six innings. The Phillies love his arm, but he needs to be much more consistent.

home_pitcher_note: Flexen will make his first start since Sept. 3 in Houston, when he allowed seven earned runs over four innings. The righty found some success in a relief role, giving up just one run over five innings in four appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Sims doesn’t have overwhelming stuff, but he has consistently commanded each of his four pitches. He believes spending time in the bullpen earlier this month helped him stop thinking too much between pitches.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets are taking things easy down the stretch with Lugo, who is pitching with a partially torn ulnar collateral ligament in his right elbow. Lugo has averaged 77 pitches in five starts since coming off the disabled list, with a high of 84.
away_pitcher_note: With Mike Foltynewicz still dealing with a lacerated  finger, Fried will get his first start since Sept. 9. The rookie southpaw will be on a limited pitch count since he has made just one relief appearance within the past two weeks.

home_pitcher_note: Montero’s brief run of success has come to an abrupt end in September. Over his past 15 innings, spanning four starts, Montero owns a 7.80 ERA with 18 hits, nine walks and 13 strikeouts. He is unlikely to be part of the Mets’ 2018 rotation.
away_pitcher_note: This could be the knuckleballer’s final career start.  After struggling through the early portion of this month, he regained a feel for his knuckleball during Thursday’s eight-inning outing -- and win -- over the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Gsellman will look to establish some consistency in likely his final appearance of 2017. After seeming to turn a corner against Atlanta, he took a step back during his last start, when he gave up six runs (five earned) in five innings vs. Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Newcomb has allowed three runs or fewer in his last four starts and has steadily developed more confidence in his changeup. He will look to finish the season strong on the road, where has a 3.66 ERA in six starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie has had a rough last two starts, giving up 13 earned runs in 7 2/3 innings. At Arizona in his previous outing, he worked four innings, giving up five runs in a no-decision. Of his 77 pitches, he didn't have any swinging strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has picked it up down the stretch, going 4-1 with a 2.08 ERA over his past six starts. In that span, he hasn't reached six innings only once. He allowed just three hits over six scoreless innings in his lone start vs. Miami this year.

home_pitcher_note: Miami's most durable starter, Straily has thrown 178 2/3 innings and made 32 starts. At Arizona in his last start, he struck out nine, giving him 167 total. Of his 110 pitches, he had 17 swinging strikes, plus eight swinging strikes on 22 changeups.
away_pitcher_note: Making his fifth Major League start, Gohara will look to build off his most recent outing. Although it was a hard-luck loss against the Phillies, he delivered seven innings of one-run ball, striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Despaigne pitched six innings of two-run ball, giving up seven hits and walking none while striking out three at Coors Field Monday. He was effective at changing speeds, using both sides of the plate and maintaining his focus against a strong lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Sims won his last start, a 6 2/3-inning, two-run effort against the Mets. Since returning from a bullpen stint, Sims has allowed three earned runs in two starts. He gave up four earned runs on Aug. 6 vs. Miami, his first start against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Urena gave up a four-run first frame in Colorado Tuesday, allowing six runs on nine hits and four walks (one intentional) while striking out four over five innings. He was unable to contain the damage, allowing three two-out runs.
away_pitcher_note: Fried will seek revenge as he faces the Marlins, the only team to tally more than one earned run against him through three career starts. The young lefty will attempt to make a good impression and improve his bid for a rotation spot next year.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb is 1-2 with a 2.35 ERA in five starts this spring, striking out 15 over 15 1/3 innings
away_pitcher_note: Atlanta's No. 3 prospect, Mike Soroka, will make the start for the Braves futures stars

home_pitcher_note: Teheran will become the first pitcher in Atlanta history to make five consecutive Opening Day starts. The righty has allowed two earned runs or fewer and completed at least six innings in each of his previous four such starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gabe Kapler wasted no time naming Aaron Nola his Opening Day starter early in camp. He earned it. The Phillies expect Nola to take another step forward in 2018, creating a tough 1-2 punch atop the rotation with Jake Arrieta.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has developed a more compact windup with the hope of finding more consistency than he has had in the past. The high-ceiling right-hander showed better command of his fastball during what was a stellar Grapefruit League season.
away_pitcher_note: After some early struggles in Spring Training, Pivetta finished the Grapefruit League season strong with two scoreless outings, striking out six in his final five innings.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy will be looking to bounce back from last year's injury-marred season, which concluded him surrendering a decisive homer in Game 2 of the World Series. The veteran righty exited camp confident he's regained a good feel for his slider.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez will take the mound in a regular-season game for the first time since requiring surgery on his index finger in August. The hard-throwing righty had an impressing spring with a 2.51 ERA with 15 strikeouts in 14 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: It has always been about control for Newcomb, who needs to further reduce the walk rate he improved on late last season. If he can consistently spot his fastball, he'll have more opportunities to realize the value of his plus curveball.
away_pitcher_note: After an uneven 2017, Roark never appeared in the NLDS against the Cubs, making this his first official game since Oct. 1. The Nats believe he is due for a bounce-back year.

home_pitcher_note: During his Opening Day start, Teheran provided indication he may once again start using his two-seamer as a primary pitch. He completed seven innings and allowed two runs or fewer in each of his final three starts against the Nationals last year.
away_pitcher_note: After years as a spot starter, Cole gets his first chance to be a regular member of the Nats' rotation. He emerged as the team's fifth starter thanks to his strong finish last season, in which he showed the promise that made him a former prospect.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz surrendered two solo homers but was otherwise impressive as he displayed an elusive slider in his first start of the season. He has developed a more subdued windup with the hope he will be more consistent with his command.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer picked up where he left off in his first start of the 2018 season, tossing six scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts in an Opening Day victory over the Reds. At one point during the game, he racked up seven straight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Not fazed by traffic (four hits, four walks in five innings), Marquez held the D-backs to one run. He makes the home opener start after going 6-3 with a 4.59 ERA in 13 starts at Coors as a rookie.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy (1-0, 3.38 ERA) went 5 1/3 innings in his first start of the season, a 15-2 win over the Phillies on March 31. The veteran righty allowed two runs on six hits with five strikeouts and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: Last Aug. 14, Bettis held the Braves scoreless for seven innings in his return from testicular cancer. Healthy this year, he debuted by struggling early but eventually pitching five innings of two-run ball to beat the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez will make his first start and begin filling the rotation spot earmarked for the injured Luiz Gohara. The righty was released by the Twins in March. His 4-seam fastball averaged 89.4 mph as he tossed three scoreless relief innings on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland gave up four runs on five hits against the Padres in his first start, although it was two Christian Villanueva homers that did him in. Better velocity on his offspeed stuff would do him good.
away_pitcher_note: Newcomb’s difficulty commanding his curveball left him without an out pitch on Monday, as endured a 37-pitch first inning and allowed six runs, including a homer to Bryce Harper, on Monday night. The key for the young lefty remains fastball command.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will make his second consecutive start vs. the Braves on Monday night at Nationals Park, after they ran up his pitch count to 110 and scored 5 runs (2 earned) in 5 innings during an uncharacteristic outing last week in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran had thrown 19 consecutive scoreless innings against the Nationals before allowing five earned runs over just 2 1/3 innings against them on Tuesday. Bryce Harper is 5-for-8 with three homers against the right-hander since the start of 2017.

home_pitcher_note: After posting the lowest home run ratio in the Majors last season, Strasburg was punished by the long ball in his last start, surrendering a pair of homers en route to giving up four runs in six innings and a loss against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has seemingly benefited from the subdued windup he developed over the offseason.  Limiting the number of moving body parts has improved his command and allowed for more consistency throughout his four-pitch arsenal.

home_pitcher_note: After winning the Nats' final rotation spot, Cole’s first start of the year could not gone much worse. He gave up 10 runs on 10 hits and lasted just 3 2/3 innings, but the Nationals want to give him another chance to prove himself.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy’s slider hasn’t been as effective as he had hoped, but the veteran has commanded his fastball consistently enough to work into the sixth inning in his first two starts. He limited the  Nationals to two runs over seven innings in June.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Darvish's Wrigley Field debut for the Cubs and his first game there since Game 3 of the NLCS when he beat the Cubs. In his last start, the righty had good fastball command and a sharp slider, and held the Brewers to two hits (6 IP).
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, Sanchez tossed five innings of two-run ball with seven hits and two walks against six strikeouts. Though he didn't pitch against the Cubs last season, Sanchez owns a career 3-2 record and a 3.82 ERA against Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana is coming off a 3-0 win over the Brewers in which he gave up three hits over six innings. This will be his Wrigley Field debut for 2018. Last year, the lefty was 5-0 with a 4.76 ERA in eight starts at Wrigley after being traded to the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander rebounded from a tough start against Washington with a scoreless six-inning outing against the Rockies last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran is coming off his first quality start of the season, during which he allowed two earned runs over six innings in a loss to the Nationals. He has a 3.52 ERA in 20 career games (19 starts) against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Nola will look to make it two straight victories after throwing an eight-inning, one-run gem against the Reds. His only issue in an otherwise sterling start to the season is the seven walks over his last 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has limited damage in each of his first three starts, but he has not yet completed six innings. The righty has had more consistent command of his offspeed pitches with the subdued windup he developed  this winter.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta has yet to give up a home run in his first three outings, while striking out 19 in 16 2/3 innings. He also hasn't given up a base on balls in his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy made a quick recovery from the partially separated left shoulder ailment that limited him to five innings against the Nationals on Wednesday.  The veteran has been effective, but is still looking to gain consistency with his slider.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez showed that his changeup can be a dangerous out pitch for him in a dominant 6 2/3-inning, seven-strikeout performance in his last outing against the Rays.

home_pitcher_note: Wisler was promoted from Triple-A Gwinnett to start in place of Anibal Sanchez, who injured his right leg while running Wednesday. Wisler’s only start last year was made against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: The numbers behind Harvey’s 4.80 ERA are a mixed bag. Although Harvey sports a 13-to-3 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 15 innings, opponents are batting .290 off him and slugging .484. He’s generated swinging strikes on just 8.7 percent of his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb has recently shown signs he’s capable of living up to the expectations set when he was one of the game’s top prospects. The left-hander’s ability to command his changeup has enhanced the value of his curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Effectiveness hasn’t been Syndergaard’s problem. Efficiency has. Syndergaard has yet to throw a pitch in the seventh inning this season, lasting just 5 1/3 last time out despite 101 pitches. He is 0-1 lifetime in four starts against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran had both of his fastballs and his two breaking pitches working as he had nine strikeouts (his highest total since '16) on Monday night vs. the Phils. Teheran can credit his slider for the success he’s had in three of his first four starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, deGrom became the first Mets starter to pitch into the eighth inning, though it backfired when he and the bullpen coughed up a five-run lead. Rather than move to 3-0 on the season, deGrom took his second consecutive no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Romano was cruising until the sixth inning on Tuesday at Milwaukee, when he gave up Eric Thames’ two-run homer for a 2-0 loss. It was a fastball over the plate and Romano was mad at himself, especially since first base was open.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz struggled with fastball command his last time out, but he found enough consistency with the slider to complete six innings vs. the Phillies. He has minimized damage and shown more consistency with a shorter windup.

home_pitcher_note: Toussaint struggled in a one-inning relief appearance Saturday, but he has impressed in each of his first three career starts.  The rookie has an outside shot of gaining a spot on Atlanta’s potential playoff roster.
away_pitcher_note: Flaherty's last outing was plenty to keep the Cards in a position to win, as the righty allowed one run in six innings vs. the Dodgers in a 3-0 loss Friday.  While it wasn't the result he wanted, Flaherty was still impressive with eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman cruised through his first six starts with the Braves before encountering trouble in his past two. He surrendered a season-high 12 hits while facing the Phillies as a member of the Orioles on July 12.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez is 1-3 with a 7.52 ERA in seven starts since pitching 6 1/3 scoreless innings Aug. 3 against the Marlins. Velasquez lasted just two innings in his last start Saturday against the Marlins, allowing four runs.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran will be attempting to strengthen his bid to gain a spot in the postseason rotation. He posted a 4.91 ERA in three starts against the Phillies in April but has not faced them since.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta went 4-3 with a 3.26 ERA in 11 starts through May. He is 2-10 with a 5.57 ERA in 19 starts since. The Phillies point to his 3.42 xFIP, which ranks 17th out of 66 qualified starters as just one reason to remain high on him.

home_pitcher_note:
Foltynewicz will be looking to rebound after his fastball velocity dipped on Monday, when he 
allowed six earned runs over just 4 2/3 innings. He completed at least five innings in 27 of his 28 previous starts.
away_pitcher_note: Since pitching eight scoreless innings in Arizona on Aug. 3, Arrieta has struggled. He has posted a 6.02 ERA (25 earned runs in 37 1/3 innings) in seven starts since in raising his ERA from 3.11 to 3.77.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez will be starting on regular rest and looking to build on the strong outing he produced Tuesday, when he baffled the Cardinals with his cutter and splitter. The veteran has a 3.02 ERA over his past nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nola's numbers have dipped a bit so far in September. In four starts this month, Nola has a 5.01 ERA and has allowed eight homers, matching his home run total from his first 27 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Syndergaard’s penultimate start of the season will come against a Braves team he hasn’t faced since May. In two outings against Atlanta this year, Syndergaard is 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA, going six innings with three runs each time.
away_pitcher_note: Toussaint has made a good impression in each of his first four career starts and may earn a postseason roster spot as a long reliever or potential fourth starter. He’s pitched into the sixth inning in three of his four starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets tweaked their rotation so that deGrom can make his last start of the season on regular rest. He is likely to win the National League ERA title and, in front of his home fans, will make his final pitch for the NL Cy Young Award.
away_pitcher_note: Newcomb will be making one last attempt to remain a candidate for the National League Division Series roster. The lefty has extended his command woes while producing a 7.44 ERA over his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his first 12 outings, Vargas went 2-8 with an 8.75 ERA. Since that time, he is 4-1 with a 3.11 mark. In three starts against the Braves, Vargas is 1-2 with a 6.14 ERA, though that was the old Vargas; he hasn’t faced them in over seven weeks.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran revived his candidacy for a postseason rotation spot as he took a more aggressive approach during Friday’s outing against the Phillies. He has a 1.69 ERA in four starts against the Mets this season.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff, who was arguably the team’s best pitcher in 2016, has missed almost the entire season because of a nerve issue in his right fingers. He has been pitching out of the bullpen recently, but the Phillies want to get him one start before enterin
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz will be tuning up for his expected start in Game 1 of the National League Division Series. The down-ballot NL Cy Young Award candidate has a 2.60 ERA over his past 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: The National League Cy Young Award candidate will make his final start of the season. He could finish as high as second in the Cy Young voting. Nola is finishing one of the greatest seasons by a Phillies starting pitcher in recent memory.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez resurrected his career this year and now will have a chance to extend his success with at least one playoff start. The right-hander has a 2.45 ERA over his past six starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies are going to give Suarez the final start of the season. Suarez could figure into the rotation’s mix next season, depending on his continued development and how the Phillies handle the offseason.
away_pitcher_note: Gausman proved to be the most influential starting-pitching acquisition made before this year’s non-waiver Trade Deadline. The former Oriole has a 2.80 ERA in nine starts for Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: It might be a surprise that Ryu will start Game 1 instead of Clayton Kershaw, but he's pitched well enough to earn it: He has a 1.88 ERA in nine starts since his Aug. 15 return from a groin injury and a 2.81 ERA in three career postseason starts.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz will start the Braves' first postseason game since 2013. While he was a first-time All-Star with a career-best 2.85 ERA this year, he lost his only start against the Dodgers, allowing four runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Dodgers have won Kershaw's last four NLDS starts dating back to 2015, and despite a shaky 2018 finale for the ace, he's pitched his team to victory in his last eight outings. He struck out eight in 7 2/3 innings against Atlanta on July 27.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez enjoyed a career renaissance this season, posting a 2.83 ERA and striking out 135 batters in 136 2/3 innings. The 34-year-old is 2-4 with a 2.79 ERA in 38 2/3 career innings in the postseason.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb will make his first career postseason start after throwing two scoreless relief innings in Game 1. The lefty carried a no-hitter through 8 2/3 innings against the Dodgers on July 29 in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Buehler will make his first career postseason start after tossing 6 2/3 scoreless innings vs. the Rockies in Monday's NL West tiebreaker. The rookie faced the Braves once in the regular season, giving up one run over 5 1/3 innings on June 8.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz will start Game 4 for the Braves in Atlanta. He lasted just two innings in the NLDS opener, yielding four runs on three hits -- two homers -- and three walks against the Dodgers in his first career playoff appearance.
away_pitcher_note: Hill was dominant at many points in last year’s postseason, finishing with a 2.55 ERA over four starts. The southpaw held the Braves to three hits and struck out eight over seven scoreless innings back on July 26 in Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Nola hopes to build upon a brilliant 2018, when he finished third for the National League Cy Young Award. He gets his second consecutive Opening Day start. The last Phillies pitcher to have more than two? Roy Halladay from 2010-12.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran will join Warren Spahn as the only Braves pitchers to make at least six consecutive Opening Day starts. The right-hander has posted a 2.73 ERA in his previous five season openers.

home_pitcher_note: Pivetta is the sabermetrician’s pick to click in 2019. He has great stuff, so while he posted a 4.77 ERA in 33 appearances (32 starts) last season, he also posted a 3.80 FIP. A step forward would be huge for the Phillies’ rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson, who is ranked the club's No. 7 prospect, has thrived since developing a changeup last year, but his slider is what impressed the Braves most this past spring.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies are hoping for a bit of a resurgence for Arrieta in his second season in Philly. He was 9-6 with a 3.11 ERA through his first 22 starts last season. He finished 1-5 with a 6.35 ERA in his final nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Blessed with the highest upside among the Braves’ highly-regarded young pitchers, Wright exceeded expectations throughout an impressive spring. He’ll be making his first start and looking to validate his status as MLB Pipeline’s 30th-best prospect.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb may have been sent to the Minors had he not showed enhanced aggression in a March 20 start. Command has always been an issue for the lefty, who impressed early last year and then was briefly removed from the rotation in September.
away_pitcher_note: Fresh off signing a four-year extension, Hendricks will start the opener in Atlanta. The righty did not pitch against the Braves in '18, but he has a 2.33 ERA with 18 strikeouts vs. six walks in 19 1/3 career innings against them.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran impressed with both his slider and fastball command during Thursday's effective Opening Day start in Philadelphia. His 91.3 mph average four-seam velocity would have ranked third among all of his 2018 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lester picked up a win on Opening Day in Texas with six solid innings, allowing two runs on four hits with three strikeouts and two walks. He is 6-2 with a 2.47 ERA in nine career starts against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Fried worked out of the bullpen during the first series and hasn't completed more than two innings since going five on March 19. The Braves will likely try to get him through the lineup at least one time.
away_pitcher_note: In Texas on Saturday, Darvish labored with his command and had a career-high seven walks in 2 2/3 innings. He allowed three runs on two hits. Chicago is hoping Darvish will show better control and tempo in a less emotional setting in Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman battled shoulder discomfort when he reported to camp, but he'll enter this season debut healthy. His fastball was back in the mid-90s during his last couple spring starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez set a career-high with seven strikeouts in his first start of the season, a win over the Rockies. His fastball touched 96 mph. Of his 23 changeups thrown, he had nine swinging strikes. On the road last year, his ERA was 4.84 in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wright will be making his second career start and first at SunTrust Park. The highly regarded prospect battled tough conditions and fatigued during the fifth inning of Sunday's loss to the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start, Alcantara threw eight shutout innings, striking out six without a walk in a win over the Rockies. In seven career starts dating back to 2018, Alcantara has lasted at least seven innings four times. His fastball topped at 99.3 mph.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb created encouragement with his last spring start, but he struggled with his command again during Monday's season debut. The big lefty has been aiming to find more consistency with his curveball, which has plagued him since the start of 2018.
away_pitcher_note: Building back from surgery on his left lat will take time, but Smith showed plenty of promise in his first start, fanning eight vs. the Mets in his first appearance since June 2018. He was lifted after 87 pitches, and likely will be under 100 again.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland gave up three runs in the first inning -- an error didn't help -- in his last start, a loss at Tampa Bay. He struck out 10, but his pitch count ran high as he lasted just 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran struggled through the first couple innings of Wednesday's start against the Cubs but cruised toward the end of his five-inning outing. His velocity was down from his Opening Day start, but he still had some success with his slider.

home_pitcher_note: The weather forecast calls for 72 degrees and partly cloudy. That's much better than last year, when Marquez struggled through 27 degrees and lost to the Braves in the Rockies' 2018 home opener.
away_pitcher_note: Fried will attempt to build off his stellar six scoreless innings against the Cubs last Thursday. The lefty retired the first 17 batters he faced and allowed only one hit. Increased fastball velocity has enhanced the value of his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: The righty faced one more than the minimum over seven scoreless in Friday's season debut. Gausman battled right shoulder inflammation early in Spring Training, but his velo has been slightly better than it was late last year.
away_pitcher_note: Because the Mets skipped Jason Vargas in the rotation, Matz will return on five days’ rest to open the Mets’ four-game set in Atlanta. Matz skated around trouble in each of his first two outings, allowing a single earned run in 10 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After battling wintry conditions in his season debut, Wright limited the Marlins to a pair of solo homers his last time out. The young prospect features a slider, but he's shown the ability to miss bats with his curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Seven walks sunk Zack Wheeler last time out against the Nationals; afterward, he blamed a mechanical flaw that he intends to fix in short order. Wheeler hopes to rebound near his Georgia hometown, where he is 2-2 with a 3.41 ERA in five career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb maintained his rotation spot as he issued just two walks over seven innings in his most recent start. Command has always been the issue for the erratic southpaw, who has struggled to get a consistent feel for his curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Pete Alonso returns to the lineup after a day off to support Jason Vargas, whose second turn in the rotation was skipped to keep the other starters on regular rest. He’ll try to find some rhythm after going 10 full days between starts, something he struggled to do with a similarly disjointed schedule early last season.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran cruised through the first four innings of Monday's start at Coors Field and then endured a six-run fifth. His velo has dropped since his season debut, but he's generated good movement when his four-seamer rests around 90 mph.
away_pitcher_note: After five long days of waiting, Jacob deGrom will return to the mound on Sunday Night Baseball following his worst start since 2017. He allowed six runs to the Twins last time out, snapping his MLB record-tying run of 26 straight quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fried has completed six innings without allowing an earned run in either of his two starts. The lefty has never completed more than 118 innings in a professional season. So, while he may eventually be sent down, the Braves will ride the hot hand.
away_pitcher_note: Ray had a no-hitter through five innings last time out against the Rangers before allowing a single to lead off the sixth. His pitch count rose quickly, thanks in part to 10 strikeouts, and he did not record an out in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman has battled early command issues in both of his first two starts, but he has worked into the sixth inning of both. The right-hander's willingness to pitch up in the zone more frequently has enhanced the value of his splitter.
away_pitcher_note: Godley allowed just one run over his first five innings last time out against the Padres. In the sixth, though, things changed quickly as the Padres posted five runs, including a three-run homer by Austin Hedges.

home_pitcher_note: Soroka will be promoted from Triple-A Gwinnett to make his season debut. The Braves’ top prospect missed most of last year due to a right shoulder ailment, and he missed most of Spring Training with a separate shoulder injury.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver cruised through the first six innings of his last start against the Padres. He allowed just one run -- a homer by Manny Machado -- and three hits. In the seventh, he gave up back-to-back one-out doubles to end his night.

home_pitcher_note: Kluber is coming off his worst start of the young season, having given up six earned runs and failing to make it out of the third inning on Sunday in Kansas City. This will be his second career start against the Braves in his nine-year career.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has really had just one bad inning through his first four starts. He's throwing strikes more consistently and while he's still susceptibile against lefties, he's kept them in the park thus far.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer has picked up right where he left off in 2018.  He’s pitched to a 2.05 ERA over four starts while racking up 32 strikeouts.  On Monday against the Mariners, he pitched into the seventh inning for the third time this year.  The only concern would be his 11 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Toussaint earned this start while not allowing an earned run over six relief innings against the Mets on Saturday.  The young hurler features and impressive curveball and a changeup that has split-finger action.

home_pitcher_note: Bieber didn’t have his best stuff on Tuesday in Seattle, but he battled through six-plus innings and gave up just one run on four hits. He’s throwing his slider at a higher rate this year, and hitters are just 4-for-29 against the offering.
away_pitcher_note: Fried worked 16 1/3 innings before allowing his first earned run this season. The lefty's velocity was down during his most recent start, but he still managed to complete six innings in a third straight start.

home_pitcher_note: Gray seeks his first Reds win despite good numbers in four starts: 2.79 ERA, 0.93 WHIP, 10.2 strikeouts per nine innings and one home run allowed. Gray suffered a left calf contusion on April 11 but was OK on Wednesday at Los Angeles, striking out nine in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gausman looked sharp in his last start against the D-backs on Wednesday, allowing two runs on three hits with 10 strikeouts and a walk in seven innings. He threw first-pitch strikes to 17 of the 25 batters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Roark has allowed one run in 5 1/3 innings in each of his past two outings. He mixed five pitches effectively Thursday at San Diego in earning his first win with the Reds. He left with a shutout intact, though one of his baserunners came in to score.
away_pitcher_note: Soroka's first start of 2019 was delayed by a shoulder issue, but it was worth the wait. He allowed just one run on four hits with two walks (one intentional), two hit batsmen and six strikeouts in five innings against the D-backs on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Despite a high pitch count and a long second inning, Castillo turned in a six-inning gem for a 4-3 win over the Padres on Saturday. Of his nine strikeouts, six came via his changeup. He has 33 strikeouts using his changeup in 2019.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran endured a six-run fifth on April 8 at Coors Field, and then he struggled through another tough fifth as he lasted just 4 2/3 innings Saturday in Cleveland. The Reds' left-handed hitters could pose a problem as the righty's top weapon is a slider.

home_pitcher_note: Fried has been one of baseball's top early-season surprises. The lefty has increased the velocity of his four-seam fastball and has routinely fooled hitters with his big curveball. He's worked at least six innings in each of his first four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela ran a high pitch count in his last start, but just one pitch -- a breaking ball for Phil Gosselin's three-run double -- cemented a home loss to the Phillies. He is 3-1 with a 1.77 ERA in his last six road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz will be making his season debut. The All-Star hurler missed most of Spring Training because of a right elbow bone spur that began bothering him in his Feb. 24 spring debut.
away_pitcher_note: The advanced numbers look good. Gray's 183 ERA-plus is 83 percent above league average. He has yielded just 23 hits in 32 1/3 innings pitched. For traditional stats, he has 30 strikeouts to 13 walks and a 2.78 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman battled inconsistent velocity and struggled early to command his splitter during Tuesday's loss in Cincinnati. The Denver native will be making his first career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: His return from a left knee injury, when he lasted three innings plus three batters in a no-decision against Washington, was a struggle. Anderson’s challenge is to use his fastball aggressively in the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a career-high 109-pitch effort, Soroka will attempt to further distance himself from his previous shoulder issues. His two-seam fastball has been quite effective, as he's allowed just one run in both of his first two starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Margevicius generally boasts pinpoint command, and he had only walked more than two hitters in a game once before in his pro career. He walked five on Tuesday, but Seattle still couldn't square him up. The Padres have won three of his five starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: If Teheran can extend the success he had with his two-seam fastball, he may have more consistent success against left-handers. Control continues to be a concern, as his walk rate (4.8 BB per 9) is higher than the elevated rates that he produced both of the previous two seasons.
away_pitcher_note: The righty is coming off a masterful seven-inning, one-hit performance against Seattle in his last start, which solidified his rank among the MLB leaders in ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Fried surrendered a season-high four runs his last time out, but he continued to impress with his fastball and curveball. If he continues to make strides with his slider, he should see his strikeout rate climb.
away_pitcher_note: The 2016 first-round Draft pick, and son of former big leaguer Paul Quantrill, is slated for his debut Wednesday night. He was roughed up in his first start in '19, but since then, he's posted a 2.86 ERA with a strikeout per inning over four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz surrendered a pair of solo homers, and then faded during the seventh inning of Saturday's season debut. The All-Star hurler missed most of Spring Training because of a bone spur in his right elbow.
away_pitcher_note: Strahm continues to build up strength as a starter, racking up a career-high eight strikeouts in his last outing. He's registered an ERA of 1.50 over his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: For the first time since Aug. 15, 2018, Urena faces the Braves. On that night, the right-hander was ejected and later suspended for hitting Ronald Acuna Jr. with a pitch. In his past three starts, Urena is 1-1 with a 2.25 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gausman will have a chance to get back on track after allowing five earned runs in both of his past two outings. The right-hander dominated the Marlins over seven scoreless innings in his  season debut on April 5.

home_pitcher_note: Richards' changeup is one of the better ones in the game, with opponents hitting just .188 against it. The right-hander also has a 30.1 chase percent with that pitch. In his last two starts, however, he's served up four homers off his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Soroka has been the Braves' best starter over the past couple weeks. The top prospect has commanded his heavy sinker and four-seam fastball while allowing just one run in each of his first three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez is 1-4 in his last five starts, and free passes have been one of the issues. He's walked eight in 26 1/3 innings in that span. In his last outing, Lopez lost the feel of his off-speed pitches in the sixth inning in a loss at Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran allowed the Padres three solo home runs as he lost his third straight start Tuesday. The right-hander allowed at least six runs in two of three starts against Miami last year.

home_pitcher_note: Buehler is unbeaten, but his ERA (5.22) and WHIP (1.193) are up from his rookie season, and his strikeout-per-nine-innings rate (7.4) is down. His 3.41 FIP offers encouragement that pitching deep into October isn’t having an adverse effect in 2019.
away_pitcher_note: Gausman starts the opener of a rematch of last year's NLDS, which pushes the rest of the rotation back a day. The righty threw just 28 pitches in his last start in Miami, as he was ejected for "intentionally throwing" behind Jose Urena on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu has yet to allow more than two runs in any start this season. He held the Giants to one run in a season-high eight innings last time out, with no walks, four hits and six strikeouts. Ryu tops the Majors with an average of 0.5 walks per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fried put together his best start of the young season his last time out, allowing just one run on four hits with seven strikeouts over seven innings vs. the Padres on Wednesday. He had not issued a walk in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw labored through six innings vs. the Padres on Friday, throwing 95 pitches and allowing early homers to Manny Machado and Ian Kinsler. His slider was more effective as the game progressed, and he retired eight of his last nine.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz, who dropped Game 1 of last year's NLDS, is trying to find a groove since returning from the injured list with a right elbow bone spur. According to Statcast, his four-seamer has been 2.1 mph slower through two starts than it was in 2018.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver has allowed more than three runs just once this season, and he's 3-0 with a 1.99 ERA in his past four starts. The righty dominated the Rockies over seven innings his last time out, allowing one earned run on three hits and striking out eight.
away_pitcher_note: Soroka has further enhanced his stock while allowing less than two runs in each of his first four starts. The top prospect has displayed his effective sinker while limiting opponents to a .182 batting average.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke continued his outstanding season with six quality innings against the Rockies during which he allowed three runs on six hits and struck out four. He is 4-1 with a 2.91 ERA in 10 career starts against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran righted himself with six scoreless innings against the Marlins, but he'll now have to handle the power within Arizona's lineup. His 1.61 home runs allowed per nine innings rank as the NL's seventh-highest mark.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly has performed remarkably well in his rookie season but hit a bump during his last start. He allowed seven runs in four innings against the Rays, his first start against the team that drafted him in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Gausman threw 28 pitches before being ejected on May 3 and then returned to pitch into the fifth inning of Monday's loss to the Dodgers. His struggles this year have been influenced by higher walk and home run ratios.

home_pitcher_note: Godley was removed from the rotation 10 days ago after struggling in four of his six starts. Since then, he's made two appearances out of the bullpen and shown the organization that he's made the changes they wanted him to make.
away_pitcher_note: Fried exited his last start Tuesday vs. the Dodgers after getting struck by a liner in his left hand. The left-hander, however, came out of his Thursday side session in good shape, which puts him on track to start Sunday and not miss a start.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz hasn't had a quality start in his first three outings of the season, going 0-2 with a 5.94 ERA. Now the right-hander faces the Cardinals, against whom he owns an 8.06 ERA in five career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Flaherty still isn't pitching as deep into games as he would like. He's gone past the fifth just three times in eight starts. He's walked too many recently (seven in his last two starts), but has done a better job of keeping the ball in the park.

home_pitcher_note: Last time out, Soroka became the first MLB pitcher since earned runs became official in both leagues in 1913 to allow one or fewer earned runs as a starter in eight of his first 10 career games. He faces the Cardinals for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: Don't let Wacha's 3-0 record fool you, as his season has been more up-and-down than it would suggest. He has completed six innings just twice in seven starts and has a 6.32 ERA in three starts since returning from a knee injury.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran has been great in his last two starts, allowing one run over 12 innings, and he has a 2.88 ERA over his past four outings. However, he's winless in his last five starts. The righty has a 3.18 ERA in six career starts vs. St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright made his first seven-inning start in 13 months his last time out and generated a season-high 23 called strikes. Key to his early-season success has been his curveball, which Wainwright is throwing at a higher clip than ever before.

home_pitcher_note: Fried exited his May 7 start after getting hit in the left hand with a second-inning comebacker, then allowed a season-high nine hits five days later against the D-backs. He has a 5.89 ERA over his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin looks to continue his solid run, opening the series in Atlanta with a chance to even his record at 4-4. Chacin has pitched to a 1.59 ERA over his past three starts, holding hitters to a .186 average and .555 OPS.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman will be making his first start since serving a five-game suspension levied for throwing behind Jose Urena earlier this month. He has a 6.04 ERA over his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his return from the injured list, looking to pick up where he left off when he sustained a finger laceration in late April. Anderson pitched to a 1.86 ERA in his only two starts of the season before being sidelined.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz made some mechancial changes he hopes will halt the struggles he's had in each of his first four starts. His fastball velocity has been down, and his once-reliable slider has been a liability.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff has been stellar in his past four starts, going 4-0 with a 1.23 ERA. He allowed one hit over six scoreless innings against the Phillies on Tuesday, winning his fifth consecutive decision.

home_pitcher_note: Suarez will be recalled for his first MLB start this season. In six starts for Triple-A Sacramento, he went 2-3 with a 6.33 ERA. The left-hander was optioned at the end of Spring Training after going 7-13 with a 4.49 ERA in 29 starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Soroka's sub-1.00 ERA has come with the benefit of him limiting opponents to two hits in 40 at-bats with runners in scoring position. Opponents have produced a ground ball on 61 percent of the balls put in play against the Braves rookie.

That includes four scoreless frames against the Dodgers in NLCS Game 2, though he wasn't sharp, walking five while striking out five in Atlanta's 8-7 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Nola starts his fourth consecutive Opening Day for the Phillies, the most since Hall of Fame left-hander Steve Carlton started 10 in a row from 1977-86. This will be the third time Nola has faced the Braves on Opening Day.
away_pitcher_note: Fried will be making his first career Opening Day start and the first by a Braves left-hander since Tom Glavine in 2002. The southpaw finished fifth in National League Cy Young Award voting last year after going 7-0 with a 2.25 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler enjoyed a successful debut season with the Phillies in 2020, pitching more efficiently as he went deeper into games. The club has high hopes for Wheeler, Aaron Nola and Zach Eflin atop their rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Morton will be making his first start since signing a one-year, $15 million deal in November. The 37-year-old right-hander debuted for the Braves in 2008 but was traded to the Pirates a year later. His career finally blossomed with the ‘17 World Series champion Astros, and he finished third in balloting for the ‘19 American League Cy Young Award.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies talked about Eflin not being their No. 3 starter this season, but he's 1C behind Aaron Nola (1A) and Zack Wheeler (1B). Eflin certainly has the stuff and the mindset to take a step forward in 2021.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson impressed over six regular-season starts last year and then began his postseason career with 17 2/3 scoreless innings before finally allowing a run in the third inning of Game 7 of the National League Championship Series. The young right-hander relies heavily on his changeup, which limited opponents to a .104 batting average last year. This will be his first appearance against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will make his sixth Opening Day start in seven seasons for the Nationals when they host the Braves. He built up to 90 pitches during Spring Training. Scherzer, who is entering his 14th season, said, "Everyone gets butterflies on Opening Day. That's a good thing."
away_pitcher_note: Smyly will be out to prove the Braves were wise to take an $11 million gamble on him, despite the fact he lasted five innings in just two of five starts last season. He displayed higher velocity and an improved spin rate with his curveball while recording 38 strikeouts over his final 22 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fedde gets the nod out of the bullpen, as the Nationals' rotation is short two starters. Last season, Fedde went 1-3 with a 4.95 ERA in eight starts in place of an injured Stephen Strasburg.
away_pitcher_note: Fried battled command issues during the early portion of his Opening Day start in Philadelphia, but found a groove near the end of his five-inning effort. The lefty posted the lowest hard-hit rate among qualified MLB pitchers last year.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg makes his first start since August 2020. He was limited to only five innings last year because of carpal tunnel neuritis in his right hand. He is 14-12 with a 4.07 ERA in 34 career starts against the Braves.

Morton will be starting the home opener, and attempting to bounce back from his season-opening loss. The veteran cruised through four innings against the Phillies on Saturday, but encountered trouble during a decisive two-run fifth.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler will face the Braves for the second time in less than a week. This time, the outing will take place at Truist Park. Last Saturday, Wheeler had two hits and two RBIs as he allowed just one hit and struck out 10 across seven innings in the Phillies' 4-0 victory at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will get his second start of the season after a 2-1 loss Sunday. Anderson had a rough first inning, with 27 pitches, but recovered in the second to end the game with seven strikeouts and one run on four hits over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin allowed one run in seven innings in his season debut Sunday against the Braves. He struck out eight and walked one as he hopes to take a step forward this season and join the conversation of elite NL starters.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly's curveball was effective as he recorded eight strikeouts and allowed just two earned runs in his season debut against the Nationals. The veteran lefty completed more than four innings in just two of five starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Moore struggled on Monday in his Phillies' debut. After he retired the first seven batters he faced, striking out four, he lost command of his pitches. He exited after just 3 1/3 innings, although he held the Mets two just two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Ynoa will be making his second start of the season after impressing manager Brian Snitker in Atlanta's 2-0 win against the Nationals on Wednesday. That was Ynoa's sixth career start and the first time he's gone at least five innings. He struck out five and allowed two hits.
away_pitcher_note: Alcantara matched a career high with 10 strikeouts in his Tuesday start vs. the Cardinals. Through two starts, he has allowed three runs (two earned) in 12 innings, with four walks and 17 strikeouts. The 25-year-old righty did not face the Braves in 2020.

home_pitcher_note: After a disappointing start against the Nationals on Wednesday, Fried looks to pick up his second win of the season against the Marlins.  In his last start, Fried just couldn't settle in and find a groove in his two innings.
away_pitcher_note: López was on his way to a second straight scoreless start to open the season on Wednesday, but Yadier Molina hit a cutter outside the zone for a two-out, two-run homer in the seventh. Since allowing seven runs over 1 2/3 frames to the Braves on Sept. 9, 2020, López has a 1.55 ERA in five regular-season starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his first two starts of the season, Charlie Morton has been an example of consistency. In his 11 innings pitched, Morton has 12 strikeouts, 10 hits and a 3.27 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: A Georgia native, Neidert worked around trouble in his first MLB start, giving up three hits and walking five in 4 1/3 innings vs. the Mets last Thursday. The bullpen allowed an inherited runner to score the only charged run to his line. Miami's No. 12 prospect is getting his shot in the rotation with Elieser Hernandez on the IL.

home_pitcher_note: Despite some rough starts, Anderson has continually worked out of jams and put the Braves in the position to win. He picked up his first win of the season in a 5-4 victory against the Phillies on Saturday to give Atlanta its first series win of '21.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers matched a career high with 10 strikeouts on Saturday vs. the Mets, beating Jacob deGrom with six scoreless innings. Miami's No. 7 prospect returns to the site of an oft-cited learning experience, when the offense gave him a 3-0 lead in the first before he gave up four runs in the bottom half. The lefty finished strong with six straight K's.

home_pitcher_note: Davies lasted 1 2/3 innings in his most recent start, allowing seven runs in a loss to the Pirates on Saturday. The righty struck out two and walked three. Davies has a 1.93 ERA in just two starts (14 innings) in his career against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Wright was recalled from the alternate training site to start the series opener against the Cubs after the Braves placed Drew Smyly on the 10-day IL. This will be Wright's first appearance of the season after he went 2-4 with a 5.21 ERA in eight starts in 2020.

home_pitcher_note: Williams took a loss in Pittsburgh on Sunday, when he allowed five runs on 10 hits in 3 1/3 innings. The righty struck out three and walked two. Williams has a 2.77 ERA in three career games (two starts) against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Ynoa has impressed with a fastball that has touched 100 mph and a swing-and-miss slider. He was used as a piggyback starter last year but has a chance to stay in Atlanta's rotation, at least until Mike Soroka returns.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs skipped Hendricks' start in Milwaukee earlier this week when the righty reported feeling under the weather. If he continues to improve, he will start against Atlanta on Sunday. Hendricks spun six shutout innings against the Brewers on April 7.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson will make his 2021 debut in the Braves’ series finale in Chicago. Wilson closed out 2020 on a high note with a dazzling one-run, five-strikeout performance in Game 4 of the 2020 National League Championship Series.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon aims to bounce back after he was knocked for five runs and eight hits in 3 2/3 innings last time out by the Blue Jays, marking Taillon's second start since returning from a 2019 Tommy John procedure.
away_pitcher_note: Morton made a couple of costly mistakes during a four-run third inning against the Marlins on Wednesday. But he felt his curveball was as good as it's been all year. He's completed six innings in both of his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Kluber has yet to complete five innings in any of his three starts this season. He tossed 77 pitches last time out vs. the Blue Jays, allowing three runs and six hits over four innings. Kluber has permitted 16 hits in 10 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson allowed three homers in his final spring start, and he's surrendered a .448 slugging percentage through his first three starts of the regular season. He allowed just one home run over 51 innings and surrendered a .230 slugging percentage  over 10 starts (includes the playoffs) last year.

home_pitcher_note: Ynoa looked nearly unhittable in his first two starts, then allowed three homers and six runs over four innings on Saturday at Wrigley Field. The hard-throwing righty has a triple-digit fastball and a plus slider. But his changeup is a work in progress.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver is off to a good start this year after a disappointing 2020 season. He allowed four runs over four innings against the Nats on Saturday, but he was outstanding in his start prior to that, holding the Reds to one hit and one walk over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson pitched effectively over five solid innings in his season debut against the Cubs on Sunday. The righty delivered six strong innings in a win over the Dodgers in Game 4 of last year's NLCS.
away_pitcher_note: Gallen was not overly sharp by his standards Tuesday against the Reds. He allowed three runs on four hits and four walks over 5 2/3 innings. He missed his first two starts of the year with a hairline fracture in his right forearm.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly will be activated from the injured list to make his first start since feeling left forearm discomfort after his April 11 outing against Philadelphia. The lefty has recorded one strikeout per inning, but he's been hurt by the long ball through two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner had his best start of the year Sunday against the Nats. He picked up the win while allowing just one run on two hits and one walk over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has felt good about his curveball in both of his previous two starts. The veteran will be pitching with an extra day of rest. He limited the Yankees to one run over six innings on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has a 12.10 ERA in his past three starts (9 2/3 innings), which includes allowing four runs in four innings to the Braves on April 16. He gave up two runs in four innings vs. the Brewers in his last start on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson constructed one of his finest starts when he tossed 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Yankees on Wednesday. His 64 strikeouts are the most by any Braves pitcher through his first 10 career appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Williams allowed one run over five innings against Atlanta on April 17 in Chicago. In his last outing, he held the Mets to two runs over five innings on Thursday, ending with six strikeouts and one walk in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Ynoa has impressed in all but one of his starts this year, in which the Cubs tagged him for three homers over just four innings on April 17. The young hurler possesses a plus fastball and a swing-and-miss slider.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks was solid last time out, giving up two runs (on solo homers) over six innings Friday vs. the Brewers. He struck out six and walked one. He allowed seven runs in four innings to the Braves on April 18, following 10 days of rest.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson will be asked to go through the lineup at least once while serving as an opener. The right-hander threw 61 pitches on Sunday, so he'll be taking the mound on short rest. He allowed three runs (two earned) over five innings against the Cubs on April 18.
away_pitcher_note: Alzolay's slider was sharp Saturday vs. the Brewers, helping him to seven strikeouts in 4 2/3 innings. This will be Alzolay's first outing vs. Atlanta since his first career start in 2019.

home_pitcher_note: Two outings ago, Ray tied a career high with six walks. Last time out, he didn't issue a single walk and struck out nine, and saw his fastball velocity jump to 98.3 mph. The talented lefty will look for more of the latter against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Smyly returned from the injured list Sunday and immediately gave up five runs in the first inning vs. the D-backs. The lefty allowed only one more run over his four-inning outing. But none of his first three starts have been encouraging.

Anderson has tossed 13 2/3 scoreless innings over his past two starts. The rookie has impressed and baffled opponents with a changeup that he is willing to throw against both right- and left-handed hitters.

away_pitcher_note: Ynoa will face the Nationals for the second time this season after shutting them out over five innings on two hits on April 7. away_pitcher_note: Fried will make his return to the mound after exiting with a right hamstring strain in an April 13 loss against the Marlins. Fried has made adjustments and feels ready to return from the injury, after posting an 11.45 ERA through his first three starts.
