away_pitcher_note: Smyly will look to pick up his first win of the season in the Braves' series finale against the Nationals. Smyly enters with an 8.05 ERA through 19 innings and an 0-2 record.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has pitched into the sixth in five straight starts, but he hasn't yet put two strong starts together. His best start of the season was completed April 9, when he limited the Phillies to one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin continues to pound the strike zone and keep the Phillies in games. He has walked just two batters in 38 2/3 innings this season, and one of those walks was intentional. His 1.3% walk rate is second-best among all qualified starters.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson had thrown 15 2/3 consecutive scoreless innings before allowing at least one run in each of the last three innings completed against the Blue Jays on Sunday. The rookie hurler relies heavily on what has consistently been a reliable changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez earned his fourth consecutive start in place of left-hander Matt Moore after allowing only one run in six innings in Monday's 4-3 victory over the Brewers. It was the second time since 2019 that Velasquez completed six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ynoa has become one of the game's top stories this year. The right-hander has allowed two runs or fewer in five of six starts and he has homered in both of his past two games.
away_pitcher_note: Nola threw 114 pitches in six innings Tuesday against the Brewers. He is 11-6 with a 3.03 ERA in 21 career starts against the Braves, although he is 2-4 with a 3.97 ERA in eight starts at Truist Park in Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson was recalled to start the opener against Toronto. In five Interleague games (one start) in his career, the righty has a 10.13 ERA. Wilson faced the Jays back in 2019, hurling  1 1/3 innings of relief, allowing two runs on four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Ray has dependably worked five or more innings in all five starts this season, allowing no more than three runs per outing. He has earned three consecutive quality starts, with 23 strikeouts over his past three appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Fried returned from the injured list to toss five strong innings against the Nationals on Wednesday. The lefty showed better command than he had when he struggled through three starts before straining his hamstring on April 13.
away_pitcher_note: Ryu's best start came at home (6 2/3 innings, one unearned run vs. the Yankees), but he's mostly worked as a visitor this season. Wednesday marks his sixth road start out of seven, as he aims to win consecutive starts for the first time since 2019.

home_pitcher_note: Morton matched a career-short start when he recorded just two outs against the Phillies on Friday. The veteran hurler has not found a consistent feel for his curveball and cutter. Consequently, he's allowed at least four runs in four of his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Despite how thin the Blue Jays' rotation is, Stripling's spot could be hanging in the balance based on this start. He has failed to complete five innings in three of four starts, and his WHIP is nearing 2.000.

home_pitcher_note: Houser had quite a night in his previous start at Miami. Besides matching a career-high 10 strikeouts, he hit a home run for the second time this season off the same pitcher: Marlins lefty Daniel Castano.
away_pitcher_note: Smyly will be starting with three extra days of rest. Instead of having him face the powerful Blue Jays lineup, the Braves opted to push the lefty back a few days. He was effective in his last start against a Juan Soto-less Nationals lineup.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson pitched three innings on 52 pitches last time out against the Marlins in his first start since returning from the injured list for a right leg injury. He should be able to extend a bit more against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson hasn't been as dominant as he was when he broke into the big leagues in the second half of last season. But he has completed at least six innings in three of his past four starts, and the Braves have won five of his past six.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is coming off his best start of the season, a seven-inning, one-hit, scoreless gem against the Cardinals. He already has three starts this season of five or more innings with no more than one hit allowed.
away_pitcher_note: Ynoa has become the modern-day Babe Ruth.  He has homered twice during his four-game hitting streak, and he has allowed two runs or fewer in six of seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fried will be looking to make a third straight strong start since being activated from the injured list. The lefty's improved command has made both his breaking pitches more effective than they were during the first few weeks of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Walker had a quality start Wednesday  allowing one run on four hits and three walks over seven innings against the Orioles. He ranks seventh in the Majors in opponents' batting average (.170).

home_pitcher_note: Davidson will be brought up to give each of the current rotation members an extra day of rest during this cycle. The lefty, who has a 0.64 ERA through two starts for Triple-A Gwinnett, will also be auditioning to permanently fill the one vacant spot in Atlanta's rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Castro will make his second start as an opener this year, after he tossed one scoreless inning in that role against the Cardinals on May 5. Only one Braves hitter has more than two career at-bats against him.

home_pitcher_note: Morton hasn't completed five innings in either of his past two starts. The veteran right-hander's inconsistent cutter has plagued him throughout the season.
away_pitcher_note: Peterson is coming off an impressive 7 1/3-inning outing, during which he allowed two runs on four hits with nine strikeouts against Tampa Bay. Despite a banged-up lineup, Peterson looks to propel the Mets to a sweep in Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly has put a rocky April behind him by impressing in his past two starts. The lefty's recent success has been a product of avoiding the home run woes that plagued him over his first four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Crowe had a season-high five strikeouts in five innings his last time out last Thursday, but a rough fifth inning (three runs allowed) vs. the Giants sent him to a loss

home_pitcher_note: Anderson carried a no-hit bid into the seventh inning of Saturday's start in Milwaukee. The young right-hander has held an opponent hitless through the first five innings of two of his first 15 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson had his first real shaky outing his last time out, allowing four runs in five innings to the Giants, his former club, on Saturday. But he rebounded from two first-inning homers to keep the Pirates in the game before they walked it off in the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson will make the start for the Braves as Atlanta looks to set up a series victory. The young right-hander has struggled with a 5.50 ERA in 18 innings over four starts. His only previous experience against Pittsburgh was in 2018 when he fired five scoreless innings in his MLB debut.
away_pitcher_note: Keller's ERA still sits above 7, but his start Sunday was a reassuring sign that he may be figuring things out. He racked up a season-high eight strikeouts and located his slider well -- a pitch that has been inconsistent.

home_pitcher_note: Fried is being given an extra day of rest after experiencing cramping in his left hand on Monday against the Mets. The lefty has allowed three runs over the 17 innings he has completed since being activated from the injured list.
away_pitcher_note: For the first time this season, Brubaker allowed more than three runs in a start Tuesday, giving up five runs to the Cardinals. All five came in the first three innings of his 5 2/3 frames on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Richards has been tremendous in his last five starts, going 4-0 with a 2.27 ERA. This will be the just the second time Richards has faced the Braves in his career; he fired six shutout innings against them on June 14, 2014, as a member of the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Morton followed two disappointing starts by limiting the Mets to one run over six innings on Wednesday. His curveball has remained effective, but an inconsistent cutter has been his primary nemesis this year.

home_pitcher_note: Having spent most of his career in the NL East, Pivetta has an extensive history against the Braves, going 5-2 with a 4.74 ERA in 12 starts. Pivetta has been solid at home this season, going 2-0 with a 3.16 ERA in five starts while holding opponents to a .189 average.
away_pitcher_note: Smyly has allowed at least two homers in four of his past six outings. The velocity of his four-seam fastball is down a full mile per hour from last year. His velocity increase was a selling point when the Braves gave him a one-year, $11 million deal in November.

home_pitcher_note: Walker will come off the injured list after missing one start due to a bout of left-side tightness. He threw live batting practice and bullpen sessions without issue this week, lining him up for something approximating a normal workload.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson returns to his home state having allowed fewer than two runs in four of his past six starts. This run began on April 21, when he tossed 6 2/3 scoreless innings with his grandmother and parents in attendance at Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Morton navigated his way through a first-inning threat on his way to limiting the Red Sox potent offense to one unearned run over seven innings on Tuesday. The veteran has gained a better feel for his curveball as the season has progressed.
away_pitcher_note: Ross has not allowed more than two earned runs in five of his six road starts this season. He tossed four shutout innings against the Reds on Wednesday before rain cut his outing short.

home_pitcher_note: Fried has allowed exactly one run in each of the four starts he has made since returning from the injured list. He matched a season-high eight strikeouts when he tossed six strong innings against the Mets on May 17.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg struck out eight and allowed only one hit over six shutout innings against the Braves on April 7. He has a career 3.94 ERA in 35 starts vs. Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly will be pitching with two extra days of rest when he makes his third start of the season against the Nationals. away_pitcher_note: Lester will start against the Braves on short rest after pitching four innings on Saturday against the Brewers. He will take the mound after the Nationals deemed Erick Fedde was not ready to do so.

home_pitcher_note: To reshuffle their rotation for the upcoming Dodgers series, the Braves will call up Davidson to make what could be just a spot start. Davidson will be making his second start of the season. He allowed three runs over six innings against the Mets on May 18.
away_pitcher_note: The southpaw allowed his fifth first-inning home run of the year against the Brewers on Saturday, which is the second most in the Majors. The most first-inning homers Corbin has allowed in his nine seasons was six in 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will be looking to bounce back after lasting just four innings against the Mets on Saturday. The young hurler will be facing the Dodgers for the first time since allowing two runs and five hits over three innings in Game 7 of the National League Championship Series.
away_pitcher_note: Urias is looking to bounce back from one of the worst starts of his career. Against the Giants in his last outing, Urias allowed a career-high seven runs (six earned) on 11 hits. The Dodgers are 8-3 in games started by Urias this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Braves have won the past three games started by Morton, who has posted a 2.50 ERA over that span. As his sinker and cutter have given him problems, he's attempted to find comfort with his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw has been slightly better on the road this season, going 4-2 with a 3.06 ERA in six starts away from Dodger Stadium. He has struck out 31 over 32 1/3 road innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fried will be facing the Dodgers for the first time since Game 6 of the 2020 NLCS. In that outing, he surrendered three runs in the first but didn't allow another run over the remainder of his 6 2/3-inning effort.
away_pitcher_note: Bauer has been stellar for the Dodgers this season, but the right-hander is trying to fix his home run problem. Bauer has allowed 13 homers, which is already four more than he allowed last season in only three more innings.

home_pitcher_note: Last Tuesday, Nola became the ninth pitcher in Phillies history to record 1,000 strikeouts. He is the third Phils pitcher to reach 1,000 before turning 28: Nola (27 years, 362 days), Steve Carlton (27 years, 137 days) and Cole Hamels (27 years, 174 days).
away_pitcher_note: Smyly will make his second start against the Phillies, who accounted for the first of the five times the lefty has allowed at least two homers in a game this year. His 2.70 home runs per nine innings would rank as the league's worst if he had enough innings to qualify.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin has not pitched since May 30 as the Phillies try to keep him fresh for the six-month season. He has already thrown 68 innings this year after tossing 59 innings last season.
away_pitcher_note: Davidson earned another start after limiting the Nationals to one hit over 5 2/3 scoreless innings on Thursday. The lefty's command issues didn't prove to be a problem as he managed to pitch around five walks. This will be his fourth career start.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler has pitched like a National League Cy Young candidate this season, but he sure could use a little help from his teammates. Wheeler suffers from some of the worst run support in baseball among qualified starters.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson held the Dodgers hitless through the first four innings of Friday's start, but he was chased during the fifth and needed 98 pitches to record 13 outs. The young hurler did not complete five innings in either of his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Alcantara played the role of stopper to perfection on Sunday, pitching a season-high-tying eight innings against the Pirates. He allowed just one unearned run to help the Marlins snap an eight-game skid.
away_pitcher_note: Morton will be looking to win a fourth straight start. As the veteran has posted a 2.74 ERA over his past four starts, he has been able to avoid the big innings that sunk him during the early weeks of this season. He still has allowed at least three runs in an inning in six of his 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Thompson wasn't used out of the bullpen Friday night against the Braves, so the Marlins are hoping to get at least three or four innings from him on Saturday. Thompson last appeared in a game on Monday against the Red Sox. He pitched three innings and allowed two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Fried has posted a 2.41 ERA in six starts since returning from the injured list. The lefty stumbled against the Nationals on June 1, but returned with six strong innings against the Dodgers on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: López went a career-high eight innings his last time out vs. the Rockies. But the Braves always give him trouble, including six runs over four frames on April 13 in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Smyly's turn remains the trouble spot for Atlanta's rotation. He has allowed three runs or fewer in six of his past seven starts, but he has completed just 4 1/3 innings in each of his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: In three starts this season, Davidson has impressed with a 1.53 ERA over 17 2/3 innings. He has allowed just three earned runs on 10 hits with 14 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez's run of rough outings continued last week, as he allowed six earned runs over 4 2/3 innings against the Astros. His season, now 12 starts in, can be broken up like this: 5-0, 3.82 ERA in the first six; 0-4, 8.49 ERA in the past six.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has impressed this season. In his last outing against the Phillies on June 10, Anderson threw seven shutout innings, allowing just four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Richards has faced the Braves only twice in his career, although one of those times came three weeks ago, when he allowed three runs over 5 2/3 innings in a loss. After going 4-0 in five starts from April 27 through May 19, he hasn't won in the four outings since.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will attempt to bounce back after lasting just four innings against the Marlins on Friday. The veteran hurler has allowed at least three runs in an inning in seven of his 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gant will look to flush his past two starts, where he's struggled to get deep after serving as a reliable stopgap. Most concerning is that the walks have come back to bite the righty, with five in his last start (all in one inning) and eight over his last two.

home_pitcher_note: Fried allowed a pair of home runs during Saturday's loss in Miami. He had allowed just one homer over his past six starts combined.
away_pitcher_note: Martínez was sharp in his last start (two unearned runs over seven frames) following two clunkers (15 combined earned runs over 4 2/3). The righty has a 3.90 ERA in 11 games (four starts) against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson will return to the Majors to take the turn previously reserved for the recently injured Tucker Davidson. The right-hander allowed three runs over 12 2/3 innings in the two starts he made for Atlanta in May.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright will make his 15th start (20th appearance) against the team that drafted him, with a 3.63 ERA in such contests. It'll be the righty's 12th career outing back in his home state and his first since May 2019.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly completed five innings for the first time in his past three starts and exited Sunday's start in Miami without allowing a home run. The long ball has consistently hurt the veteran lefty, who is looking to win consecutive starts for the second time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kim will hope his second go on Sunday Night Baseball will be smoother than the first, when he was chased after allowing four runs (one earned) in 3 1/3 innings on May 16. His last time out on Tuesday, he tossed a quality start despite allowing a career-high five walks.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom will continue his push to make ERA history after an MRI of his right shoulder showed no structural damage and he went through his between-starts routine without issue.

Stroman has completed at least six innings in eight consecutive starts, a career high. Seven of those eight have been quality starts, resulting in a 2.50 ERA over that stretch, with 46 strikeouts and 12 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Morton carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning of Thursday's win over the Cardinals. The veteran right-hander's successful outing might have been a product of him relying primarily on his fastball and curveball, which he combined to use with 87 percent of his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Santillan didn't miss many bats during his three-inning start vs. the Padres on Friday. Of his 53 pitches, there were only three swings and misses, and several balls were hit with an exit velocity of over 105 mph. He was lifted for a pinch-hitter when the Reds had a chance to score, before eventually finishing with an 8-2 loss.

Gutierrez gave up five runs, but he got through some rallies to reach five innings during Saturday's 7-5 loss to the Padres. His fastball remains his bread and butter pitch that sets up the rest of his arsenal.
